notes: PICK6 #511 restart hook (built, not on the box yet): the basket unit now retries itself 20 seconds after a crash, up to 5 times in 10 minutes, and finishes the saved basket instead of entering again. A new boot unit resumes today's open basket if the box comes back between 15:27 and 16:00 ET so the 15:59 exits go out for the filled shares only; it never makes a fresh entry. Back after 16:00 with legs open, or the unit failing for good, sends one high phone line and no order.

PAPER > Webull fill parity: each published trade now carries the hatch verdict at the top - its band in cents, in band yes / no, outside the minute range, ORB breakout design - and the trade flag reads that band instead of the old flat 15 cents. A fill 22 cents off inside a 42 cent band clears; 64 cents off against a 42.6 cent band stays flagged and the note names the band. A trade that cannot be judged reads not judged, never flagged. Publish only, no order change.

PAPER > Webull: a BOOKS fold lists every book (463, 20, 25, 30, 35, 35 cons, 40, 50 and the provisional ones) with each leg - name, run, share of the book, instrument and size, a status chip and an OFF / SHADOW / PAPER switch, plus an all shadow button per book. PAPER is open only where the QQQ box runs that exact version (ORB #314, NOISE #382); other versions stop at SHADOW, PICK6 and the last-10-minutes trade stay at SHADOW until their gate clears, gold is shadow only, and the futures-only legs are greyed with the reason. The box applies a change only while flat and only in PAPER mode; until it does the row reads pending, then applied HH:MM. The table comes from tools/book_legs_publish.py on the PC.

FEATURE BOARD: a verdict card is headed by the readable feature name instead of the raw key - Volatility level rather than atr_norm. The key is still on hover.

EXIT AUTOPSY: the hold curve says it is pre-lockbox only, and the one-line read is labelled PRE-LOCKBOX. Both are written off that stretch alone and sat under a table whose other column can say the opposite.
LEADERBOARD and the run report: the regime-drift pill now carries its own number on hover, so two rows that both read drift mild can be told apart.

EXPLORE: a row measured on fewer than thirty trades now carries a warning that says how many, because every ratio on this board - MAR, profit factor, Sortino, EV R, ROC at $30k - is measured over that row own trades, and a three-trade row was sitting at the top of all of them above an 833-trade row. The row is still drawn and still ranked, as a short window is.

EXPLORE: a month that holds none of the strategy you picked now names the MONTH as the reason instead of the strategy. It used to say no run of that strategy has records to read, which was untrue, and then tell you to untick a chip the month had already taken off the rail.
EXPLORE: a strategy you have picked keeps its chip on the rail even when the month holds none of its runs, so you can always untick it.

The RUNBOARD family chips follow the show-archived switch the board itself follows, so a family of archived runs gets a chip when archived runs are on. FEATURE BOARD no longer prints retired family names. The matrix column, the verdict cards and the exit autopsy read DIP and ENGU-Q where they used to read NQDIP and ENGUQ - in the headings, in the family pills and inside the written reasons. The two offline reports that write those files are fixed as well, so a regenerate keeps the right names.

RUNBOARD FIXES FROM THE w129 AUDIT (ORB), FOUR OF THEM. The ROC @ $30K DD hover no longer says MAR x 30 flat: the number is MAR x 30,000 over the ACCT chip account, so it equals MAR x 30 only at $100k and moves with the chip - the number is unchanged (deliberate), the words now say so. + ADD now stops the 11th tick instead of letting you tick any number and silently dropping the extras. EXPLORE: the run chip that clears your pick is called KEEP ONE, because it always leaves one run ticked - an empty pick draws nothing.

PICK RUNS empty state reads NO RUNS PICKED YET.

THE SCATTER MOVES (your 11-13: the dots are bunched, you want to zoom in and move around). SCROLL to zoom where the pointer is, DRAG to move, SHIFT-DRAG to box-zoom a region, DOUBLE-CLICK to zoom in and double-click again - or FIT ALL - to put every dot back. On a phone, pinch to zoom and drag with one finger. The axes rescale with the view, the break-even and zero lines stay, and every dot keeps its hover, its click that opens the run and its right-click that hides it. A zoomed view DROPS the rows outside it rather than pinning them to the edge, and says how many it left out. No new library: the chart already redraws from its own rows in milliseconds.

EXPLORE CONTROLS, FIVE CHANGES (your 11-13 screenshots). MONTH chips are MULTI-SELECT: click SEP and NOV and the board reads both, click one again to turn it off, ALL TIME clears back to everything. A non-contiguous pick reads the span and then filters to the months you ticked, so OCTOBER never sneaks in. AXIS (ABSOLUTE / CHAMPION) is GONE - the board reads each row own figures, which is what ABSOLUTE always was. The TABLES button is gone and the tables are ALWAYS ON. DOTS / SHAPES and WHICH DRAWING moved off the board bar ONTO the chart tile, because they only change the chart. The axis pickers show EVERY measure - the MORE / FEWER fold is gone, the four numbers still lead. Labels sit on ONE LINE and the rows are tighter. And a phone fix found on the way: the six sub-tabs were wider than a 390px screen and pushed the whole page sideways - they wrap now.

THE WORD COMPARE IS OFF THE SCREEN (your GO, 11-13). The rail tab is EXPLORE, the top strip is LEADERBOARD and EXPLORE only, and a view you open - OVERLAY, RUNBOARD, PICK RUNS, FEATURES, BOOKS - lights EXPLORE, because that is what those views are now.

THE BUTTON ON A LEADERBOARD RUN IS + PICK, and a picked one reads PICKED. The list it feeds is the same one as before (same saved pick, same cap of eight), so nothing you had picked is lost - it is called what it does now. The empty card says the same thing in the same words.
AND THE FULLSCREEN EQUITY WINDOW IS EQUITY OVERLAY, which is what it is - the run report opens the same window, and it should not be named after a screen that no longer exists.

WHAT IS NOT RENAMED, deliberately: COMPARE ON and COMPARE FOR on the EXPLORE board. Those are that board’s own controls - what to compare ON (ratios as is, or per year) and what to compare FOR (the axis pair) - and they are not the retired screen. Renaming them would cost you two controls you know to save a word that is doing honest work.

RETIRING COMPARE, FIRST PASS (your GO, 11-13). EXPLORE is the FIRST of the view buttons now rather than a screen off to one side: EXPLORE, OVERLAY, RUNBOARD, PICK RUNS, FEATURES, BOOKS all sit on one second-level bar, and EXPLORE draws that bar too - it used to draw none, which is most of why it read as somewhere else.

WHY THIS SHAPE. All six views already render from the same code and read the same run pool; they only looked like two places. Rebuilding five screens inside EXPLORE would have copied working code into a second place and left two of everything to keep in step. What is being retired is the COMPARE SCREEN and its name - the views are kept and re-filed under EXPLORE.

AND THE STAGE IS ONE SETTING ACROSS THE RESULTS SCREENS. The LEADERBOARD and the hosted boards read a SINGLE stage; EXPLORE ticks a SET, because it compares several stretches of one row side by side. Tick exactly one stretch on EXPLORE and every other screen follows it; pick IS, WF or LB on the others and EXPLORE ticks that one. Tick two or three and the single-stage screens keep what they had - naming one of your ticks ‘the’ stage would be a figure nobody chose. FULL stays out of it: EXPLORE has no such tick, so it never stands in for one.

THE SUB-TABS ARE A SECOND LEVEL OF THE SAME TAB BAR NOW (your 11-13 note). OVERLAY, RUNBOARD, PICK RUNS, FEATURES and BOOKS were a separate pill group floating under LEADERBOARD / COMPARE / EXPLORE, which said they were a different kind of control rather than a deeper level of the same one. They are one bar now: the second row is attached to the first, spans the same width, and the open sub-tab is joined to the page below it by its own underline sitting on the bar’s bottom edge - no pill bubble.
THE STAGE PICKER KEEPS ITS SEGMENTED SHAPE, one size smaller and aligned to the same bar rather than floating on a line of its own - it belongs to that second level, so that is where it sits.

IT IS BUILT GENERIC, not named for any one screen, and every place these sub-tabs appear draws the same bar from the same builder. That matters because the plan is to retire COMPARE and keep EXPLORE: a style written around COMPARE would have had to be redone, and the four places that drew this strip by hand would have drifted apart again.

THE MONTH CHIPS NOW CHANGE THE BOARD (your 11-13 note: toggling a month does not change anything). Measured in your browser first: NOV, OCT, SEP and ALL TIME each gave the same 112 rows and the same 40 run chips - the chip moved the status line and nothing else.

WHY IT DID NOTHING. The run chips were taken from the whole loaded pool with no date test at all, and ALL CANDIDATES reads its rows out of whichever runs are ticked - so the month could not reach the chips, and through them it could not reach the rows or the scatter. On top of that the month’s own run read was switched on only for EXPLORE, so anywhere else a month could only ever narrow to runs that happened to be inside the newest 75 already loaded.

WHAT A MONTH MEANS FOR A CONFIGURATION, because it has no date of its own: it is a row of the search its run ran, so its date is the date of that RUN. That is the test now - the chips offer the runs of the month, the candidate rows follow them, and a starred or watch-list run is forced past the newest-80 cut but NOT past the month, so OCTOBER cannot quietly include an August run. A run carrying no timestamp is held back rather than shown as if it were inside the window, and the count is named.

AND THE CAP LINE SAYS WHICH READ CAPPED. It used to say ‘this month is NOT whole’ whichever read hit its limit - alarming about nothing on ALL CANDIDATES, where the rows come from run documents and the 1,500 that capped are CHAT records this source never draws. It now names the read that capped and says plainly when it cannot touch the rows on screen. An empty month says so in its own words instead of looking like a broken board.

PAST RUNS, ONE FILTER BAR INSTEAD OF A SCATTERED ROW (your 11-13 note). CHAMPIONS, the seven family chips and GROUP were sharing the title’s own line, spread apart by whatever space was left over - CHAMPIONS adrift left of centre, the families floating in the middle with big gaps, GROUP pinned far right. Nothing was wrong with any of them; they had no line of their own. They get one now, directly under the PAST RUNS title, left-aligned, every control the same height and padding, wrapping onto a second line on a narrow screen instead of spreading.

AND THE BAR LEADS WITH A SEARCH BOX THAT CAN REACH A RUN THIS PAGE NEVER LOADED. The list holds the most recent runs - 79 today - so typing 283 could only ever have found nothing. Type a run number now and if it is not among the loaded ones the page FETCHES that run document and the row appears with the rest. Type anything else and it matches what you can see on a row: strategy, family, market, timeframe, mode.

IT SAYS WHICH ANSWER YOU GOT, because an empty list is not one. Looking up #283; found it but a filter above is hiding it; or no run #283 on this account. The search narrows ALONGSIDE the chips rather than overriding them - a fetched run goes through exactly the same chip test as every other row, from one shared test rather than a second copy of the conditions. Esc or the ✕ clears it, SHOW EVERYTHING clears it with the rest, and every filter already there behaves as before.

COMPARE, THE RUN CHIPS ARE IN ONE ORDER NOW (your 11-09 note: they read ’#425 #424 #432 #433 #434 #452 #451 #484 #483 #507’). That was not random - it was three orders in one row: watched runs first in watch-list order, then the rest by number, then FAIL, then VOID. Nothing on screen said so, which reads exactly like no order at all. One numeric order now, HIGHEST RUN NUMBER FIRST, and the rail says ’RUNS · NEWEST FIRST’ so it never has to be guessed. Nothing is lost: a watched run wears a star, and FAIL and VOID already carry their own word and their grey.

AND THE BOARD NOW SAYS WHICH ROW IS TRADING PAPER MONEY - but it does not stamp ’#424.1’ on every row, because that would answer your question with the wrong number. The Webull ’.N’ counts rows of the run’s whole saved search grid sorted by in-sample net (set 1 of 150 for DIP #424, set 22 of 382 for ORB #314). COMPARE lists a different and much shorter population - the validate candidates - and the ’R2’ beside each is its WALK-FORWARD RANK among them. Those two numbers coincide only by accident. What is true is printed: where a paper leg is matched to its run’s CHAMPION, and COMPARE crowns that same champion, the crowned row now carries the WEBULL TEXT ITSELF - ’#424.1 raw’ - and a green PAPER mark, so the two boards match by eye, character for character. And where the paper leg is a grid cell instead, the crowned row says PAPER SET NOT ON THIS BOARD and the hover names the set (22 of a 382-row grid) - ’none of these’ is an answer, a wrong number is not. Every candidate hover now also says that its id is a walk-forward rank and not the set number the paper boards print.

COMPARE TABLES column filters now work on the AUTO-VALIDATED configuration rows: the FAMILY value list shows every value with its count (DIP RAW, DIP GATE ...) instead of 0 values, so you can tick just RAW.
Every column filter - values, min / max, top N, blanks - now narrows those configuration rows too, not only the study rows.
SORT LARGEST FIRST / SMALLEST FIRST sits in the same funnel menu on every sortable number column.

COMPARE: THE TWO AXIS ROWS WERE 28 BUTTONS (your ’too many buttons’). VERTICAL AXIS and HORIZONTAL AXIS were fourteen each - more than every other control above the first dot put together, which is why they go first. Each row now shows the FOUR NUMBERS this project ranks on - ROC @ $30K DD, DD5, DD % from peak, SORTINO - with the other eleven behind one MORE button.

MEASURED, NOT CLAIMED: 48 controls on screen before, 31 as the board now opens, counted by the chart gate on the same board and printed on every run from here on so the figure cannot drift quietly. The scope’s target is under 15 and the month pills, the strategy rail and the two tables are still to come.

NOTHING IS REMOVED AND NO SAVED VIEW BREAKS. The folded buttons are still in the page, only hidden - a board set to EV R or MAR opens on it exactly as before, and the fold OPENS BY ITSELF when the measure you have ticked is one of the eleven, so you never see a row whose own setting is off screen.

AND DD5 IS AN AXIS AT LAST, which is the real gap behind all this: the four numbers are the yardstick, but DD5 has been a column and a sort key for months with no axis button, so the board could not actually plot what it ranks on. It is on both axes now, reading the same figure the DD5 column prints through the same reader, so a dot and its row can never disagree. Lower is better.

THE BOARD ALSO OPENS ON THE YARDSTICK PAIR: a new FOUR NUMBERS preset, first on the row - ROC @ $30K DD across against SORTINO up the side - and it is the default. It used to open on EV R up, a fair pair but not the one every ranking here is made on. EDGE, RISK, QUALITY and LEVERAGE LINE all stay.

A RUNNING VALIDATE SAYS WHERE IT IS: the queue card and the top-bar job chip now show the stage it is in (search, walk-forward, selection, lockbox, whole run, surrogate, ML gate, reports), which of the 8 it is, how long it has been in that stage and how long the run has been going. Read from the engine own stage markers; no percentage is invented. Shows after the next runner restart.

AND THE SHADOW ROWS WERE STILL LOSING CHARACTERS. The gate that proves your label is never cut - measured the way you see it, the name’s own width against the box it has, at every width the board is drawn at - found one row the previous ship had missed: the shadow fold’s rows do not carry the wrap flag the leg rows do, so ’ENGU-Q #335 ...’ was still being cut by the base ellipsis one fold away from the rows I had fixed. The no-cut rule now covers the whole WEBULL PAPER list.

THAT CHECK IS NEW AND IT IS THE POINT: a cut label still looks like a tidy one-line row of the right height, which is exactly why ’DIP #42’ got past every existing check on this board. Putting the old three-figure value column back now fails the gate out loud, which I tested before trusting it.

WEBULL PAPER ROW, YOUR FINAL SPEC - and I had been fixing the wrong side of it. Your phone picture showed ’DIP #42’ with the unrealized line running over the name, which told me the name was not what was too wide. The value column was: it carried THREE money strings stacked - closed P&L, ’unrealized +$196.53 . 3 lots . 300 sh’, and ’equity +$506.53’ - and the widest of those sets the column, leaving the name about 120px at 390px wide. No font size fixes that.

SO THE RIGHT-HAND SIDE IS NOW ONE NUMBER: net equity, realized and unrealized together. That is what the 10-18 note always intended (’a leg that holds overnight reads as one figure’); the code had drifted into showing closed P&L large with equity small underneath.
Under it, small, the open position’s P&L alone - no lots and no share count. Those were the longest strings on the row and they are not headline facts.

AND THE LABEL IS NEVER CUT, which is your priority 1. With the column down to one figure it fits on one line at 390px, and it is allowed to wrap rather than lose a character if it ever does not. No ellipsis and no silent clip: what those discarded was the run number, the parameter set and the model word - the characters that say which run is trading your money.

NOTHING IS HIDDEN, it moved one tap away. The row’s expander now carries its own labelled facts: realized in the range, unrealized now, the open position’s lots and shares, and the parameter set - including the sentence that a leg’s traded values match no row of its run’s saved grid, which must never go quiet wherever it is said.

The board gate moved with the spec rather than being loosened: the headline is checked as realized + open, the small line as the open part alone, a third money line fails outright, and the account reconciliation now adds up the REALIZED figures out of the expanders - so it also proves every row really does carry its split.

COMPARE, THE P&L CHART UNDER THE SCATTER (owner 11-08): it now has the same drag handle as the scatter, so you can make it taller or shorter (remembered; double-click resets), and it runs on dates with the walk-forward stretch shaded blue and the lockbox purple, the same colours as the Auto-Validate report.

WEBULL PAPER, ONE LINE WITH THE WHOLE NAME ON IT (your 11-08 14:50 note: "just make it one line"). The row said the parameter set twice - ’DIP #424.1 raw’, and then a tag repeating ’. set 1’ - and that repetition is what pushed it onto a second line. The set is said once now, by the name.

The tag is KEPT where it says something the name cannot: that a leg’s traded values match no row of its run’s saved grid, and that a set is the strategy file’s defaults rather than a searched cell. Those two sentences are the point of the tag; the repeated digit was not.

AND THE LINE IS MADE TO FIT RATHER THAN CUT. No ellipsis is coming back - what it used to discard was the run number, the set and the model word, the only characters on the row that say which run is trading. The name is a point smaller on these rows with slightly tighter pills, and the board gate is back to demanding one line (76 px) instead of the 120 it was raised to yesterday.

COMPARE TABLES NO LONGER CUT IN SILENCE (your 11-08 screenshot: the list "gets truncated arbitrarily vertically", ending at row 11 of 24). No row was ever dropped - the box has always scrolled - but a cut edge and the end of a list look identical, so eleven rows read as all there was.

Under a table that overflows, one line now says how many rows there are and how many sit below the edge, and it follows you down until it reads ’at the end of the table’. A table whose rows all fit says nothing at all, so the line appearing IS the signal that there is more.

And the cut comes later on a tall screen: the 430 / 520 / 560 px caps were flat numbers from a narrower board, and are now the floor, with a tall window getting about 62% of its height. Nothing gets shorter than it was.
The scatter and the P&L chart in that same screenshot are not mine - they are with TRADING-LOG and TBIS.

THE SOURCE CHIPS SAY WHAT THEY HOLD (your 11-08 note). The board that draws 504 rows - the crown, the raw top-10 and the gate / tilt / keel / hybrid variants of every ticked run - is ALL CANDIDATES. It was ML CONFIGS, which was wrong in both directions: most of what it draws is not an ML configuration, and a run with no ML rows at all still has candidates on it. One run contributes MANY rows here, and the chip now says so.

AND ONE ROW PER RUN IS BACK, as VALIDATED RUNS. For about ten minutes the two boards were merged into a single chip still called AUTO-VALIDATED, which left that name promising validated RUNS while drawing their CANDIDATES - the same mix-up pointing the other way - and took the per-run board off the page completely: it could not be reached from the rail, from a saved view or from a bookmark, because every request for it was being rewritten to the candidates board one line after it was read.

THAT ALSO HAD THE CHART GATE RED. Eleven cases failed on the merged build, w50_source among them, all of them cases that read a run row - which is what a run board being unreachable looks like from the outside. 172 of 172 pass again.

WHY IT IS NOT CALLED CROWNS, which is what was asked for: that chip holds EVERY validated run, crowned or not. A crown has been a MARK a row carries wherever it appears since 10-20, never a filter, precisely so that looking at the champions stops hiding the rest of the board. Labelling the chip CROWNS would promise a shortlist and hand over all of them - so it is named for what it is, one row per validated run.

COMPARE SOURCE: AUTO-VALIDATED and ML CONFIGS are one chip now - AUTO-VALIDATED shows every config of the runs you tick (crown, raw top-10 and the gate, tilt, keel and hybrid variants, coloured by family). The ML CONFIGS chip is gone.

1E MATRIX ALL table: columns packed into one block instead of spreading across the full width (COMPARE ON too), and every ML row now carries a config id like G12, T07, K01 or H03 in the CONFIG column and the scatter hover, so any row can be referenced.

1E MATRIX: new TR/Y column (trades per year over the ticked SAMPLE) right after TRADES in the ALL table, and a TR/Y row under TRADES on RAW. ALL table headings now sit on one line with short names - hover a heading for the full name.

A LANE OR LAB ROW OPENS NOW (your 11-07 note: rows with no run number, clicking does nothing). A run row opens its report; one of these rows was the end of the road, which is the same dead end as a row that is hidden. Click one and a DETAILS card opens underneath it. Click it again and it shuts.

WHAT THE CARD SAYS: what ran, the market and timeframe, which stretch it covers in the record own word and in plain English, the window and its length, which lane measured it and on which machine, and when. Then the four numbers EXACTLY as the record stores them - ROC at a $30k drawdown, DD5 in dollars, DD % from the high, Sortino - plus trades, whether the lead is one episode, the net and its start, and gross and cost per point. Nothing on the card is re-derived by the page.

AND THE TWO ROC COLUMNS ARE NAMED SIDE BY SIDE (your 11-07 note: the page shows 113 to 136% while the records store 70 to 78). Both figures are right and they are different measures: ROC % / YR is that row money per year over the account on the ACCT chip, ROC @ $30K DD is the same trades resized so the worst drawdown is $30,000. The card prints both and says so in a sentence. I did not make them equal - that would have falsified a column; the board still ranks on the $30k one.

IT PROMISES NO PATH IT DOES NOT HAVE. The ask was for the prereg or results path from the record, and there is no such field on any of the 3,440 lines. So the card gives the provenance a record really carries - the LEDGER ROW it was written against and the COMMIT of the code that produced it - and says in a line that there is no path and no report to open. An invented path would be worse than none.
Fourteen new checks in the chart gate cover it, including that the row is clickable at all, that the card stays shut until asked for, and that neither ROC figure is bent to match the other.

THE SCATTER OPENS ON THE MIDDLE OF ITS SCALE AGAIN (your 11-07 note: a wall of dots at DD % 200 to 1,000 squashing everything else). This moved twice in one day and the reason is worth having in writing: the trim went in on 11-06 for ONE six-week ORB record, came out this morning because that record was deleted and it was then guarding nothing, and is back now because your whole-board view carries 362 records reading DD % from peak between 100% and 690%.

THOSE 362 ROWS ARE NOT CORRUPT, so nothing has been written over them. DD % from peak divides the fall by the running peak of the account - start plus profit - and a strategy that loses more than the account began with falls by a multiple of it. One of them stores minus $690,334 on a $100,000 start, which is a DD % of 690 and perfectly honest. They are all losers, and the lane that writes them already knows this: it derives each row ceiling from that row own worst drawdown in dollars precisely so readings like these are not refused.

SO WHAT SHIPPED IS THE TRIM, NOT A 0 TO 100 CAP. It reads every lane record this account holds, with no date range, so CHAT SWEEPS is not empty before you pick a month - and the line under the chart reports that read: how many records, when they last synced, whether a read failed, whether it hit its 1,500-row cap (it drops the OLDEST rows when it does), and what the colours and shapes on those dots mean. Until this release that whole line was hidden on ALL TIME, so a failed read looked exactly like having no records.

THE 1E CONFIGS OFFER WORKS AGAIN. When a run has no figure on the axes you picked, the line under the chart offers to show the configurations inside it instead - and for one release that button changed nothing at all, because it still wrote the old SHOW setting that nothing reads any more. The same bug had stopped the LEVERAGE LINE preset from reaching the view its own lines live on. Both move the chip now.

YOUR OLD VIEW IS TRANSLATED ONCE, NOT KEPT ALIVE BESIDE THE NEW ONE. A board left on the old LEVEL maps to the chip that means the same thing - SWEEPS to CHAT SWEEPS, AUTO VAL and CROWN to the runs, SHOW on CONFIGS to ML CONFIGS, and ALL stays ALL - so the lit chip and the board always agree. A first cut of this release kept both meanings running at once, and it showed: CHAT SWEEPS could sit lit over a board with none of your chat records on it, clicking the chip that was already lit changed what was drawn, and CROWN went on hiding the rest of each family.

ONE MONTH CONTROL, NOT TWO (your ask: if i click october it shows october, and all time shows all). MONTH ONLY is gone. A month chip now shows that month - the chart and the tables together - and ALL TIME shows everything the page holds. ALL TIME is the default, so nothing disappears until you pick a month, and the rows a month leaves off are still counted and named under the chart.

THE TEXT UNDER THE CHART IS TWO LINES (your ask: the scatter plot below the table is a novel. condense for only relevant info). Line one is what is drawn - how many rows of how many, which stretch they are read on, and what the month chip read. Line two is what is NOT drawn and the biggest reason, with its switch where there is one. Everything else - what the colours and shapes mean, the rest of the reasons, the read warnings, the configuration lists - is behind one DETAILS tap, and it remembers whether you left it open. Nothing was deleted, only folded.

THE MONTH LINE NOW SAYS WHEN THE LANE RECORDS LAST REACHED THE BOARD, and says it plainly when that is more than three hours ago: a run recorded since then is not here yet. Nothing uploads a lane's line by itself - a month can be read whole, drawn whole, and still be behind what the lanes have written, which is the one way this board could go quietly stale. It costs no extra read: every uploaded record already carries the pass that sent it.

DD5 IS BACK ON THE LANE RECORDS. One of the four numbers was being dashed on every record in the table - with the wrong reason, that the row saves no equity curve - while the dot two inches away printed the figure. The lane measured it off its own daily series and the page now reads it, says whose it is, and makes that lane own ONE EPISODE call. Ordering the table by DD5 had been sinking every lane record below every run.

ONE AXIS, ONE MEANING. A run row on ROC @ $30K DD is divided by the ACCT chip; a record carried its figure flat, which is the reading at a $100,000 account. On any other account setting a record and a run with the SAME return over drawdown sat at different heights. Records are now put on the account the axis is drawn on.

NOT TESTED IS NOT NO. A lab writes NOT TESTABLE for the one-episode question, and that read exactly like a run whose lane tested it and found no single episode. The hover and the DD5 note now say which of the three it is.

A record is a run a lane measured and nobody has judged, so its hover no longer says reference or superseded. The LANE AND LAB RUNS table used to label itself with the family of its first row, right for every other table here and wrong for this one: it holds twenty families and called itself BOOK. Hiding a record now follows the record, not its position in the month - hiding October record 4 used to hide September record 4 after a chip click. And on a level that builds no record rows at all, the line under the chart says the records were read and not drawn instead of counting rows that are not there.

The uploader refuses a flat 0 percent against whichever dollar drawdown a record carries, not only against DD5 - 273 of the lanes real lines carry one dollar figure and not the other, and a 0 on one of those drew no fall from the high for a run that fell.

EVERY CHAT'S RUNS ARE ON THE SCATTER NOW (your ask 10-18, the second half). A Stage A sweep in a worktree, a Qwen Lab dry run and a forward line on the box were never run documents, so they could not be drawn. Each lane writes one line per finished run (tools/run_record.py), tools/run_records_sync.py uploads it once, and the MONTH chips read them beside the runner's own runs. 886 of the seven lanes' 1,199 recorded lines went up today: 753 in October, 133 in September. COLOUR says where it ran - the PC runner, a lane worktree, the Qwen Lab, the Oracle box - and SHAPE says which stretch: square in-sample, diamond pre-walk-forward, triangle walk-forward, circle lockbox, cross forward, and a HOLLOW square or diamond for the two wider stretches (the whole run as one, everything before the lockbox). A hollow mark fills no stretch column, so a whole-run total is never added into a walk-forward figure.

THEIR FIGURES ARE READ, NOT RE-DERIVED. A record carries the four numbers its own lane measured through the one house definition (augur_engine.drawdowns.four_numbers): ROC at a $30,000 drawdown, DD5 in dollars, DD % from the high, and Sortino on DAILY returns with zero days counted. The page used to need the money, the drawdown and the years to work a ROC out for itself - measured against the real records, 886 of 1,199 lines carry a ROC and only 18 carry those three inputs, so it reads the lane's figure and says so in the hover.

A ROW WITH A GAP IS SHOWN, NOT HIDDEN. 399 of October's 753 records recorded a DD % from peak, so on the default axes about half of them can be placed and the rest are counted and named under the chart, exactly as a run with no saved curve already is. The hover on every record names the lane, the host, the stretch, its DD5 and one-episode flag, its ledger row and the code it ran.

The uploader refuses what would draw a lie rather than what is merely missing: a percent in the DD5 dollars field, dollars in the percent field, a provisional run id from a Firestore outage, a non-boolean one-episode flag, a DD5 deeper than the worst drawdown. A caption it cannot use costs itself and not the run - 50 lines put a 64-character content hash where the commit sha goes, and they upload without it rather than being dropped. 313 lines are still refused and every one is named with its line number: 273 recorded no figure any axis can place (most of them carry their money in the note text) and 40 never named a stretch. It is dry by default and idempotent by the content of each line.

THE MONTH SELECTOR IS WHERE YOU CAN SEE IT (your ask 10-18, part two). It went in behind FILTERS, which on EXPLORE is a second panel you have to open - a headless screenshot of the real page showed no chip anywhere on screen. It now sits on the always-visible control row beside LEVEL, SHOW and PROFIT STAGE: MONTH - OCT SEP AUG JUL JUN MAY - 30 DAYS - ALL TIME, with MONTH ONLY OFF/ON next to it.

MONTH ONLY REALLY NARROWS NOW. Measured on the live build: October with MONTH ONLY on drew 72 run dots, runs #416 to #479 among them - September runs - under a line that correctly said eleven. Run rows are put on the board by a different path from the research rows (the level gate refuses a registry row there), so the narrowing never reached them. It does now, and the line under the chart counts what it is holding back. Re-measured after the fix: October shows ten dots of the eleven runs in the month, and the eleventh is named - it carries a FAIL verdict, and PLOT FAILURES is off by default on that screen.

A RUN THAT ARRIVED WITH THE MONTH NOW HAS A DATE RAN. The lookup that answers when a run ran read only the newest-75 list, so a run fetched by the month chip showed a dash in the DATE RAN column and had no date for any range or month test to read. It now reads the same shared pool every other part of the board reads.

THE LINE UNDER THE CHART SAYS WHICH STRETCH THE FIGURES ARE. The stage tick starts on all three, so every ROC on screen is the whole-run reading with the tuning years in it - correct, and silent about it until now. It says so, and says that WALK-FORWARD alone is the house yardstick.

A LANE RECORD IS NO LONGER DROPPED FROM EVERY PER-YEAR AXIS. The rule that protects a registry write-up - one window for the whole row but money for only part of it, so its years and its money do not match - was refusing a lane record too, and a record IS one stretch that states that stretch own years. The tools that write those records, and the probe case for them, are in the next ship.

A MONTH SELECTOR ON COMPARE, EXPLORE (your ask 10-18: everything run in the past month visible on the scatter, wherever it ran). Chips for the last six calendar months, the rolling 30 days, and ALL TIME. Picking a month READS that month in one query and ADDS its rows to the board - it hides nothing, because no caps and no auto-hide is the rule on this screen. MONTH ONLY, beside it, narrows to the month on your click, and the line under the chart then counts what it is holding back.

WHY YOUR MONTH WAS NOT THERE. The page only ever holds the newest 75 run documents (LOAD MORE adds 75 at a time), so a month that is not among the newest 75 runs was never in the browser to plot. Measured on 10-18 against the real collection: September 2026 holds 173 runs, August 125, and 440 runs exist in all. A month now arrives in one projected query, with the same fields the run list already reads, and the runs join the shared pool - so they are on EXPLORE, RUNBOARD and PICK RUNS together, the same way a starred run outside the window already is.

AND THE RUNS THAT WERE NEVER RUN DOCUMENTS AT ALL: a Stage A sweep in a lane worktree, a Qwen Lab dry run, a forward line on the Oracle box. Those are not in Past Runs and never were. Each lane now writes one line per finished run (tools/run_record.py), it is uploaded once (tools/run_records_sync.py), and the month read picks them up. On the chart the COLOUR says where it ran - the PC runner, a lane worktree, the Qwen Lab, the box - and the SHAPE says which stretch: square in-sample, diamond pre-walk-forward, triangle walk-forward, circle lockbox, cross forward.

THE FOUR NUMBERS ON THOSE ROWS ARE THE LANE OWN MEASUREMENTS, not something this page derived: ROC at a $30,000 drawdown, DD5 in dollars, DD % from the high, and Sortino on DAILY returns with zero days counted, all from augur_engine.drawdowns.four_numbers, the one definition. DD % from peak is READ off the record rather than worked out here, because a lane record saves no equity curve and the standing rule holds: a stored dollar drawdown is never divided into a percent. A record that carries no percent says so in its hover instead of showing a made-up one.

THE MONTH LINE TELLS THE TRUTH ABOUT WHAT IT READ: how many run documents and how many lane records, a read still in flight, a read that failed and its reason, a read that hit its cap (so the month is NOT whole), and the one legacy run - #156, which saved an integer timestamp where every other run saved a string - that a month range can never match and which therefore reaches the board only through the ordinary newest-75 list. 439 of the 440 runs are unaffected, measured.

Probe: a new cmp2 case (w47_month) injects three lane records - one from a lane worktree, one from the Qwen Lab, one from the box - and checks they reach the chart on ROC at $30k against DD % from peak, that the page places them in the order of the figures each lane recorded, that the colours and shapes are the right ones, and that the month line says the counts, the hold-back and a failed read. It fails on the build before this one.

ROLL CHECK (owner ask 10-08: the roll defect must not recur; MANAGER #31). Since ORB’s roll guard, every run the PC runner saves carries a roll stamp: the price series it ran on, where its roll dates come from, the contract switches in its window, the trades held across one and their money, any pure roll step booked, and the money made on switch sessions. A run whose stamp says its prices may not follow the true contract roll table - a stale adjusted price file, a wrong label, a market with no roll table, a level-reading file on an adjusted price file, the guard’s refusals waived, or a roll step counted as profit or loss - now carries a ROLL CHECK tag wherever VOID and ROLL tags show. A report, not a void: it changes no ranking.

Run report: a ROLLS chip in the ROBUSTNESS rail for every run with a stamp (true roll table, no contract rolls, true roll table · raw signals, or check) opens the whole stamp in plain words, including the raw-versus-adjusted check (the same file re-run on raw prices, trade by trade). Runs saved before the guard carry no stamp and show no chip; the 22 old roll-detector runs keep their ROLL tag.

DD % NOW READS LIKE A BROKER (owner ask 10-08). It used to be the worst drawdown in dollars divided by the fixed starting account, which is a share of the opening balance and not a drawdown at all: run #424 worst drop of 116,900 dollars printed as about 117 per cent on a run whose profit and loss never once went below zero. No open account can fall 117 per cent. It is now the fall from the highest the account has been, which is what a broker shows you - a 100,000 dollar drop after the account reached a million reads 10 per cent.

One definition, written once and checked. The engine owns it and the page carries the same rule so a hover does not wait on a round trip, exactly as DD5 already works. A new check runs the page copy in a real browser and compares it against the engine on six curves, and it deliberately plants two wrong formulas - the old share-of-the-start one, and the plausible one that measures each dip against its own high instead of the account high - and fails on both.

What it is NOT used for: nothing about ranking changed. Crowns, the frontier and the house yardstick still read dollars of drawdown and ROC per year at a 30,000 dollar drawdown, with DD5 beside them. The reason is on the hover: contract size is fixed, so the same dollar fall is a smaller percentage as the account grows - the percentage tells you how a drop FELT against the account at the time, the dollars tell you how big it was.

A run saved before today has no such figure stored and the page cannot work one out backwards - the worst fall in percentage is not always the same episode as the worst fall in dollars once the account has grown, so no division of a stored dollar figure recovers it. Those cells are left blank rather than filled with the old number; their dollar drawdown is unchanged and says everything it always said.

RUN REPORT, CONFIG FUNNEL: EQUAL RISK (owner ask 10-07). A new toggle beside ONE CURVE and DOORS. Switched on, every family line - the raw config, the gate, the size tilt, KEEL, the hybrids - is resized so that all of them took the SAME worst drawdown, and then compared on the money they made at that one level of risk. The point is run 424: KEEL made more dollars than the crowned raw config but against a far deeper drawdown, so it was winning by trading bigger rather than by being better. At equal risk the ranking can turn over, and this is the view that shows it.

The size for each line is worked out ONLY from the tuning stretch, before the first walk-forward test begins, and then applied unchanged to the walk-forward and the lockbox. So the size is never chosen with knowledge of the held-out years. Each line is labelled with its size - x1.39 - beside its ending dollars. Default budget is a 30,000 dollar worst drawdown, the house yardstick; MATCH ML instead reads every line at whatever drawdown the crowned machine-learning line actually ran.

What the size is measured from, stated because it changes what the numbers mean: a saved run holds no day-by-day equity for these lines, so the drawdown used is the one the engine computed trade by trade over the tuning stretch, not a daily one. That is the deeper and more cautious of the two, so the sizes here are if anything on the small side and the equal-risk dollars understated rather than flattered. A line whose tuning drawdown was not saved is left at its own size and says so rather than pretending it was already at the budget. A size the budget would push past 25 times is capped, with an exclamation mark, because that means the tuning stretch was too quiet to size from at all.

Switched off, the chart is exactly as it was. The report render check now covers both states, and it fails if the toggle is on but nothing was actually resized - which is how it behaved on the first run, before the labels existed.

Hover any family line for what its size rests on: the tuning drawdown the size was worked out from, what that size is worth over the held-out years, and - marked HINDSIGHT, because it is not used - the size the whole curve would have allowed if you had known it in advance. On the probe run that second figure is about six and a half times the first, which is the gap the no-hindsight rule exists to close.

DD5 is in the hover too, beside the worst drawdown, read off the line as drawn - so it is the DD5 this line would have run AT the budget, which is the whole point of the toggle. It carries a tilde like every other DD5 on the site, and it also carries the number of saved points it was read from: this chart compares a raw line against a machine-learning line, and those curves are saved at different densities - about 160 points against 300 - so two DD5 figures here are not equally resolved and the count says which is the coarser. A line whose worst dip is more than 1.3 times its DD5 says 1 EPISODE, the same words RUNBOARD uses.

NINJATRADER NIGHT MODE (owner 10-07). After the close NinjaTrader now does its final checks and then stops by itself: from 16:15 New York on trading days it takes the day backup, finishes the 10-second data (retries up to 45 minutes and logs any gap it cannot fill), checks every fill was recorded, then closes NinjaTrader and keeps it closed until 05:45 Arizona on the next trading day (Friday to Monday, holidays skipped). Flat: the strategies stop and NinjaTrader closes cleanly. A paper trade open with its stop: NinjaTrader is force-closed with nothing switched off, so the stop stays at the broker but does not trail until the morning. A paper trade with no stop, or your real account holding a position or an order: NinjaTrader stays on that night and you get a push.

Two Desktop switches: NinjaTrader OFF tonight (the same checks, right now) and NinjaTrader ON now (ends night mode and starts NinjaTrader). The morning check, the 30-minute sweep, the order-flow alarm and the cloud watchdog treat the night as expected; a failed morning start still alerts. While NinjaTrader is closed the ENGU-Q NinjaTrader paper leg does not trade the evening and overnight session; the engine paper record still tracks it. It only adds the trades your journal is missing, sets each fee to the statement fee per contract times its size, and lists any trade the journal holds in another size or direction without changing it. A reversal fill (long 1, sell 2) now makes two trades instead of one, and a clearing fee is split across the symbols traded that day instead of charged to each one.

THE TWO WALK-FORWARD READINGS NOW HAVE DIFFERENT NAMES. The folds re-tuned on their own past and traded blind stay the WALK-FORWARD TEST (the pill now reads WF TEST). A run too old to have either saves pooled re-tuned folds in that column and now says so, instead of one heading meaning three things by run age. Where a run has both readings, its row carries a gap chip: the crowning score sits N per cent above the test, and in our own record a bigger gap went with a weaker sealed year. A run with only one candidate reads SAME READING.

A WALK-FORWARD TEST UNDER 30 TRADES NO LONGER RANKS AHEAD OF A REAL ONE. It still shows its figures with a THIN TEST mark, sinks below every run that cleared the floor, and can never take a best mark, a heat shade or a RUNBOARD column; a test that took no trades still sinks below that. On the lockbox stage every screen now says what the sealed year is: one look and a pass-or-fail check, not a ranking - a 12-month lockbox has roughly an 11 per cent chance of confirming a real edge, and a strategy with no edge passes its money-above-zero test about half the time.

In an expanded family the first run no longer wears a star it does not have; a lockbox that took no trades says so instead of 'no curve saved'; the RUNBOARD window row says RUN WINDOW and its hover names the stretch the figures use; the MAR hovers say net per year over the worst drawdown, which is what the board ranks on; the funnel info box no longer describes stripes, a wash and a door the chart does not draw; the books notes drop a renamed column and a file name; a book's name in chart keys and tables is its own, not a leg's run number; two EXPLORE hovers and the run-rows subtitle now match what the chart does; FEATURES tells apart loading, not built yet and a real error; and the study rows that still called #234 and #226 the standing champions now read as the paper control and a reference, leaving your crowns #257 and #335.

A book's in-sample years now start at the run window like every other figure, so its in-sample MAR and return per year line up with the rest of the board and in-sample plus lockbox add up to the whole run.

EVERY WEBULL PAPER TRADE NOW HAS A CHART BUTTON (owner: add that to the trades so i can look at the price action). It opens the same candle viewer the run blotter uses, centred on that trade, with QQQ 1-minute bars for ENGU-Q and 5-minute for ORB and NOISE. Worth knowing: this does NOT come from NinjaTrader. Its bridge has no bars feature at all and only listens to your own PC, and NinjaTrader here only ever records ES and NQ - it holds no QQQ. The bars come from the QQQ history the engine already keeps, and as with the futures paper tab the chart needs your PC awake to serve them.

ON THE WEBULL PAPER CALENDAR, COLOUR NOW MEANS MONEY AND HATCHING MEANS DATA (owner: having calendar show red is confusing as that would normally indicate a loss). A day with a flagged price feed used to be painted red whatever it earned, so 3 September read as a red loss when it actually made 5.78 dollars. Green and red are now always the day P and L, and anything that makes the numbers less trustworthy shows as diagonal hatching in that same colour with one amber dot. Three things hatch a day: the feed was flagged invalid, an exit could not be marked so its money came from the 1-minute tape, or a trade failed its parity check - so 17 and 18 September are now hatched too. The tooltip says which.

Dragging the 1E table tile shorter now scrolls the TABLE inside it again, with its headings pinned, instead of scrolling the whole card. Releasing the grow-to-fit floor had also thrown away the box own height cap.

DAYS WITH A MISSING EXIT PRICE NO LONGER READ AS $0. When the book could not mark an exit - which happened on 17 and 18 September, because the end of day sell fired two seconds after the closing bell and there was no live price - the trade carried no profit figure, and every total on the Webull paper trading tab quietly counted it as zero. Both days showed $0 with three real trades in them. The calendar, month total, leg rows, running curve and the trade list now fall back to the price recovered from the 1-minute tape, and a day tooltip says how many of its trades were priced that way. About $58 of profit was hidden on those two days.

THE 1E TABLE TILE CAN BE RESIZED AGAIN (owner: i cant resize the table). Making the tile grow to show every row put a floor under it as tall as the whole table, and the drag handle could not get beneath that floor, so the tile would not shrink. Now the grow only applies while the tile is on automatic height: drag the handle and your height wins - the table scrolls inside, as it did before - and double-click the handle to go back to automatic, where it fits every row again.

CLICKING ONE OF YOUR OLDER CROWNS NOW OPENS THAT RUN. A starred run older than the newest 75 - today #243 NOISE and #257 ORB - opened the book #366 report instead, and the star, archive and delete buttons on that page acted on the book. Those runs now open their own report, or say they are loading. The same older runs also reach PICK RUNS, EXPLORE and the RUNBOARD family chips and pins, which could not see them before; a screen that cannot resolve a saved pick now says the run is older than what is loaded instead of claiming it no longer exists, and one click no longer erases it from your saved picks.

IN-SAMPLE MONEY IS NOW THE MEASURED IN-SAMPLE. EXPLORE run rows, the RUNBOARD whole-run in-sample column and the PICK RUNS in-sample row worked it out as the whole run minus the walk-forward tests minus the lockbox, which mixes one fixed configuration with re-tuned ones: crown #335 read $155k there against $44k on its own report, and 30 of 44 validated runs were off by more than 0.10 of profit factor. All three now read the run's own measured in-sample stretch, or dash with the reason. A book run report also builds its in-sample, lockbox and whole-run columns from the book's own blocks - #366 read minus $2.1k in-sample and 622 trades against a real $1,395,904 and 9,707.

RANKING NO LONGER REWARDS THE WRONG RUNS. Archived runs are out of every leaderboard, champion and RUNBOARD ranking, as they already are on Past Runs. A run shorter than two years sinks below full-length runs instead of topping them on ratios built from a near-zero drawdown (an 18-day run ranked first). A walk-forward test that took no trades now sinks below every run that traded on NET as well, so $0 can no longer outrank a loss or take a column. Every ETFDIP variant is one family again. Books no longer win the smallest-drawdown mark from a sign difference, and their robustness cell says why it is blank instead of printing NaN.

BOOKS WITH AN ORB LEG ARE NO LONGER FLAGGED FOR A BUG THEY DO NOT HAVE. 22 of 26 books, adopted #366 and #396 included, carried an ORB look-ahead warning that belongs to the old touch-entry ORB files only; the always-on note under the table is gone and the badge now appears only for those files. Gate-Validate runs read the same whole-run and in-sample figures on every screen, EXPLORE stops rebuilding a book's Sharpe and Sortino from a thinned curve, and the PICK RUNS money tile follows the stage you are looking at instead of always showing the tuning figure.

CHARTS: THE LOCKBOX AND IN-SAMPLE SLICES SIT ON THEIR OWN DATES. On the RUNBOARD funnel a one-year lockbox curve was drawn across the whole 16-year width, and its key read the whole run's years and a different stretch's dollars. Each slice now has its own span, and the key shows the stage's own figure marked as approximate. Saved curves place their lockbox door at its real date rather than spreading trades evenly, so a door no longer lands months early. The full-screen view opens with every picked run drawn and keeps the runs you greyed or hid switched off, a hand-added run always gets its own column, and two EXPLORE hovers that described the wrong rows or the wrong rule now say what actually happens.

WALK-FORWARD PF ON OLDER RUNS NOW MATCHES COMPARE. The run report's older walk-forward column left out a fold that lost every trade, or won every trade, when it pooled profit factor, so the same run could read 1.81 on the report and 1.76 on every COMPARE screen. It now pools them the same way. Every screen also names the fold behind a dash - a fold that broke exactly even, or one that lost every dollar but saved no win count - instead of calling the run too old.

EXPLORE: hovering a table row lights its pinned RANK / FAMILY / RUN cells too; in the STACK layout the sideways scrollbar stays inside its column; the ticked column heading is no longer see-through; trade counts show as whole numbers. The note under the chart names MAR or PROFIT, counts each cause once, words the MIN TRADES note correctly, and offers LOAD ALL only when runs are really missing - including while a LOAD ALL is still arriving, when it used to claim the runs were not on this account. 1E CONFIGS prints one off-chart line instead of two that disagreed.

RUNBOARD / PICK RUNS: a lockbox that took no trades no longer wins the LB $ best mark with $0; a lockbox where every trade won shows a dash with its reason instead of PF 0.00; figures marked ~ take no heat shading; the RUNBOARD inside COMPARE opens on LOCKBOX when no stage was saved; the walk-forward WINDOW shows the split-to-lockbox dates on runs without a usable test and says why a saved test is not used; a PICK RUNS WF PF dash gives its reason. The top bar and Past Runs keep LOAD 75 MORE / LOAD ALL on screen while a bigger load is on its way.

Walk-forward charts: the key drops the in-sample line style, shows each test's length and gives each missing curve its own reason. The full-screen TRADES button is off on walk-forward, with the reason on hover, and dates no longer show a day early in US time zones. Past Runs GROUP view picks a book group's champion by pre-lockbox net over drawdown, the same rule as CHAMPIONS, and no longer prints score NaN; the CHAMPIONS hover describes that rule.

It saves as you tick and the box reads 10s + 1m. Trades with one timeframe are unchanged.
In ANALYTICS, BY TIMEFRAME counts a two-timeframe trade under both, so those rows can add up to more than your total, and the TRADES table TF filter finds a trade under either of its timeframes.

DROPDOWN LISTS ARE READABLE AGAIN (owner: the TF selector shows all white when clicked). When a dropdown opened - TF, SETUP, GRADE and every other one in the app - the browser drew its list on a white sheet while the words used the theme light text, so the choices were white on white. The open list now uses the theme dark background with light text, and the chosen item is shaded.

SECTION 1 IN TWO ROWS WHEN BOTH 1E CARDS ARE OPEN. The first row is the 1A config funnel beside the second 1E card (your scatter), so the scatter gets the width it lost as one of three tiles. The first 1E card - the table - now has a full-width row of its own underneath, so every column shows without scrolling sideways. Close the second 1E card and the row goes back to 1A beside 1E as before. Tile heights you dragged still apply; the width split in the new top row is remembered on its own.

MAX DRAWDOWN MATCHES THE CHART AGAIN (owner: keep drawdown matching the chart). A trade marked IGNORE IN METRICS now stays in MAX DD, the same as it stays in P&L and the equity chart. It is still left out of win rate, profit factor, averages, streaks and the breakdowns.

NOTES CAN BE ADDED AGAIN (owner: cant add notes). The NOTES column on the HOME table was plain text, and the trade panel showed notes without a way to change them. The column is now a box like CHART - click it, type, press Enter - and the panel has a notes area that saves when you click away.

IGNORE IN METRICS (owner: some trades were testing settings on the live account). Click a trade to open its panel and tick IGNORE IN METRICS. An ignored trade shows a small crossed-circle beside its symbol, and the WIN RATE tile says how many are being ignored.

HOME P&L PERCENT FIXED (owner: why does this say 100% all time?). In P&L view the percent under the big number divided your profit by your profit, so on ALL it always read +100.00%. It now divides by the money in the account: what the account held at the start of the range plus any deposits made during it. All time that is $79.66 on $4,476.08 put in, +1.78%. Hovering the chart measures each point the same way. EQUITY view is unchanged.

HOME TABLE: NEWEST TRADE ON TOP. The table view listed trades oldest first while the feed view lists newest first, so yesterday's VEEA trades sat at the very bottom of the table and a February SPY trade sat near the top - nothing was missing, the two views were in opposite order. The table now opens on your most recent trade, like the feed.

HOME TABLE: THE LEFT COLUMNS STAY PUT (owner: lock the columns up to the instrument name). The row number, DATE, IN, OUT, DUR and SYM now stay pinned on the left while you scroll the table sideways, so when you reach CHART, TAGS or NOTES you can still see which trade the row is.
1E MATRIX ALL table: the tile now grows to show every row, so the table no longer scrolls inside it. A dragged tile height still applies to the other tabs.

The unit under each heading: ROC over % / YR, WIN over %, DD over %, EV over R, R over / YR, DD over (R), NET over $. Those headings were the widest thing in their columns - ROC % / YR made its column about twice as wide as its numbers - and the cell padding is tighter too, so the table is much narrower.

1A funnel DOORS view: the lockbox panel is back to a quarter of the width. DOORS restarts every line at $0 in each panel, so it is not a timeline and has no reason to squeeze the lockbox; ONE CURVE stays on the calendar.

1E MATRIX ALL table is denser so more of it fits in the tile: rows lost most of their padding (about 12 px a row instead of 17) and the four-line explanation above the table is now one line - ALL CONFIGS, the count, PBO, the account chip - with the how-to moved into the hover on the info mark. About 40 per cent more rows show before the table scrolls.

1A CONFIG FUNNEL: THE LOCKBOX IS BACK ON THE CALENDAR. It had been fixed at a quarter of the width, which drew its one year about five times wider than any other year, so every lockbox line looked stretched even on runs where every lockbox trade is saved. The lockbox door now sits at its real date - about 6 per cent of the width on a 16-year run - so the chart reads as performance over time. The funnel, the expanded view, the CHAMPION tab and the 1B monthly bars underneath line up again.

COMPARE ON WALK-FORWARD NOW READS THE SAVED WALK-FORWARD TEST. The LEADERBOARD, the comparison table and PICK RUNS fill in the drawdown, MAR, Sharpe, Sortino, profit factor, win rate and window length of the folds’ own unseen trades joined in fold order. Money, trade counts and folds held are still pooled from the fold results, and nothing on the whole-run, tuning or lockbox stretches moved. MAR and Sharpe now rank on walk-forward; a run saved before that detail existed shows a dash saying so and sorts last.

THE COMPARE CHART DRAWS THAT TEST. On the walk-forward stretch each picked run is drawn as its folds joined end to end over their own dates - one dashed line, no sealed-lockbox tail - and a run that saved none is listed beside the chart instead of showing its whole run under a walk-forward heading.

RUNBOARD HAS A WALK-FORWARD SAMPLE. The funnel, the grid and the strategy list now read that stretch instead of holding the whole view, every empty cell says why in plain words, and the window row shows the dates the test covers. Books keep a hold of their own: a book trades frozen configurations and tunes nothing, so it has no walk-forward stage.

EXPLORE: a run row ticked on walk-forward alone now plots its drawdown, MAR, Sharpe, Sortino, profit factor, win rate and years, and the READ hover MAR is the ticked stretch’s own. Walk-forward plus lockbox still dashes - they are two separate trade sequences and no joined one is saved - and now says that. A report left open while a job finishes no longer keeps saying the detail was never saved.

A WALK-FORWARD THAT TOOK NO TRADES READS $0 AND 0 TRADES, AND NOTHING ELSE. Its pooled money and trade count print as the readings they are; its profit factor, win rate, drawdown, MAR, Sharpe, Sortino and expectancy - and its dollars per trade, where a screen shows that for the folds - dash with one sentence, that the run took no trades in the walk-forward folds, on the leaderboard, the comparison table, PICK RUNS, the RUNBOARD, EXPLORE and the report alike. Neither that $0 nor the empty drawdown takes a best mark or a heat shade, and ranked on drawdown or MAR the run sorts after every run that traded, so a strategy that never traded the folds can no longer take the smallest-drawdown mark, or the top of the order, from one that did. A test that saved no window dates leaves MAR, R / YR and ROC blank on all five rather than annualising the folds’ own money over the longer tuning-split window. And one expectancy in R is read off that test everywhere it is shown, instead of two figures a rounding apart.

PAST RUNS AND THE REPORT NOW AGREE ON HOW MANY TRADES A RUN TOOK. The runs table said 1,257 on run 398 where the report header, and the run own saved record, both say 996. The row was adding the in-sample fit to the walk-forward folds re-tuned trades and the lockbox - three different configurations - so the walk-forward years were counted twice. The count now comes from the run own whole-run record, as its net dollars, drawdown, Sharpe and win rate already did.

The same row PROFIT FACTOR was pooled from those three pieces and is now the champion measured one: run 398 reads 2.01 against the pooled 1.67. Runs saved before those figures existed keep the pooled numbers. The TOTAL column of the report stage table is fixed the same way, so the two never disagree again.

CHART COLUMN ON THE HOME TRADE TABLE ACCEPTS A LINK AGAIN (owner: 'i cant add a link to the chart here'). That column only ever drew an icon when a chart link was already saved, and a row without one showed a dash with nothing behind it - the only way in was the pencil at the end of the row. It is now the same paste box the TRADES tab has: click the dash, paste the link, press Enter. A saved link keeps its small chart icon, the icon still opens the chart in a new tab, and hovering it previews the snapshot. Clicking into the box no longer opens the trade detail panel behind it.

RUN REPORT 1C NOW DRAWS THE WALK-FORWARD TEST ITSELF. The engine saves, on every validate, the walk-forward folds' own unseen trades joined in fold order - each fold re-tuned on its own past - and 160 older runs were rebuilt the same way. 1C now draws that curve with a divider at each fold and chips beside it: net, PF, win %, trades, max drawdown, MAR per year, Sharpe, Sortino and the window. A fold that took no trades is marked as such instead of borrowing the fold before it, and a run with nothing saved says why in plain words (saved before this existed, walk-forward did not run, or a book, which tunes nothing).

1E WALK-FORWARD COLUMN: SHARPE AND SORTINO WERE THE WRONG MEASUREMENT. That column is the champion held constant over the walk-forward years, but its Sharpe came from a fold-by-fold series and Sortino was blank (run 306: 0.79 and a dash, now 1.69 and 3.60). IN-SAMPLE Sharpe on that path changes for the same reason. Every hover on the screen now names one source per figure: net and trades pooled across the folds, PF and win % from the saved walk-forward test when the run has one, drawdown, Sharpe and Sortino from that test alone. A test that saved no window dates leaves MAR, ROC and R / YR blank rather than divide by an estimate.

PAST RUNS: hovering a run's WF cell shows its walk-forward test figures, and the fold hovers on the equity chart, the funnel and 1C now carry the real fold dates and trade counts instead of estimates. The run list carries this detail with each run at no extra read cost.

EXPLORE TABLES: KPIS FIRST, CONFIG LAST (owner: 'move this junk to the end of the row'). Every table now reads RANK, FAMILY, RUN, then MAR, SHARPE, SORTINO, PF, WIN %, EV R, R / YR, ROC % / YR, $/TRD, TRADES, TRADES / YR, then READ, with the long configuration name and its badges at the very end. RANK, FAMILY and RUN stay pinned on the left while you scroll right, and the heading row stays pinned to the top of the table.

EXPLORE TABLES NO LONGER SNAP BACK (owner: 'the table keeps snapping me back to the upper left'). Changing an unrelated control keeps the table exactly where you scrolled it; only a new LEVEL, SHOW or strategy starts a fresh table at the top left. In the side-by-side layout the table area is now bounded to your window, so its sideways scrollbar is on screen instead of below the fold - on a laptop a table 9,988 pixels tall now sits in a 667 pixel box.

EXPLORE EMPTY CHART EXPLAINS ITSELF (owner: 'why is this not showing anything?'). When rows are missing from the chart the note underneath breaks them down by cause with counts - failed runs hidden, a measure never recorded for that stretch, rows citing runs older than the ones loaded, a stretch that took no trades - and offers one-click buttons (PLOT FAILURES ON, SHOW 1E CONFIGS, another stretch, another measure, LOAD ALL), each showing how many rows it would actually place, counted with the same readers the chart uses.

WRITE-UP ROWS NO LONGER INVENT A PER-YEAR FIGURE. A study row that records one window for the whole row used to divide one stretch's money by the whole window's years - a one-year lockbox over sixteen years read 5.5% a year. It now shows that figure only when the ticked stretches are the row's whole recorded window, or when the row cites a loaded run whose saved windows give the stretch's real dates; otherwise it dashes and says why.

COMPARE AUDIT ROUND 2 (11 fixes) plus the fixes three independent reviews found on top of them. FULL profit factor reads the champion's own whole-run figure (#335 read 1.48 where the champion ran 1.82); books are no longer counted as a strategy anywhere (#397 sat in the ENGU-Q column where #335 belongs); a run you starred stays on the board when it is older than the loaded runs; IN-SAMPLE MAR and R / YR are annualised over the tuning years the search actually scored (they read about 25% low); RUNBOARD trade counts, sort order and best marks follow what the table prints; a lockbox or stretch that took no trades dashes with the reason everywhere instead of showing $0, 0.00 or a best mark; strategy files sharing one short label show their own names; EXPLORE stretch combinations a run never saved together are pooled honestly or dashed with the reason; chart hovers name the measures actually plotted.

COMPARE AUDIT ROUND 2 (11 fixes). Every book now sits in its own BOOKS group, RUNBOARD uses the leaderboard's champion rule (your star wins), and a strategy file whose name merely starts with COMBINED is no longer mistaken for a book.
A run you starred stays on the LEADERBOARD, the OVERLAY and its family crown even when it is older than the loaded runs; the run-count note shows + N STARRED OLDER and names them on hover.

IN-SAMPLE means the tuning search's own pick on the first 75% of the tuning years, and its MAR and R / YR are now annualised over those years (they read about 25% low). A book's in-sample years stop where its lockbox starts. Walk-forward R / YR on the LEADERBOARD and OVERLAY now shows a number that matches EXPLORE.

RUNBOARD: whole-run trades use the run's own saved total (#382 read 6,020, real 4,825); sorting by PF, drawdown or net sorts by the printed number; most trades and highest win % are no longer marked best; books tables say NET / DD and SLICES instead of MAR and WF; top 10 recent shows a dash, not $0, for a run with no figure; live books follow RANK BY.

A lockbox with no trades shows a dash with the reason on every figure instead of $0 (a lockbox that lost every trade shows PF 0.00). Strategy files sharing one short label (three ETF-dip files all read ETFDI 1.0) show their own names on the LEADERBOARD and OVERLAY. The TOP RUNS short-window badge no longer says the champion list leaves the run out.

EXPLORE: ticking stretches a run never saved together (IN-SAMPLE + LOCKBOX always) now builds PF and win rate from the ticked stretches and dashes drawdown, MAR, Sharpe and Sortino with the reason, instead of showing the whole-run figure (766 of 894 NOISE config rows were outside their own IS and LB range). Chart hovers name the measures actually plotted, the QUALITY preset plots EV R up and Sortino across as described, and MIN TRADES no longer double-counts rows.
1E MATRIX ALL table: the tile now grows to show every row, so the table no longer scrolls inside it. A dragged tile height still applies to the other tabs.

The unit under each heading: ROC over % / YR, WIN over %, DD over %, EV over R, R over / YR, DD over (R), NET over $. Those headings were the widest thing in their columns - ROC % / YR made its column about twice as wide as its numbers - and the cell padding is tighter too, so the table is much narrower.

1A funnel DOORS view: the lockbox panel is back to a quarter of the width. DOORS restarts every line at $0 in each panel, so it is not a timeline and has no reason to squeeze the lockbox; ONE CURVE stays on the calendar.

NOISE ROUND 57, PART TWO - SINGLE VALIDATES OF THE EXACT CONFIGS (owner: run single validates on the exact configs too). READ THEM WITH CARE. A Gate-validate headline on Past Runs is the ML filter number, not the plain config. The plain config rows are inside the report as ungated. WIN % IS ON BOTH EXPLORE AXES, right after PF (owner: add win rate next to PF). It plots the win rate of the ticked stretch, the same figure the WIN % column prints, and a row that saves none for that stretch is left off the chart and named underneath.

ONE MAR ON EXPLORE (owner: go for 3).
