HYBRID RECYCLED AND EQUAL-DRAWDOWN ROWS ARE SIZED PER STRETCH (owner: go for 4). They scaled every stretch by one factor measured on the whole run. The run report has sized each stretch by its own ungated twin since v69.6, and the board now does the same, so under REDEPLOY or EQUAL DD a walk-forward or lockbox figure is what that sizing earns on that stretch - which also means the stretches no longer have to add up to the whole. DD (R) on EVERY configuration row that saves an average loss per stretch - raw, tilt, keel and all three hybrids, not only the sized ones - now divides the stretch drawdown by that same stretch average losing trade. It used to divide by the whole-run average loss, so a single-stretch tick mixed two stretches; the figure moves for those rows. Gate rows save no per-stretch average loss and are unchanged. Under a combined tick a sized hybrid reads the combined stretch own total at that stretch own factor, as the report does.

RUNBOARD WHOLE-RUN DRAWDOWN IS THE SAVED ONE (owner: go for 6). It was read off the saved equity curve even though every validated run saves a whole-run drawdown. Checked on 46 runs: the saved figure is never smaller, and the curve read up to a third shallow, so a whole-run MAR on RUNBOARD read up to 1.5 times high. The saved figure is used now. Where a drawdown still has to come off the curve it carries a ~, is explained under the grid, and can never take the best mark. Correction to the audit: books were never affected - RUNBOARD reads each book own saved drawdown.

HYBRID RECYCLE AND HYBRID EQUAL-DRAWDOWN: THE STRETCH ROWS NOW ADD UP TO TOTAL (owner pick, option A). These two tabs size each hybrid column up or down. Since v73.768 their TOTAL and DD used one size for the whole ticked SAMPLE, but the IS $, WF $ and LB $ rows still used a separate size per stretch - on run #384 the rf hybrid, IS + WF ticked, read IS $49k + WF $565k beside a TOTAL of $746k.

Every dollar row, TOTAL, DD, EV and AVG CONTRACTS on those two tabs now use the same single size for the ticked years, so the rows add up: the same rf column reads IS $30k + WF $716k = $746k. A stretch row can therefore change when you tick or untick another stretch - same trades, sized for the whole pick. The one-lot HYBRID, TILT and KEEL tabs do not change.
The 1E render gate now checks that the stretch rows add up to TOTAL on the recycle tab, for a current run, an old run and a pick that skips a stretch, and it fails the previous build.

CORRECTION TO v73.769, found checking it against live runs. Drawdown, Sharpe and Sortino for IN-SAMPLE, WALK-FORWARD and WALK-FORWARD + LOCKBOX on a run row were cut from the saved equity curve at a boundary placed by trade count. That boundary was wrong: the saved curve is the champion held at one set of settings across every year, while the walk-forward folds are re-fitted and trade a different number of times - run #340 champion made 215 walk-forward trades against 236 in its folds, run #343 made 505 against 481. Those cuts measured the wrong stretch and now dash. The claim that the curve boundary was placed exactly is withdrawn.

What stays, and why it is sound: LOCKBOX keeps its saved figures; IN-SAMPLE + WALK-FORWARD, whose money is exactly the champion pre-lockbox money, keeps a drawdown, Sharpe and Sortino cut from the curve at the saved lockbox boundary, and that drawdown carries a ~; ALL THREE reads the run own saved whole-run totals, with no ~. Books keep theirs, because a book has no walk-forward and its split is that same saved boundary.

Read IN-SAMPLE on a run row for what it is: the whole run minus the pooled, re-fitted walk-forward folds minus the lockbox - the same remainder the run report and RUNBOARD use for in-sample money. Its trades, profit factor and win rate follow that convention; they are not the champion own in-sample trades, which only the configurations view of a run carries.

QQQ SHADOW BOOK CAN NOW RUN OFF THE CLOUD SIGNAL ENGINE INSTEAD OF NINJATRADER (owner: move it off NinjaTrader, which kept disconnecting and cost the shadow every trade on 2026-09-03/04). A new setting, signal source, defaults to ENGINE: entries and exits now come from the same crowned strategies computed on Webull or Yahoo QQQ bars, and shadow fill prices come from that same bar, never from NinjaTrader or the NQ export. The old NinjaTrader mirror is kept as a fallback setting for now. Every rail is unchanged either way: the share cap, the daily loss breaker, the session window, the kill file and the feed heartbeat.

THE NOISE LEG WAS STALE. The cloud signal engine was still pricing the NOISE leg off the retired run 243 config from three weeks ago; it now uses the current crown, run 304, the same definition already used by the NQ paper board.

NINJATRADER MODE ALSO GOT SAFER: a strategy re-enable or relaunch can fire a startup entry that matches no real signal (this happened twice on 2026-09-03). Those are now ignored and clearly marked rather than mixed in with real trades, on a five-minute guard window.

QQQ PAPER TAB: a new STATUS block at the top states, in plain words, the signal source, the price source and how many seconds behind it is, whether this is running on the PC or in the cloud, and the age of the last update with a clear STALE label. Each leg now shows its run number (314, 335, 304) and the ENGU-Q leg keeps its own caveat about running an ETH-fit crown on a regular-hours-only tape.

RUN ROWS ON EXPLORE FOLLOW THE STAGE YOU TICK (owner: the metrics should follow the sample selected). A run row used to carry figures for the LOCKBOX only: under any other tick its money followed the stage while PF, drawdown, win %, Sharpe, Sortino, EV R, DD (R) and MAR quietly read the whole run, and walk-forward per-year figures divided by the whole run. Each run row now carries its own figures for every stretch, from what the run saved.

WALK-FORWARD pools the folds - money, trades, wins, and gross wins and losses rebuilt from each fold own net and profit factor. LOCKBOX is the saved lockbox. IN-SAMPLE is the whole run minus walk-forward minus lockbox, which is exact because trades, wins and both grosses add; checked against the saved curve end to the dollar. IN-SAMPLE + WALK-FORWARD and WALK-FORWARD + LOCKBOX add the two; ALL THREE is the run own whole-run totals. A book reads its own pre-lockbox, lockbox and whole blocks.

Drawdown, Sharpe and Sortino that were never saved for a stretch are cut from the saved equity curve, which is laid out per trade - its lockbox mark sits at exactly the lockbox share of trades - so the in-sample / walk-forward boundary is placed by trade count. A drawdown cut that way carries a ~ in the MAR and DRAWDOWN cells, because the curve is thinned for storage and can only read shallow.

WHERE IT CANNOT BE DONE IT SAYS SO. On 6 of the 44 validated runs loaded today, including the ENGU-Q crown #335, the walk-forward folds hold more trades than follow the split, so they overlap the in-sample years; those runs dash every in-sample figure with that reason rather than printing a remainder that mixes the two - and any tick that includes IN-SAMPLE dashes the money-based figures too, rather than quietly adding up only the stretches that can be read; with all three ticked they read the whole-run total, which is known exactly. IN-SAMPLE + LOCKBOX has no combined drawdown or profit factor, so those dash, with the trades added.

THE TILT, KEEL AND HYBRID TABLES UNDERSTATED DRAWDOWN ON TWO-STRETCH SAMPLES. With IS + WF or WF + LB ticked on the 1E matrix, the DD row was read off the saved equity curve - about 300 points across the whole run - so any drop that opened and closed between two saved points never showed. On run #384 all 32 of those cells read low, by 2% to 34%, and MAR, DD (R) and the heat map inherited the error.

THOSE TWO PICKS NOW READ THE ENGINE OWN FIGURES for the combined span, measured trade by trade - the same figures the GATE tab already used. On the one-lot tabs dollars and trade counts do not move; drawdowns get deeper and lose the degree sign. On the HYBRID redeploy and equal-drawdown tabs these two picks now size each column with ONE ratio across the combined span, the way the all-three pick already did - the only way the drawdown beside the dollars describes the same book - so the dollars there move too (run #384 redeploy, IS + WF: up to 21%). Runs saved before the engine wrote these spans keep the old curve reading, still marked with the degree sign.
The 1E render gate now seeds combined spans whose drawdown the curve reading, the larger of the two parts and the sum of the two parts would each get wrong, and it fails the old build.

NOISE ROUND 57 - EVERY NOISE CONFIG THAT WAS NEVER AN AUTO-VALIDATE CHAMPION IS NOW QUEUED (owner: start auto validating the ones that are not). NOISE ROUND 56 - THE SCORECARD (owner: rank the noise configs with their metrics, and say which are auto-validated, which are not, and which need it). Every NOISE configuration run so far was replayed on one continuous tape and window at house cost, ranked on recent profit factor first. The full table, with trades, win rate, net, profit factor, drawdown, profit factor by era and sealed year, and each validation status, is in the family doc.

THE TOP ROW IS NEW: the squeeze FILTER on the live crown. Run 321 validated the filter on the retired base. Moved onto the live crown, the textbook hourly setting keeps 615 trades at profit factor 2.351, 2.184 since 2024 and 1.985 in the sealed year, with one losing year of seventeen and 1.814 without its ten best trades. 25 of the 27 grid settings beat the raw crown and all nine hourly settings sit between 1.68 and 2.35, but the textbook cell is the top of that plateau, so expect nearer 2.0.

ONLY ONE CONFIG NEEDS A VALIDATE AND IT IS QUEUED: run 321 re-based onto the live crown with its own 27-cell grid unchanged, parity checked to the dollar. Its saved lockbox must be read on a continuous replay. The other never-validated configs either duplicate a validated one or fail on their own numbers.
ALSO ON THIS BASIS the retired 243 outranks the live crown on every quality number and made slightly more in the sealed year - the crown swap was a coin flip, not an upgrade.

THE ML LINES NO LONGER RUN STRAIGHT AFTER THE LOCKBOX DOOR (owner: the lockbox on the 1A funnel still shows as stretched). Measured on run 384: the gate, tilt, KEEL, hybrid, recycle and ALL CONFIGS lines each had about 20 saved points for the whole lockbox year - one point every 11 pixels, against one every 2.5 before the door - so with the lockbox a quarter of the width they drew as long straight strokes. The raw config lines never did this, because they save their lockbox stretch on its own with 80 points.

WHY. Every ML line is saved as ONE 300-point sample of the whole run. On run 384 the 273 lockbox trades are under 7 per cent of its 4,075 trades, so they get under 7 per cent of the points - about 20 - however wide the lockbox is drawn.

THE FIX. New validates save a dense lockbox section next to every ML line: up to 80 points read off the real trade-by-trade running total, never smoothed or filled in. The funnel draws the saved points up to the door, the value on the door, then that section - in ONE CURVE, DOORS, ALL CONFIGS and the fullscreen explorer. The in-sample and walk-forward part of each line is unchanged, and so is every finish figure, pill and key value, because the section ends on the same final total. A line whose saved sample already has as many lockbox points - a short run, or one whose lockbox is a big share of its trades - keeps that sample, so no lockbox is ever drawn with fewer real points than before; and a lockbox so small that only the final saved point sat past the door, the most stretched case of all, does get its section.

OLD RUNS. Runs saved before this carry no lockbox section, so they keep exactly their old look (checked byte for byte on run 384 and on the report test run) until they are backfilled or re-run - and new validates only carry it once the runner is running this version. A section that does not line up with its own curve is ignored rather than drawn in the wrong place.

NOISE ROUND 55 - THE FRONTIER, LIKE FOR LIKE (owner: which noise configuration is most worthy of forward or live testing, and does anything never auto-validated approach the frontier). No two NOISE rows on the board are comparable - three different end dates, each with its own split and lockbox - so every distinct candidate was replayed on one tape, one window, two costs and the same eras.

RUN 382 CORRECTED. It returned PASS with a lockbox of 239 trades at profit factor 1.395. The continuous run takes 314 trades that year at 1.275, the crown own figure: the validate grades its lockbox by reloading the tape with no history, and NOISE needs forty prior sessions, so a quarter of the year vanishes. On the continuous basis its own pick fails the bar written into its file. Every saved NOISE lockbox is a cold-restart number, so round 54 ranking is replaced.

THE ONE THING THAT BEATS THE CROWN: the textbook hourly squeeze (hourly frame, length 20, ratio 1.0) as a 1.5x size tilt. It sat inside run 382 grid and was never picked because that search ranks on dollars. It beats the crown in both eras at both costs, passes the whole tilt battery at both costs (walk-forward drawdown falls 11 percent, zero of 2000 shifts match), sits on a plateau (all four hourly cells beat all four 30-minute cells), and keeps 97 percent of its gain when read a full hour late, so it is not a look-ahead. Thin spot: only 41 tagged trades in the sealed year.

NOTHING ELSE BEATS IT. Run 316 (confirm 2 bars) comes closest with far less drawdown, but since 2024 it earns 22 percent less on 11 percent less resampled risk. The 2-minute, 15-minute and 1-minute cards, the cost-robust corner and run 305 all lose their recent profit factor. The momentum tilt is real but adds 34 to 73 percent drawdown. The textbook squeeze on the live crown is not on paper anywhere yet.

BOTH AXES OFFER THE SAME TWELVE MEASURES, IN THE SAME ORDER (owner: anything missing from the vertical or the horizontal, add it; left to right should go from risk metrics to reward metrics). The vertical axis gains DRAWDOWN in dollars - DD % was already there - and the horizontal gains RAW PROFIT, MAR and EV in dollars.

The order on both is SORTINO, SHARPE, DD (R), DD %, DRAWDOWN, MAR, PF, EV R, EV, R / YR, ROC % / YR, RAW PROFIT: risk-adjusted first, then the drawdowns, then reward over risk, then reward per trade, then reward per year, then the money itself.

On VS CROWN the point hover now names the horizontal measure it is quoting. It said drawdown whatever was across the bottom - Sortino, EV R, anything - which predates these new pairings but would have mislabelled them too.

$/TRD FOLLOW-UP: the fix one version ago also moves EV (dollars per trade) wherever it is plotted, on either axis, because the chart reads the same figure the column prints. And a row that saves per-stage figures but no trade count of its own now takes its whole-run count rather than falling back to the ticked stage.

Each new pairing uses the reader the other axis already had, so a row sits at the same value whichever side a measure is put on. Dollar drawdown up the side ranks the SHALLOWEST first, like DD % and DD (R), and is never divided per year - a drawdown is one worst event, not a rate.

RUN IS ITS OWN COLUMN, AND IT SORTS (owner: auto validate has different runs, I want to be able to sort that). It sits beside FAMILY on every table, not only under ALL columns, so configurations from different runs can be grouped at a glance. Click the heading to put the newest run first; rows never saved as a run sit last. It replaces the grey RUN column that only ALL used to show, so nothing is listed twice.

TRADES / YR, beside TRADES (owner: there is a cumulative trade count but no trades per year). It is the trade count divided by the years of the ticked stretch - the same count and the same window R / YR already uses, so EV R times TRADES / YR is R / YR on every row and the two can never disagree. It sorts like every other number column.

$/TRD IS WHOLE-RUN MONEY OVER WHOLE-RUN TRADES AGAIN, as its heading has always said. On a configuration row the trade count was being read per ticked stage while the money stayed whole-run, so with only WALK-FORWARD ticked, for example, a row divided all of its money by its walk-forward trades and read several times too high. Sorting on $/TRD also used a third formula of its own; it now orders by the figure the column prints.

FIXED ON THE WAY: with IN-SAMPLE and LOCKBOX ticked and WALK-FORWARD not, a configuration row printed its WHOLE-RUN trade count and divided by a window that still included the unticked walk-forward years. That combination is the one with no saved block of its own. Trade counts now add up the ticked stretches and the years add up the ticked stretches, so TRADES, TRADES / YR, R / YR, ROC, DD (R) and the MIN TRADES chart filter all read the stretches actually ticked. Every other combination gives exactly the figures it did before, because touching stretches add up to the same span.

DOORS - THE 1A FUNNEL CUT AT ITS DOORS (owner: go for the door; the lockbox seems stretched here). A new ONE CURVE / DOORS switch sits on the funnel control row. DOORS draws the same chart as three panels - in-sample, walk-forward, lockbox - and every line starts again at $0 at each door, on that panel's own dollar scale.

WHY THE LOCKBOX LOOKED STRETCHED. On one continuous axis the lockbox gets about five times the width per year that a walk-forward year gets, so the same pace draws about five times flatter after the door, and the gate, tilt and hybrid lines only have around twenty saved points in there. DOORS gives each stretch the full height, so the lockbox is read on its own terms.

WHAT STAYS THE SAME. The dates, the fold stripes, the lockbox stripe and the drawdown strip underneath do not change - drawdown is still one continuous account. The key rows, ALL CONFIGS, the hover link to the 1E tables and the hold-up ladder work in both modes. Each panel labels its own peak, $0 and low, each sitting at the value it names; the right-hand equity scale is left out of DOORS because there is no single scale, and the hover $ reads from the panel under the pointer.

THE KEY MOVES OUT OF THE WAY. In DOORS the in-sample panel fills its full height, so the key box shows names only (each row still gives its finish on hover, and ALL CONFIGS drops its line count) and moves to the panel corner that hides the fewest lines and no panel label.

THE LAST TRADES ARE KEPT. A saved equity curve is a sample that leaves off the final few trades; ONE CURVE shows that as a small step where the lockbox tail starts. In DOORS each raw walk-forward line and each lockbox tail ends on the true total instead, so the panels add up. On a run whose raw configs saved no lockbox curve but whose ML block has lockbox trades, the ML lines stop at the lockbox rather than carrying its money into the walk-forward panel.

HOVER $ FIXED IN BOTH MODES. The dollar readout on the right edge measured against the whole chart box, padding included, so every level read a few per cent off (the top of run 384 read $952k against a true $993k).

CHECKED. ONE CURVE is byte-for-byte what v73.756 drew. On run 384 every DOORS line equals its ONE CURVE line less its value at the door, within drawing rounding, and every walk-forward and lockbox piece starts at $0.

THE LOCKBOX NOW TAKES A QUARTER OF THE 1A FUNNEL (owner: one curve first, the LB at 25% is fine). It used to sit where the calendar puts it - about 6 per cent of the width on a 15-year run - which was too thin to read the lines the funnel exists to judge. The walk-forward fold stripes, every line, the ALL CONFIGS lines, the drawdown strip and the hover date all moved together, and the date strip now has a tick on the lockbox door. A short run whose lockbox is already more than a quarter of its calendar keeps its true share. This deliberately undoes the calendar placement from v71.4. The expanded view and the CHAMPION tab still use the calendar, because they have real date axes, so the lockbox looks wider on this tab than on those - and the 1B monthly bars underneath are calendar-spaced, so they no longer line up under the funnel.

NEW: THE HOLD-UP LADDER, UNDER THE FUNNEL AND ITS DRAWDOWN STRIP. One small chart per family. Every config is a line through three columns - in-sample, walk-forward, lockbox - at the dollars it made inside that stretch, scaled within its family. Parallel lines mean the in-sample favourites stayed on top; crossing lines mean the order flipped. Underneath each family: how well the in-sample order held into the lockbox, from +1 (exactly the same) to -1 (fully reversed), marked only N where there are too few configs to lean on. The ring marks the most in-sample dollars in each family - named that way on purpose, because the funnel blue in-sample-best line ranks by the search own score and can be a different config.

THE LADDER NUMBERS ARE THE 1E TABLE NUMBERS. Nothing is recomputed: each line is drawn from the family table own column, with the same key its row carries. Checked in a browser on run 384 with the SAMPLE tick on in-sample, then walk-forward, then lockbox - 51 of 51 configs matched the table in every stretch - and on a second run with different families. Hovering picks the line nearest the pointer, fills a one-line readout with its three figures, and lights the same config in the 1E table (on its family tab too) and on the funnel.

DRAWDOWN STRIP. The lockbox door is now drawn down through it, so the wider lockbox has an edge there too. Two switches were broken: the KEEL key row hid KEEL line but not its drawdown line, and switching GATE off was quietly undone by its own drawdown line staying visible. Both fixed.

HYBRID LINES BENT AT THE WRONG POINT, on the funnel and inside the 1E tables. A hybrid curve runs across every trade, including the ones it skipped, but its lockbox door was placed by counting only the trades it took - so on run 384 it bent at point 272 of 300 while tilt, KEEL and gate bent at 279. Inside 1E the same counting put its in-sample / walk-forward cut at 27 per cent of the curve against a true 38. All five families now cut at the same, correct place; the tilt, KEEL and gate figures do not change.
Hovering a config now lights its lockbox stretch as well - the dotted lockbox tails were the one part of each line that never joined the highlight.

HOVERING A ROW OR A DOT NOW LIGHTS ITS LINE ON THE 1A FUNNEL (owner ask, third time). The join is by identity, not by name: the funnel and the 1E table are drawing the SAME configuration objects, so each line is stamped with a handle that survives the table being re-sorted, and the real link is swapped in once the column order is settled. Checked in a browser on run 384 - ten funnel lines carry the link and all ten match a row in the table, with none left pointing at nothing.

A LINE ALSO HAD TO LOOK PICKED. The highlight fades everything else and brightens the one you want, which reads well on a dot and not at all on a half-pixel line. The hovered line thickens now, which is what actually reads on a chart of thin curves.

WHAT LIGHTS AND WHAT DOES NOT, plainly: the ten RAW configuration lines do. The gate, tilt, KEEL and hybrid lines do NOT yet - the funnel draws one line per family plus a bundle of candidates behind the ALL CONFIGS toggle, and those carry no handle back to their row. They can be wired the same way and it is the obvious next piece; I would rather say so than have you hover a tilt row and wonder why nothing happens.
The funnel lines other than the crowned one only DRAW when ALL CONFIGS is on, so that is where you will see this. With it off there is one line and it is already obvious.

THE LAST TWO FUNNEL LINES THAT WERE NOT FULL STRENGTH (owner: all I am asking is to change the line opacity to all be the same). Two versions ago I levelled the six named lines and stopped there. Turning ALL CONFIGS on draws every remaining candidate through a different piece of code, at just over a third strength - so the moment that toggle is on, which is how your funnel is set, the chart had two populations at two different opacities all over again. They are at full strength now. They stay thin, because there are about 37 of them and thickness was not what you asked about. A stray gate line on the non-funnel version of the same chart was at 95 per cent for the same reason and is now at full too.

Every stroke on that chart is now at full strength except one, and that one is on purpose: the faint grey cloud. Those configurations STOP at the in-sample door and never reach the walk-forward - being faint is what tells you that, and it is the one thing the funnel exists to show. Say the word and it goes to full as well.

THE CONCENTRATION PILL AND ITS OWN CARD NO LONGER DISAGREE (owner: why does the pill say top 5 is under 10 per cent of net when underneath it says half the profit came from 13 of 4,075 trades - is that not conflicting). It was, and the pill was the wrong one. The pill was worked out once when the page drew, from the 400-trade sample the run saves; the card beneath it is rebuilt from the real trade list the moment that arrives, and nothing ever went back to correct the pill. On this run the sample never even reaches half the run real profit, so the pill gave up on the sentence and fell back to a top-5 percentage - a floor of 10 per cent against a true 24. Both now come from the same numbers.

AND IT WAS GREEN FOR A SECOND REASON. The pill had four states and only three colours - anything that was not bad or warn came out green, including the state that means measured from a sample, nothing alarming in it. That is why it sat there in green with a GREY status dot beside it, the dot having got it right all along. Unmeasured reads are grey now, like the dot.

WHAT THE PILL WILL NOT DO IS GUESS. The trade list it reads is capped at the most recent 6,000 trades, so on a longer run it is real trades but the wrong stretch. In that case the pill keeps the sampled wording, which at least counts the whole run, and the card says the most recent N of M instead of claiming all of them. Where the card declines to answer at all, the pill declines too rather than printing a percentage of nothing.

HOVERING A DOT ON THE 1E SCATTER NOW LIGHTS ITS ROW ON THE OTHER 1E CARD (owner ask). Those dots were the one chart in the family that never carried the shared marker, so there was nothing to match on. Checked in a browser on your own layout - left card on ALL, right card on SCATTER - 51 rows and 52 dots now share it, the extra being the gold crowned ring, which fades with its own dot instead of staying lit. The PARALLEL view joins in as well.

A TILE YOU HAVE DRAGGED SHORTER NO LONGER HIDES THE SCROLLBAR. The bar lives at the bottom of the table box, the box was capped at a fixed height, and the card was locked to whatever height you dragged - so the bar ended up below the fold of its own card with no way to reach it. The cap follows the card now, and it is measured from where the table actually starts rather than assumed, so a wrapped control row or a narrow column cannot push it out of view either.

THE CONCENTRATION CURVE HAS AN AXIS SWITCH NOW (owner: why is the evenly spread line so compressed, is there a way to show it at 45 degrees). A diagonal only reads at 45 degrees when both axes cover the same range and the plot is square. This curve climbs to 437 per cent of net, so an axis that fits the curve cannot also put the reference line at 45 - the two asks are in direct conflict and no single frame satisfies both. So it is a choice, on the AXIS control beside the panel title.

FIT CURVE is what you have been looking at: the axis follows the curve, you see how far the winners get and how much the losers hand back, and the evenly spread line lies almost flat - measured at 4 degrees, which is what you were reacting to.

45 REFERENCE draws a square plot that stops at 100 per cent, so the evenly spread book is a true 45 degree line - measured at exactly 45 - and the panel reads as the classic inequality curve. The curve leaves through the top of that frame, and where it does the chart marks the spot and says how high it got, so nothing is quietly cropped.

THE COLUMN HEADERS ON THE 1E ALL TABLE STAY PUT NOW (owner ask). They were never pinned - not a pin that failed, there was simply no pinning on that row. And a pin alone would have done nothing: the box the table sits in scrolls sideways, so it is the box a pinned header would anchor to, but it had no height of its own and so never scrolled up and down - the header would have drifted away with the page regardless. The box is capped in height now, which makes it the thing that scrolls vertically, and the header row is pinned to it with a solid background so the gold crowned row cannot show through, and its own separator line because the old one belonged to the first row and left with it.

YOU COULD ALWAYS SCROLL THAT TABLE SIDEWAYS - YOU JUST COULD NOT SEE HOW (owner, twice: cant scroll over horizontally). 887 pixels of columns in a 349 pixel window, and the bar to drag was three pixels tall on a transparent track, under a fifty-row table. It is eleven pixels now with a visible track, on that table only. Shift and the wheel has always worked too, and the panel says so now.

THE ALL TAB GETS A WIDER COLUMN. It holds sixteen columns in the narrower of section one three columns, so the card itself was 373 pixels and the table was already using every pixel of it - there was nothing to reclaim inside the card. The column is wider while that tab is open and goes back when you leave it, so the other tabs and the comparison card are unchanged. Measured 349 to 472 pixels. If you have dragged the section-one splitters yourself your sizes still win; double-click a splitter to clear them.

THE HOVER HIGHLIGHT WAS NEVER BROKEN - IT WAS ON A TAB YOU DID NOT HAVE OPEN. The dots it pairs with live on the 1A card RISK MAP tab, not on the trade scatter in section 2. With 1A on RISK MAP and 1E on ALL, all 51 dots and all 51 rows carry the same key and hovering either lights the other - checked in a browser, 51 of 51 matched. The panel now says so on its own header rather than leaving you to find it.

THE CONCENTRATION CURVE WAS RUNNING INTO ITS OWN CEILING (owner: is this still an accurate representation). The numbers under it were right - half the profit from 13 of 4,075 trades, top 10 equals 42 per cent, 451,840 dollars without the top 5 - but the picture was not. The curve walks the trades best first, so it climbs to everything the winners banked and then gives back down to what you actually kept. On run 384 the winners banked 2.6 million against a 596 thousand net, so the curve peaks at 437 per cent - and the chart stopped at 125. Everything past about one per cent of the trades was pinned flat against the top edge, which read as a gentle plateau just above 100 when the real shape is a climb to more than four times the net followed by handing three quarters of it back.

The axis now follows the curve, and the high point gets its own labelled line marked every winner banked. That height is the finding, not decoration: the gap between it and the 100 per cent line is the losing side of the book, drawn to scale for the first time.

THE 2B REACH-VERSUS-HEAT SCATTER WAS PAIRING TRADES AT RANDOM (owner: just check to make sure this is right on the 2B charts). It was not. When a run is too big for the database, the save step thins the list of trade profits down to 400 - but it never thinned the matching list of how far each trade ran for and against you, which stayed at 600. The chart then read them side by side, so the dot in position 50 showed one trade money against a completely different trade reach and heat. On run 384 that is 400 of the 864 dots. The run own saved won-or-lost flag proves it: it disagreed with the sign of the profit on 34 per cent of those trades, against 0 per cent on the lockbox trades, which were short enough that the save step left them alone. Those dots are now left OFF the scatter with a note saying how many and why, rather than drawn as trades that never existed. The points-versus-profit chart beside it was never affected - it uses no pairing - and its dots were all real.

THE SAVE STEP NO LONGER CAUSES IT. Profits and their reach-and-heat figures are thinned together now, by one shared set of positions, so position 50 stays one trade. Runs saved before today cannot be repaired - which trade each surviving profit came from is not recoverable - so re-validate anything you want the full scatter for.

THE CONCENTRATION LINE UNDER BOTH 2B CHARTS WAS DIVIDING BY THE WRONG TOTAL. It measured the biggest winners against the saved sample own total instead of the run total, which on run 384 made it print top 5 equals 105 per cent of net and without the top 5 minus 5,096 dollars. The run real answers are 24 per cent and plus 451,840 dollars. The shares now divide by the run own full net and carry a greater-than-or-equal sign so they read as the floor they are, and the without-the-top-5 figure is only printed when it is exact.

The concentration card had the same wrong total waiting in its fallback - it used the selection stretch, 254,001 dollars, where the run whole-window net is 596,112. You never saw it because the card reads the real trade list whenever it can get one, but it would have shown through on any run whose trade list was unavailable.

EVERY LINE THAT GOES THROUGH IS NOW THE SAME CONTRAST (owner, twice: I just want the current lines that do go through to be the same contrast - it didnt take effect). The previous attempt stopped the extra variants of a family from stepping darker, which was a real ramp but not the one on screen. Six different strengths were in play among the lines that run the full width of the funnel: the surviving configurations were drawn at just over half strength, the in-sample best at 95 per cent, the crowned line at full, the lockbox tails at 95, the gate at 95, and the tilt, KEEL and hybrid lines at 90. They are all at full strength now, and the five family lines share one thickness so no family reads as more important than another. Colours are untouched - they say which family a line belongs to and that meaning stays.

THE FAINT CLOUD IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED. Those configurations stop at the in-sample door and never reach the walk-forward; being faint is what tells you that, so making them match would hide the one thing the funnel exists to show.

The expanded funnel had a second ramp of its own - the runner-up configurations stepped progressively paler and less saturated so the champion stayed the deepest line. That is the same ramp in colour rather than strength, so it is flat now too. You still tell those lines apart by their label and by hovering, exactly as with every other line on the chart.

NOISE ROUND 54 - THE FORWARD-TESTING RANKING (owner: look at the noise configs ran thus and the compare scatter plots, give me a ranking for what you think is most worthy of forward testing). Thirty-five NOISE runs are on the board. Reading the scatter cloud each one searched, rather than the row it reported, changed two answers.

WHAT ONLY THE CLOUD SHOWS. The live crown sits at the 80th percentile of its own 495 configurations - it is not the peak, which is the shape you want because the plateau test picked it rather than the maximum. Every other candidate sits at the 87th to 100th. The 2-minute card has the thinnest cloud measured, only 64 percent of its neighbours making money at all against 100 percent for the 5-minute rows. And the resampling strip says the two compression legs had a drawdown shallower than 94 to 98 percent of their own reshuffled paths, so their headline risk figure is path luck as much as edge.

THE FINDING - THE COMPRESSION TILT BELONGS ON THE RETIRED BASE. The validated tilt, and both deployed paper legs, pin lookback 44 and volatility skip 90 - which is the crown the family retired on 2026-09-05. Re-basing it onto the live crown looked like an obvious fix and the battery says it is the wrong one: identical harness and identical null, the tilt PASSES on the retired base with drawdown growing 6 percent and zero of 2000 shifts matching, and FAILS on the live crown with sealed-year drawdown growing 17.9 percent against a 10 percent tolerance. It is real on both - it beats its own flat-leverage control everywhere - it just costs more risk on the newer base, which loosened the volatility skip and so takes about 400 more trades in noisier conditions. The deployed legs are not stale by mistake; they are on the base where the tilt passes.

THE RANKING. First the live crown raw, still unbeaten across eight swept spaces and the only row off the peak of its own cloud. Second the retired base with the tilt at 1.5x, already forward-testing and the only add-on that clears the whole battery. Third the live crown with the same tilt, the most money and the best risk-adjusted return measured but failing the drawdown clause, now queued for the house verdict with the tilt switched off inside its own admissible set as the parity control. Fourth the 2-minute card at small size for the diversification. Nothing else earns a slot.

THE GATE ROWS ARE BACK ON THE CHART (owner: why are there only 600 shown, fix it). All 600 missing rows were gate rows - every gate row on the board - and they were missing on purpose: the code reported no walk-forward figure for a gate at all, on the note that a gate pools its tuning years and saves no separate slice. It does save one, and all 300 gate candidates loaded carry it - though a gate that genuinely saved none still has nothing to show on that stage, and says so rather than guessing. With the stage rail on WALK-FORWARD a gate therefore had no profit, and with no profit there is no MAR and no return on capital, so nothing to plot and two dashes in the table.

The split is the engine own, not a reconstruction: in-sample plus walk-forward add up to the pooled pre-lockbox figure to the dollar on every case checked, and pre-lockbox plus lockbox add up to the whole. It is taken both halves or neither, so the stages can never sum to more than the pooled figure they came from.

THE IN-SAMPLE COLUMN FOR A GATE ROW WAS THE TUNING YEARS POOLED, which is in-sample PLUS walk-forward money under an IN-SAMPLE heading. The pooled figure is exactly the two halves added together - checked to the dollar on twelve gate candidates across four runs - so with the stage rail on IN-SAMPLE alone a gate row read high by its whole walk-forward profit. It now shows the in-sample slice there. Ticking IN-SAMPLE and WALK-FORWARD together gives the same total as before, because the two halves add back up to the pooled figure.

RETRACTION - the reason shipped one version ago was wrong. It said these rows came from runs validated before the engine wrote Sharpe and Sortino onto every configuration. That cannot be it: the count was exactly the same on every run including the newest, and the rows were not short of Sharpe or Sortino at all - they had both. The board sentence no longer blames the age of a run, and points at the stage rail instead.

RUNS IS DRAWN ONCE (owner: why are there duplicates for run). It was in the FILTERS sheet and in the row of controls I had pulled out into plain sight, so it rendered twice. It belongs in plain sight, because it decides which runs the configurations are read out of, and the copy in the sheet is gone.

THE ROWS-NOT-ON-THIS-CHART LINE NOW SAYS WHY (owner: why are there only 600 shown, fix it). It said what was missing and never what caused it, so it read like a fault in the board. It is not one: the engine only began writing Sharpe and Sortino onto every 1E configuration at a certain point, and runs validated before that leave those two fields empty for good. The line says that, says a re-validate fills them in, and names an axis pair that plots every one of those rows today.

A filter with nothing ticked now reads ALL on its menu rather than a bare dash. Three of the new menus showed a dash because nothing in them is set - accurate, but it says nothing, and putting what is set on the face of the control was the entire point of the change.

THE CONTROLS ARE MENUS NOW, LAID ACROSS (owner: so much space with all of these, and I get lost with things not being viewed). Each group shows one closed menu with whatever is set, and they sit in a wrapping row instead of a tall stack - so what is ON is always on screen and nothing scrolls out of sight.

Nothing about what the controls DO changed. The real buttons are still in the page, hidden, and the menu clicks the one you pick, so every handler, preference and tooltip is the one that was already there. That also means a control cannot drift out of step with the board.

A group where several things can be on at once - the run ticks, the 1E families, the verdicts - keeps its chips, because a closed menu cannot show three answers at once. Those now say how many of them are set.

EVERY NUMBER COLUMN CAN ORDER THE TABLE (owner: cannot rank by any of these). Five of the headings were clickable and the rest were not, with nothing on screen saying which was which - so expectancy in R, R per year, return on capital, dollars per trade and the trade count all looked sortable and were not. They are now, and every sortable heading says so on hover.
Drawdown sorts SMALLEST first, because a smaller one is the better result. Sorting it like a score would have put the worst rows at the top under a heading that reads like a ranking.
A row that records nothing for the column you picked still sits at the bottom rather than being given a place it did not earn.

PLAIN DOTS, AND THEY ARE THE DEFAULT (owner: the scatter was dots before). A verdict shape per point is readable at twenty points and a wall of icons at eight hundred, which is what this chart usually holds. Colour still carries the verdict either way, and SHAPES is one click away for a sparse chart or for anyone who reads shape faster than colour.

EVIDENCE and SHOW ARE BACK IN PLAIN SIGHT, and this answers three things at once - why the table looked like it only had raw configurations, how to put every 1E configuration of one strategy on the chart, and where KEEL went. Those two controls decide what kind of thing the board is showing: SWEEPS are study-registry rows, where RAW is the only family there is, and the 1E families - GATE, TILT, HYBRID and KEEL - only exist once the level is AUTO VAL with 1E CONFIGS showing. Burying them behind FILTERS made a whole half of the board look missing.

THE NOT-ON-THIS-CHART LINE NOW SAYS WHAT TO DO. When a large share of the rows record nothing for the axes you picked, it names a pair they do carry - money and profit factor - instead of only reporting the loss. Those are mostly older sweep rows that predate expectancy in R being on the board at all.

THE SPLIT TOGGLE IS BACK and it splits. The structure is the old board own, verbatim, minus the sidebar it used to sit beside. It only appears when the tables are actually on, because with them off there is nothing to put beside the chart - which was the real reason my earlier attempts collapsed a column to nothing.

THE TAB STRIP STOPS JUMPING (owner: clicking compare or runboard changes the layout of the subtabs). Two different builders were drawing the same navigation - the tab own screens used one, the views borrowed from the old tab used another with its own inline styles - so the row changed height and the page shifted under the cursor. There is one builder now, and the tab stylesheet is emitted wherever that strip renders.

EXPLORE SPLIT VIEW WORKS AGAIN (owner: it does not work). When the sidebar came off that screen the chart-beside-tables layout went with it, but the toggle in the top bar was left pointing at it. SIDE now puts the chart and the tables in two columns and STACK keeps them one above the other, as before.

KEEL HAS ITS OWN COLOUR ON THE SCATTER (owner: do the keels show up on explore). They always did - the engine writes a KEEL row beside the tilts and it plots like any other family - but the family palette had six entries and KEEL was not one of them, so on the one view where colour IS the family its points borrowed the verdict colour and it never appeared in the key. THE PICKED-RUN TABS AND SAVED SETS ARE ON THE COMPARE OVERLAY. A TABS + SETS button next to CLEAR opens a panel with the numbered tabs and every set you have saved: switch tabs, open a new one, close one, load a set, rename it, delete it, or save what is on screen as a new set. Switching a tab writes the runs on screen into the tab you are leaving first, so nothing is lost, and the last tab cannot be closed. They read and write the same stored lists the PICK RUNS view uses, so a set saved on either screen is there on the other. Under CHAMPIONS the panel is gone entirely and one line says why: that list is chosen for you and refills itself, so there is nothing to keep.

THE BUTTON THAT STARTS A BOOK RUN IS NOW ON THE BOOKS VIEW. It used to sit only on the RUNBOARD, with a line here pointing at it; that line is gone and the button is here. It is the same button and the same panel - the leg list, the from and to dates, the lockbox months, the name, the shared-window readout and the queue button are unchanged, and it queues exactly the same job it always did. A short line beside it says that pressing it puts real work on your PC.

BY STRATEGY IS ABSORBED. That view was one curve per family with its champion chosen for you, which is a SOURCE of runs rather than a screen - so the COMPARE overlay gained a SHOW switch: PICKED, which is what it has always done, or CHAMPIONS, which fills itself with the best run of every strategy. The old view comes off the strip.

The champion rule is now written ONCE and read by both screens. It used to live inside the leaderboard, and copying it would have repeated the mistake this rebuild has already had to fix three times: one rule in two places drifts, and then two screens disagree about which run is a family best.

In CHAMPIONS the chips lose their remove buttons and the CLEAR control disappears, because there is nothing to remove - the list fills itself. The note says how the choice was made and how to take it back.

TOP RUNS on the LEADERBOARD, and the last of the old runboard list. That list showed the same rows the leaderboard already shows once a family is opened, minus three things - so those three were added rather than a second list built: the strategy colour, so a run is findable by eye; the family run number the studies board and the notes call it by; and the robustness score.

The genuinely missing half was the panel of INDIVIDUAL runs, and it is the more useful one. The leaderboard only ever shows champions; this ranks every run in every family on whatever is picked above, so the best run of a family that never won anything is one click away - and so is the WORST, which is usually the more informative click. NEWEST ignores the ranking and just lists the ten latest.

It reaches runs the champion list leaves out for having a window under two years. They are shown with a warning and their length rather than dropped, because a short sample is a caveat, not a disqualification.

Every read this screen ranks on - R per year, MAR, profit factor, net - is better when it is larger, so BEST and WORST really are the two ends of one sorted list. A smaller-is-better read would need a direction flag, and there is a note in the code saying so.

COMPARE: the BOOKS table is now a view of its own on the new COMPARE screen, drawn there directly instead of being borrowed from the old tab. Pick BOOKS on the view strip. Every real book run in your history is listed first, newest first, then the four older offline rows a script worked out and someone pasted in. Clicking a live row opens that run report.

The STAGE control drives the table: the whole window, the tuning years, or the sealed lockbox. Every figure on a row comes from that ONE pooled stretch, so the net, the profit factor, the drawdown and the trade count always describe the same piece of history. Return over drawdown in this table is plain net divided by the worst drawdown of that stretch, with no years in it - the same number the old table printed, so the column stays comparable top to bottom.

A book pools its legs over one window and tunes nothing, so it has no walk-forward stage. Picking the walk-forward stage now says that in a sentence and offers the other three, instead of drawing a table full of blank cells.

The two look-ahead warnings still travel with the rows that earned them, and the button that starts a new book run is deliberately not duplicated here - the table points at the RUNBOARD view, where it lives.

BOOKS: the day-stamping rule is now a decision you can see rather than a note in a document. A trade calendar day has two defensible answers. The engine truncates a New York index, which numpy does in Universal Time, so a 24-hour leg exiting at or after 8pm New York books on the NEXT day; the other answer is the session day you would write on the ticket. The money is IDENTICAL under both - only the daily curve moves - but drawdown is measured on the daily curve, so the two can disagree about which month holds a book worst stretch. On the house baseline they do: 34,329 dollars in May 2022 against 34,903 in February and March 2020.

Every book run now scores BOTH and stores them, and the BOOKS row prints the second reading beside the first whenever they differ - which is never for a book that only trades the day session. NOTHING WAS CHANGED: every stored figure is still the engine rule, because switching it would move the recorded drawdown of every book at once and make old and new runs incomparable. Adopting the other rule is a re-scoring of every stored book, not a patch. The point is that the choice is now in front of you instead of in a file.

THE RUNBOARD MATRIX IS ABSORBED. A FULL stage joins in-sample, walk-forward and lockbox, so a run can be read end to end in one column - something the old board could do and this screen could not. Its net comes off the saved curve endpoint the way the run report reads it, and a book reads the whole-run block the engine pooled for it rather than its pre-lockbox figure. Its profit factor is pooled from the three stages with the in-sample part taken as the RESIDUAL - total minus walk-forward minus lockbox - because the in-sample champion figure overlaps the fold windows and pooling it directly double-counts. That is how the run report and the old board both do it, and the three parts now sum to the net printed above them.

The shading follows the board rule: a run is coloured by where it PLACES in its row, not by how far its number is from the others, so one runaway figure cannot wash the rest of the row flat. It has its own button.

Three rows are honest about not following the stage control, and say so under the table: robustness and the verdict describe the whole run whatever is picked, and folds held is always the walk-forward. A drawdown measured off the saved curve still carries its tilde and still never wins its row.

KEEL v12 - HALF SIZE BEFORE THE FED SPEAKS. Every earlier round searched the same features harder and found nothing: about 175 candidates across seven directions, none of them beating v11. Trades entered on a decision day BEFORE the 2pm Eastern statement are the worst bucket found anywhere in this work: expectancy of minus 0.48 and minus 0.43 R on the two NOISE runs against a plus 0.31 and plus 0.28 baseline, losing in the in-sample stretch, the walk-forward AND the lockbox on both runs, and losing in 8 of 9 walk-forward years on both. Against 4,000 random calendars of the same size the real one lands in the bottom tenth of one percent. Three placebos all lose money as they must - the morning before a decision day, a random matched day-set, and an every-morning shrink of the same dollar size - so the rule is keyed to the events and not to mornings. Half size, never a cut.

On top of v11 it is better on all four stretches with drawdown never worse on any of them: paper run walk-forward $532,380 against $523,760 at identical drawdown and lockbox $90,740 against $86,080 at slightly better drawdown; crown walk-forward $497,200 against $490,620 at better drawdown and lockbox $144,260 against $139,020 at identical drawdown. Stated against itself: the pre-registered story was backwards - the 2pm shock was supposed to be the bad half and it is the better half - so the split is after the fact, which is what the permutation test and the placebos are there to price.

The hole is not a NOISE quirk. The same bucket is negative on the ORB breakout crown and on the ENGU-Q continuation crown, which share nothing with NOISE but the tape, so the tilt is also available without the model for those legs.

Runner: the Firestore read meter was blind to idle polling. Firestore bills a minimum of one document read per query even when it returns nothing, and every [reads] site counted returned docs, so a quiet runner reported 0 reads/min while the 5-second commands poll on the primary alone cost about 17,000 reads a day and four workers another 11,500 - about 58% of the 50k Spark quota, invisible. Fix: every metered query counts at least one read; drain-only workers no longer start the commands thread at all (it only ever served chart lookups - job control lives in the main loop they still run); the commands thread on the primary is now a Firestore listener with a 10-minute backstop poll instead of a flat 5-second timer; the NT heartbeat and paper end-of-day reads are metered under other. Idle floor is now a few hundred reads a day across all five processes. Tests: tests/test_runner_quota.py (+8).

tools/queue_guard.py and tools/continuous_lb_check.py now resolve the params of a leg the way the runner does: any key you do not pass comes from the DEFAULT_PARAMS of the strategy file default, never from the Python function signature. A JOB THAT WAS RUNNING WAS INVISIBLE. The queue chip at the top said 5 WAITING with nothing running, and BUILDER agreed, while the runner was 29 percent of the way through ENGUQ_1M_ETH_ERW_1_0 and eight more jobs were stacked behind it. The web was reading the newest twelve job records BY QUEUED DATE; the runner claims the OLDEST waiting job first. Those two orders point opposite ways, so the running job - requeued a day earlier, and therefore old - had fallen out of the window, and so had three of the waiting jobs. A ninth job queued by a script carried no queued-at date at all, so a date-ordered read could never have shown it under any window size.

THE FIX READS UNFINISHED WORK BY STATUS INSTEAD OF BY DATE, so every queued, running or paused job appears no matter how old it is and no matter whether it carries a date. The finished list is still the newest twelve, fetched once and re-fetched the moment a job leaves the live set. That is still ONE live connection, not two - the runner writes a progress figure about every one and a half seconds and each connection is charged a read for every one of them, so the daily read budget only stretches to one.

THE CHIP AND THE TAB NOW READ THE SAME COUNT, from one shared piece of code, so they cannot drift apart again. The chip reads QUEUE, then the strategy name, then its percent, then plus how many are behind it.

A WAITING JOB WITH NO QUEUED-AT DATE SAYS SO rather than being hidden or guessed at: it is listed last, marked in amber as no timestamp, and its hover explains that its real place in the line is held in a field only the runner can read.

COMPARE FOR - one click sets BOTH scatter axes to the pair that answers one question, because the PAIRING is the part that is easy to get wrong. EDGE = expectancy in R against R per year, the ranking pair. RISK = expectancy in R against DRAWDOWN IN R, reward and risk in the SAME unit so size cannot flatter either, and upper LEFT is the good corner. QUALITY = Sortino against expectancy in R, which asks whether the edge arrived smoothly or in a few lucky jumps. MONEY = profit against drawdown percent, the reporting pair rather than the picking pair. Both pickers still work on their own underneath.

RATIO HEALTH opens from the calibration text in the header (it turns red with a warning triangle the moment the ratio drifts) into a small panel: current ratio, its age, a sparkline against its normal band, and the drift in plain English - every shadow price is an NQ price divided by this one number, so a stale ratio quietly mis-sizes every fill.
All three degrade cleanly on a doc published before this shipped: dashes instead of blanks, never "undefined" or "NaN".
FIXED: the WORST figure on the rail was hardcoded red even on a book with no losing trade yet; BEST and WORST now colour by their actual sign.

FIXED: the WEBULL PAPER ACCOUNT button linked to an always-empty $100,000 paper account the owner had already opened twice expecting real numbers. It is now a plain sentence: not used, nothing is ever sent there, this book is the paper record.

A RUN ROW NOW READS ITS REAL LOCKBOX. Ticking LB moved a run MONEY but left PF, WIN %, SHARPE, SORTINO and the trade count at whole-run values - so EV R and R / YR came out as lockbox dollars divided by the WHOLE RUN trades and average loss. A hybrid of two stretches printed as one number, and it was the number being used to decide what to trade. Run #304 read PF 1.43 / SORTINO 2.95 / 4,833 trades on every stage; its saved lockbox block says PF 1.45 / SORTINO 3.20 / 409 trades.

IS and WF are left alone deliberately: a run saves no equivalent block for either (validate.is_* is the Stage-A 75% split, a different stretch, and walk-forward saves only its net), so they keep reading whole-run rather than being guessed at. The CONFIGS view has had real per-stage blocks since 73.474.
DD (R) confirmed on both scatter axes, and its caption reads further LEFT is better - the first measure on this board where lower wins.

THE NOISE CROWN MOVES FROM RUN #243 TO RUN #304, on the owner call. #243 was a PINNED single-config validate - one configuration, so no landscape, no PBO, no parallel plot and no neighbourhood to check. #304 is the open re-run of the same idea over the same window (495 configurations, PASS 8 of 8, PBO 0.135) and it is simply the better book: total $413,255 against $380,745, and a LOCKBOX of $82,123 against $40,648 - more than double, on the years the search never saw.

THE LOCKBOX AGREES INDEPENDENTLY. Across 634 NOISE configurations from 13 runs, #304 takes 15 of the top 30 places on expectancy in R and R per year, and its RAW, GATE, TILT and both HYBRID sizings all land within 0.01R of each other out of sample - a plateau, not a peak. THREE MEASURES FROM THE 1E MATRIX JOIN BOTH SCATTER AXES: ROC % / YR, DD %, and DD (R) - the drawdown in average losing trades, the same unit EV R uses, so risk and reward finally speak one language on the two axes.

Reviewed before shipping and held back three times: the crown row would have mixed two runs figures, it would have labelled the former crown an archived duplicate, and DD as a vertical axis would have ranked the WORST drawdown first while the caption called it the good end. STUDIES BOARD: ROUND 30 - the R / YR CEILING OF EVERY FAMILY, rows 1253 to 1257, all measured with the identical objective search so they read against each other. NOISE is the frequency family (ceiling R / YR 103 at 368 trades a year). The ENGU-Q efficiency variant is the edge family (ceiling EV R 1.40, the library record, at 55 trades a year). The BASE ENGU-Q family - the one on paper - tops out at EV R 0.45, so the efficiency variant is a better family and not one lucky configuration. ORB is the floor: 400 configurations, nothing past R / YR 21. TTM Squeeze confirms closed at 12.
WHY IT MATTERS: the two ceilings sit in DIFFERENT families, which is exactly why pooling them beat every book measured - and why pooling two legs from the same family would not have.

ROC % is now ROC % / YR - net per YEAR against the fixed account, annualised the same way MAR and R / YR already are, so a 16-year run and a 3-year run can sit on the same axis. A configuration with no year count prints a dash rather than a whole-run figure wearing a per-year label.
DD % stays absolute on purpose and its hover now says why: a drawdown is a single worst event, not a rate, so it cannot be annualised. It is the half of a leverage decision the ratios hide.

STUDIES BOARD: ROUND 29 - the frontier legs go into the book, rows 1246 to 1252. AND THE LIMITS: adding the ORB crown DILUTES it (R / YR 240 to 189, EV R 0.57 to 0.32) because ORB has the lowest edge per trade in the library - an R / YR search over 400 ORB configurations could not pass 21. ALL and NONE on the RUNS row: tick every run the picked strategy is offering in one click, instead of fourteen clicks to see one strategy whole 1E landscape. THOSE DIAGONAL STREAKS ARE NOT DUPLICATES. Counted: 789 points, 789 distinct configurations, none repeated. Reviewed before shipping, and the review stopped it: that count was assembled BEFORE the chart that produces it, so it showed the previous render figures under a tooltip promising it followed the axes ticked now, and it stayed on screen on the parallel, radar and lattice charts, which do not place rows that way. THE BOARD AND THE RUN REPORT DISAGREED ON THE SAME CONFIGURATION, and the board was wrong. A CONFIGURATION ROW NOW READS THE SAVED BLOCK FOR THE TICKED STRETCH, the same one the 1E matrix reads - is_rng, wf_rng, lockbox, and the pre / full / wf_lb combinations, each carrying its own profit factor, win rate, Sharpe, Sortino, trade count and drawdown, written by the engine from that stretch real trades. AND ITS YEARS ARE THE TICKED STRETCH TOO - anything divided by years (PER YEAR, MAR, R / YR) was dividing a walk-forward slice by the whole run length.

R / YR IS ON THE BOARD: a column beside EV R, and an option on both scatter axes. EV R multiplied by trades per year over the ticked stretch - the cross-strategy rank read, leverage-blind like EV R but rewarding a strategy for trading often enough to compound its edge.

Reviewed before shipping, and the review stopped it: RAW rows would have blanked their whole ratio block on the default view, the trade count would have quietly borrowed the run whole-run number, the stretch marks were read from a path that does not exist so the years fix never ran, and R / YR up the side rendered as dollars. All four fixed before the push.

FOUR NEW STUDIES ON COMPARE - STUDIES (rows 1185-1240), round 6 of the hunt, every family scored on the two cross-strategy reads: EV R (expectancy in units of the average losing trade) and R / YR (EV R x trades per year). NOISE: the crown with lookback 44 to 51 beats it on all four legs (EV R 0.254, R / YR 68.4, lockbox 52,823, worst year -2,911); queued as NOISE_1_1_LB51.py. QQQ PAPER tab redesigned as QQQ SHADOW BOOK, the shadow-fills book (api/qqq_exec.py) leads the tab now instead of being tacked above the old content. One REFRESH control now reloads both Firestore docs together.

api/qqq_exec.py now publishes trades_all (every closed shadow trade since inception, capped at 500) and cum_pnl (per-leg and total cumulative P&L by date) on every tick, plus live_from and a per-leg unrealized figure on open positions, so the new equity curve and since-start KPIs have real data instead of only the last 100 rows. tools/qqq_exec_smoke.py: ALL PASS.

MAR IS ANNUALISED NOW - same label, new meaning, everywhere it appears (1E every tab, KPI, Past Runs, STUDIES, COMPARE, RUNBOARD): net over the ticked stretch PER YEAR of that stretch, divided by its max drawdown. The old net-over-drawdown grew with the length of the window - measured on the ORB crown with every knob pinned, an 8-year and a 4-year window with the SAME worst drawdown read 6.91 and 4.37, and the 16-year figure beat the 4-year one while PF, EV R, Sharpe and Sortino all said the recent years were better. Inside one run nothing re-ranks: every column shares the years, so the crown floor and every RANK order are unchanged. Only cross-run reads change, which is the point.

NEW ROW ON EVERY 1E TAB AND KPI, NEW AXIS ON THE CHARTS AND STUDIES: R / YR = EV R times trades per year on the ticked stretch - the edge, in units of the average losing trade, a config earns in a year. Leverage-blind and window-length-blind, so it is the number to rank strategies on across families. What Gemini calls opportunity-adjusted expectancy or daily R velocity, under ONE name, per year, beside the $ / YEAR axis it is the size-blind twin of.

NEW ROW: DD (R) = the drawdown over the ticked stretch divided by the average losing trade - how many typical losses deep the worst stretch went. Scale-free, so it reads across instruments and contract sizes. Lower is better.

THE ENGINE NOW WRITES, on every validate, the calendar date the optimize window splits into in-sample and walk-forward, plus the dates, years, average loss and per-trade Sharpe / Sortino of every IS / WF / lockbox block a config carries. So an IS-only or WF-only tick annualises exactly on a new run; on an older run those two ticks dash rather than guess, while IS+WF, LB and the full run annualise off the windows every run already stores.

ONE SORTINO. The GATE / TILT / HYBRID blocks used to carry their own Sortino arithmetic (sample deviation, downside about the mean) while sweeps and validates used another, and the RAW tab read a third off a sampled curve. Every block now comes through the single definition in analytics.py; RAW reads the stored per-stretch figure when a run has one and only falls back to the curve on older runs.
The KPI tab $100k-account MAR (ann.) row is gone: with MAR itself annualised there is one MAR, not two, and that one needs no account-size assumption.

NEW: QQQ SHADOW execution adapter (api/qqq_exec.py) - Stage 1 of trading the crowned NQ strategies as QQQ shares on Webull. SHADOW ONLY, no order is ever sent anywhere: it mirrors NinjaTrader's live NQ fills (fills.csv, the same feed the real-money journal sync reads) into paper QQQ share lots, one per leg (ORB / ENGU-Q / NOISE). Priced off a real Webull quote when fresh, else an NQ:QQQ ratio calibrated daily from Yahoo data. Rails: per-leg share cap, a daily shadow-loss breaker that flattens everything, an entry window with a forced flat-by, a kill file, and a feed-staleness guard - every trip pushed to the phone. Runs on its own runner thread, ticking every ~5s during market hours. QQQ PAPER tab gets a new SHADOW EXECUTION section above the existing content: status strip, one tile per leg, today's shadow orders, closed shadow trades with running P&L, and the rails in force.
tools/qqq_exec_smoke.py: synthetic-fills unit test covering a partial+full exit round-trip, an EOD-flattened leg, a refused late entry, and a breaker trip - all passing.

NEW 1E MEASURES: ROC % and DD % - net profit and worst drawdown as a percentage of a FIXED account you set with the ACCT chip (25k to 1M). They are the only readings on the board that recycling can move: every ratio beside them divides money by something that scales with position size, so the leverage cancels and a recycled hybrid reads exactly like its parent. Available on the scatter, both parallel views and the ALL table.

ROC % ranks in the same order as NET $ by construction - it is a constant divided into it. It is there to make a sizing decision concrete against a real account, and it sits beside DD % on purpose: recycling multiplies the drawdown by exactly the factor it multiplies the profit by.

1E SCATTER: a point that lands exactly where another already sits is drawn as an open RING around it instead of painting over it, and the header says how many did. HYBRID looked missing because all five of its dots sat under the recycled hybrids - on ratio axes a recycled hybrid IS its parent, since recycling scales the money and the drawdown by the same factor.

1A funnel with ALL CONFIGS on is readable again: the raw cloud draws as a faint haze (it was fusing into a solid green wedge), survivors sit a step quieter than the family top line, and the gutter no longer stacks a lock pill for every survivor - crown and family tops only.
The pinned sub-tab strip re-measures the topbar after the web fonts load, so it sits flush under it (it was 2px short before the fonts arrived).

1E SCATTER CAN NOW PLOT EVERY FAMILY ON SHARPE AND SORTINO - on runs validated from this build on. The engine now writes those two scalars onto every GATE / TILT / HYBRID column at validate time, computed from each column real trade list over the same window and annualisation the RAW configs use, and the scatter and parallel views read them. Runs saved before this build never recorded them, so their ML columns still sit those axes out and the not-plotted warning keeps naming them - re-validate to fill them in.

1E SCATTER, driven end to end: the not-plotted warning now names WHICH families are missing the measure (e.g. no SORTINO - GATE 20 / TILT 10 / HYBRID 5 / HYBRID-R 5). An all-green chart on the ALL tab was the truth, not a bug: SORTINO and SHARPE come off a stored equity curve and only the RAW top-10 keep one - the ML columns record no curve, so those two axes can never plot them.

PBO is gone from the scatter axis pickers - it is one number for the whole run, so every dot landed on a single vertical line. It stays on the table and parallel views. And the second 1E card now picks its OWN scatter axes instead of being chained to the first cards X / Y.

Scatter and parallel charts fill their column again. They were remembering an absolute pixel height, so a height recorded while the tile was narrow pinned the chart small once the tile grew - it sat at two-thirds scale with dead margin down both sides and the re-fit could not override it.

What the handle remembers is now the share of the fit height, not a pixel count, so a chart you deliberately made small stays small and one left at full size keeps filling whatever width its column ends up.

Scatter and parallel charts now re-fit whenever their tile changes width, so they fill the column instead of sitting small with dead margin down both sides. The fit was being measured one frame after the build, before the report had settled its column widths.

Scatter and parallel charts FIT at every size now - the whole drawing is always on screen, centred, never clipped and never stretched. v73.407 sized them off their height so the handle could magnify them, which pushed the right-hand edge (dots and the x-axis title) off the side behind a sideways scrollbar.

The drag handle shrinks the chart and grows it back only as far as the point where it exactly fills the column width, so there is no empty space to drag into and no cropped edge to scroll to. Resizing the window or the tile re-fits them.

TWO NEW AXES ON THE 1E CHARTS: EV R and SORTINO (owner: "scatter plot options need ev in r and soritno since those seem to be the fairir yardstick"). Both are on the parallel view, the scatter and the axis pickers, on the all-configurations chart and on the phase chart, so one name means one thing on both.

EV R is expectancy measured in units of the average LOSING trade - the edge per bet with the contract size, the instrument and the account divided out, which is what makes two configurations on different markets readable against each other. The average loss is not recorded per configuration, so it is DERIVED rather than read - and exactly, not approximately: expectancy over average loss equals one minus the win rate, times profit factor minus one. That identity was checked against ten real runs using each one own stored average win, average loss and win rate, and matched to nine decimal places on every one. A configuration that has never lost has no R to measure by and draws no point rather than an infinity.

SORTINO charges a strategy for its DOWNSIDE only, so a run that simply moves a lot is no longer punished for moving upward. It is computed from each configuration own saved equity curve, using the same series, the same denominator and the same annualisation as the SHARPE axis beside it - one function, one flag - because two ratios drawn side by side have to be comparable or the comparison is the thing that misleads.

HONESTY NOTE ON THE CHART ITSELF: the curve-derived Sortino here reads HIGHER than the per-trade Sortino the phase chart and a STUDIES run row print, because a sampled curve hides intra-trade dips. The axis says so on hover. Compare configurations against each other on this chart; do not read one against the other chart number.

FIXED WHILE IN THERE: the Sharpe axis was pinned to the whole optimize window while profit factor, win rate and EV beside it followed the IS / WF / LOCKBOX tick - so a lockbox tick drew one whole-window number in a row of lockbox ones. Both risk ratios now follow the tick, and fall back to the whole-window figure only when the tick IS the whole window.

ALSO FIXED: the fallback that fills profit factor, win rate, trades and EV R for a configuration was reading a block that never exists, so those axes silently vanished on many runs - not only old ones, since the pooled profit factor is dropped whenever any ticked slice sits at or below 1. Some existing reports will now show axes that were previously missing.

NEW PRE-PUSH GATE, tools/matrix_axes_render_probe.py: renders both 1E charts headlessly over fourteen cases and checks the drawn numbers, including that EV R equals the hand calculation, that a configuration with no losing trade draws nothing, and that an axis only some configurations record still draws with its degree mark.
