THE AUTO-RECOVER SWITCH NOW LOOKS LIKE A SWITCH. It was a bordered pill in the exact costume of the read-only status lights beside it, so nothing said it was clickable. It now follows the page rule: a checkbox toggles. Checked box when on; hollow box plus OFF in amber when off; the only checkbox on the status strip - the one thing there you can click.

A RUN THAT VALIDATED ONE CONFIGURATION NOW POINTS AT THE RIGHT SIBLING, not merely the newest one. It prefers a run that says in its own note that it searched AROUND this configuration, then one measured over the same window and the same data, and it tells you which of the two it found. When all it can offer is a same-window sweep it says plainly that the population may not contain this exact configuration - because it searched the space, it did not aim at this point.

WHY THAT MATTERED, on the NOISE crown (owner: "check auto validate 243. its missing quite a lot of info"). Run 243 evaluated ONE configuration, so it has no plateau pick, no surrogate, no overfit probability and no deflated Sharpe - none of which can be back-filled, because one configuration has no landscape. Re-running it would change nothing: its strategy file is pinned, so it would evaluate one configuration again. The landscape already exists in run 304, a restricted re-search around the crown on the same window that holds the crowned configuration itself plus 69 of its immediate neighbours. The family full sweeps, runs 237 and 302, do NOT contain it - not exactly and not within one knob - so pointing there would have answered a different question in silence.
REPORT_COMPLETENESS.md carries the audit, and corrects its own earlier note that the NOISE crown needed no full-discovery run.

DENSE CHARTS DRAW SMALL DOTS (owner: the triangles and circles make things hard to read because there are so many of them). Past 250 points every mark becomes a small dot in its family colour, the crowned or chosen one a slightly larger dot with a white ring, and the status rings stand down - at that count a verdict shape carries nothing a colour does not. Under 250 points the shapes draw exactly as before. Reviewed pre-push; the review two notes - the hover ring scaling with the dot, and a dimmed champion ring fading with its fill - are folded in.
A GATE ROW COUNTED ITS PRE-LOCKBOX TRADES BUT ITS WHOLE-RUN MONEY, so every per-trade figure on a gate read a shade rich. The lockbox trades count now, matching the stretch the total covers.

FOUND ON THE DRIVE-THROUGH: the view rail on RANKINGS rendered but did nothing - its buttons were only ever wired inside the COMPARE branch, so rankings was a room you could enter and not leave. The rail works from there now.

THE 1E FAMILY COLOURS NOW MATCH THE RUN REPORT OWN KEY - RAW green, GATE red, TILT amber, HYBRID violet, recycle pink, exactly as the 1A/1E key paints them. Equal-DD takes teal, the one colour that key does not use. They were an invented palette before, which is why RAW read blue here and green everywhere else.
MARKS SHRINK ON A DENSE CHART - past 250 points everything scales down together, so 850 candidates stop being a wall of icons.

THE STRAY MARK SITTING ON THE AXIS WAS NOT A DATA POINT. Stacked duplicates fan out a few pixels each so they stay clickable; unbounded, the 30th duplicate of one busy pixel walked clean off the plot. The fan is capped at six and the result clamped inside the axes, labels included.
THE SIDEBAR IS ONE COLUMN ALWAYS. The auto-fitting grid re-solved its column count whenever a label width changed, so picking a study re-wrapped the controls under your cursor.
The RAN AS A VALIDATE RUN section row hugs the column headers instead of floating below them.
Reviewed by a second set of eyes before shipping; its two findings - labels stacking past the cap, and a stale comment - are folded in.
FIX on 73.421: the per-run accounting was declared inside the configs branch and read by the chart note outside it, so the CONFIGS view threw before drawing. Declared at the scope it is read from.

THE 1E CONFIGS SCATTER IS READABLE NOW, four fixes from one deep dive. First: every point was a washed-out grey triangle because config rows never declared their run number in the field SPLIT BY RUN reads - so the chart faded them all as never-run and their hovers said so. They are run-backed rows now, undimmed, and the run tag opens the report.

SECOND: ON THIS VIEW COLOUR IS THE 1E FAMILY, not the verdict - RAW blue, GATE red, TILT amber, HYBRID violet, recycle pink, equal-drawdown teal, with the legend swapped to match. A verdict colour is meaningless for candidates no lockbox has judged; which family a point belongs to is the thing worth seeing.

THIRD: IS / WF / LB SWITCH ON THIS VIEW NOW. The pin claimed a config record holds one window; wrong - the records carry per-stage slices (RAW its calendar split and lockbox end, GATE its own lockbox block, TILT and HYBRID is/wf/lockbox), so the stages are wired and the pin is gone. A record genuinely missing a stage shows the dash with the reason, as everywhere else.

FOURTH: EVERY TICKED RUN IS ACCOUNTED FOR under the chart - its point count, or STILL LOADING, or NO CONFIGURATION RECORDS with why on the hover. Eleven of the twenty-one NOISE runs are the last kind: validated before the engine saved per-config records, or pinned single-config runs. An empty contribution is never silent again.

A MONEY AXIS ROUNDED TO THOUSANDS IS USELESS WHEN THE NUMBERS ARE IN THE HUNDREDS. With EXPECTANCY PER TRADE up the side every tick read $0k and the axis carried no information at all. It prints whole dollars below a thousand, thousands above it, millions above that.

THE CONFIGS VIEW STOPS DOWNLOADING WHOLE RUN DOCUMENTS. Reading a run 1E candidates meant fetching its ENTIRE document - equity curves, trade excursions, gate bake-offs, megabytes of it - to get at two fields, which is the very thing the fast page load exists to avoid. It asks Firestore for only the parts it reads now, using the same field mask the runs list already uses. Kilobytes instead of megabytes.
It keeps its own small cache, so it never evicts a run report you have open, and if the projected read is refused it falls back to the whole document rather than leaving the view stuck on LOADING.

AND THE TAB NO LONGER LOCKS UP WHEN SEVERAL RUNS ARE TICKED. A run document is large - the fast page load exists precisely because fetching them all is about 25 megabytes - so asking for ten at once wedged the renderer while they landed. Three are fetched at a time now and the rest queue, so the board fills in progressively instead of freezing and then arriving all at once.

THE CHART SAT ON LOADING FOR EVER WHILE THE TABLE UNDER IT FILLED UP, and the reason is dull: the run-document cache holds EIGHT runs. Tick ten and it evicts one to load the next, so the test for everything-has-arrived could never come true. The cache now holds as many as are ticked.

AND THE CHART DRAWS WHAT IT HAS instead of being replaced wholesale by a LOADING panel. Ticking one more run used to blank everything already on screen; now the runs that have arrived stay drawn and a line underneath names the ones still coming.

FIX: LOAD ERROR - cannot access _reCfgFam before initialization. The new 1E FAMILY setting was declared next to its own buttons, hundreds of lines below the code that READS it, and a const is hoisted but not initialised - so the first read threw and took the tab down. It is declared above its first use now. Anyone whose board was left on the old CONFIGS level hit this immediately, because that pick is what switches the reading code on.

CONFIGS IS NO LONGER A SEPARATE LEVEL - it is a VIEW of the runs you have already ticked, which is what was asked for in the first place. Pick a strategy, tick one or more of its Auto-Validates, then SHOW decides whether the chart plots the RUNS themselves or every 1E candidate inside them, overlaid on the same axes.

THE STRATEGY PICK IS NO LONGER THROWN AWAY. Switching to configs used to repoint the rail at RAW / GATE / TILT, so the NOISE you had picked simply vanished and there was no way to tell what you were looking at. The rail always means the strategy; the six 1E families have their own control.

AND THE RUN CHIPS OFFER ONLY THAT STRATEGY RUNS. Seventy-five chips while the rail said NOISE was most of what made this confusing - the pick looked ignored. Untick the rail and every run is offered again.

The profit stage still pins itself while the configs view is on, because a candidate record holds exactly one window - but you only meet that pin when you ask for candidates, not the moment you arrive.

The zoom handle on the scatter and parallel charts now actually zooms. It was pinning the chart to the tile width, so dragging past the fit height only added blank space; the chart is sized off its height instead, so dragging down magnifies the whole drawing - dots, labels and trend line together - and the tile scrolls sideways.
These charts open at their exact fit height, and they remember a dragged height under their own name so a height you set back when they were being stretched cannot reopen them wildly zoomed.

Aspect-locked charts (the scatters and parallel-coordinate views) have a drag handle again, and dragging it ZOOMS them: the whole drawing scales, text included, instead of the chart sitting at one size while the tile grows empty space underneath it. Nothing is stretched - the shape is kept at every size.

NUMBERS / RATIOS / BOTH no longer applies to the SCATTER, and the control is hidden while the scatter is up. The scatter names its own two measures, so the filter was pulling the axes out from under you whenever you switched it.

Scatters and parallel-coordinate charts keep their shape again. Report charts are stretched to fill their resizable tile, which is right for a line chart but wrong for these - a squashed scatter turns dots into ellipses and, worse, makes the fitted line look like a slope it was never fitted at.

The 1E scatter axis picker now shows how many configs actually record each measure, so picking one only the raw pool carries (SHARPE, on most runs) is an informed choice instead of a chart that empties out.

1E dropdown menus now open directly beneath the control that was clicked. They are fixed-position, and a fixed element is placed against the nearest transformed ancestor rather than the window - the report cards are one, so the menu was landing far from its button.

Follow-up: each 1E dropdown now finds its OWN menu by name. A wrapper can hold more than one popover, and the plain lookup was handing back whichever sat first in the page - so the menu skipped its anchoring step and opened at a stale position, well away from the button that was clicked.

THE CONFIGS SCATTER DREW NOTHING, and here is why: the board opens on SORTINO across the bottom and NOT ONE configuration row carried a Sortino, so every point was dropped for want of an x value. The rows themselves were fine - the table beside the chart was listing all 211 of them the whole time.

EVERY RECORD THAT SAVED AN EQUITY CURVE NOW CARRIES BOTH A SHARPE AND A SORTINO, derived from that curve the same honest way the run report derives them for its own candidates. A record that saved no curve stays blank, which is the truth rather than a fabricated number.

AND THE EMPTY-CHART MESSAGE NAMES THE AXES THAT ARE ACTUALLY EMPTY. It said a profit and a drawdown whatever the axes were set to, so picking SORTINO against EV IN R and getting nothing pointed at the wrong two figures entirely.

FIX: LOAD ERROR - _reCfgRunId is not defined. Making the CONFIGS level read several runs renamed a variable inside the per-run loop, and the rename swept up the DECLARATION as well, so the panel that says LOADING RUN read a name that no longer existed. Declared again; the loop keeps its own name.

The 1E control rails are one-word dropdowns now instead of rows of pills - view, columns and both scatter axis pickers. The axis pickers alone were nine pills each, which is what pushed the header off the edge of the card.
2B and 2C inherit the same compact control, so the whole report has one dropdown behaviour: click to open, one menu at a time, click anywhere else to close.

THE 1E MATRIX GOES ON THE SCATTER FOR SEVERAL AUTO-VALIDATES AT ONCE. The CONFIGS level read one run, which answered what a run found but never whether two runs found the same thing. The RUN control is a row of tickable chips now - tick as many as you like and every one of their RAW, GATE, TILT and three HYBRID candidates lands on the same axes.

EVERY POINT SAYS WHICH RUN IT CAME FROM. A row is named #304 GATE logistic at 50 percent, so a point is always traceable back to the run that produced it, and the family rail still narrows to RAW or GATE or any one hybrid sizing across all of them at once.
THE HONEST CAVEAT IS PRINTED when more than one run is ticked: the runs may cover different windows, so the ratio axes stay fair and NET does not.

Follow-up to 73.391: the second 1E card was still borrowing the first card view setting. The per-card context is set before the card body is built now, so KPI on one card and SCATTER on the other really do hold at the same time.

The two 1E cards are independent now. Each keeps its own TABLE / PARALLEL / SCATTER and NUMBERS / RATIOS / BOTH setting, so COMPARE can hold one card on the scatter and the other on the table instead of forcing both to show the same drawing.

1E header laid out properly: the tab strip keeps the title row and the drawing controls drop to their own row underneath. They were all competing for one line, which pushed the last tabs off the edge of the card.

FIXED: the TILT and HYBRID families were missing from the 1E SCATTER on the EV and TRADES axes. Their per-config block records the trade count as n, not kept, so both measures came out empty and every one of those points was dropped - leaving a chart of GATE dots that looked like the whole population.
The scatter never drops a point in silence now: an amber note says how many were not plotted and which measure they lack, so a thinned chart can never read as a complete one.

1E has a third view: SCATTER, on the same rail as TABLE and PARALLEL. It plots the SAME measures the parallel view uses - two pickers choose which goes across and which goes up, defaulting to MAX DD against NET $ - so the three views can never disagree, and the NUMBERS / RATIOS / BOTH selector filters the axis choices too.

On the KPI tab one point is a phase (IS / WF / LB / TOTAL); on a candidate tab one point is a config, coloured by family with the crowned one ringed in gold. Unlike the parallel view nothing is inverted - each axis runs in its natural direction and its caption says which end is good.

A run that validated ONE configuration now says which sibling run does carry the param curves, the PDP finder and the surfaces - it names the same-family run that searched a real population instead of just showing N/A. (A one-config run cannot draw them: there is no population to draw them from.)
The TABLE / PARALLEL switch leads the 1E control row now instead of trailing the tab strip.

The 1A funnel no longer picks its TILT and HYBRID line by LOCKBOX recovery factor. It now uses the same ticked SAMPLE slices and RANK rule as the 1E table - default pre-lockbox (IS+WF) ranked by NET $ with an 80% MAR floor - so the two panels cannot disagree and nothing is selected on the held-out year.

Measured before changing it across runs 234 / 243 / 302 / 303: the old lockbox rule disagreed with this one on 6 of 8 pools and picked xgb 4 times out of 5 - the model with the weakest walk-forward-to-lockbox relationship (on run 243 xgb reads lockbox MAR 0.09 against walk-forward MAR 11.57). The lockbox is now confirmation only.

THE SIDEBAR IS A PICKER NOW, NOT A DATA TABLE. The COLUMNS switch is gone and the strategy table is locked to the four key readings - thirteen columns could never fit a sidebar, which is where the cropped numbers came from. Everything beyond the key four is on the row hovers, where it always was.

TWO SHAPES, USED CONSISTENTLY, so you can tell what is clickable and how. A choice is a labelled tray - VIEW, FAMILY, TYPE, with the label inside the tray and the active cell solid - which also ends the two-ALLs confusion, because one now reads FAMILY-ALL and the other TYPE-ALL. A toggle is a checkbox line: baselines only, detail, archived. If it has a checkbox it toggles; if it is a tray you pick one.

THE FOOTNOTES UNDER THE TABLE ARE GONE - both wrapped into grey noise at sidebar width. The crown note is a tooltip on the STRATEGIES heading; INCLUDE ALL appears beside that heading only when something is excluded.

YOU CAN NOW TELL WHAT IS ON. Every active filter is inverted - solid fill, dark text - instead of the faint tint that was near-invisible on the monochrome theme, where the blue accent renders grey. Active toggle chips carry a check mark.
EVERY STRATEGY ROW HAS A CHECKBOX. Filled means included, hollow means excluded, and an excluded strategy is struck through as well as dimmed - three signals instead of a 40% opacity change.

THE SIDEBAR IS LABELLED. VIEW, FILTER, COLUMNS, then STRATEGIES with a live count - so each block says what it is instead of being anonymous rows of chips. The BASELINES tooltip now warns that it hides every ML overlay.

WHERE THE MLs WENT, ANSWERED ON THE BOARD. The ML legs were hidden by the RAW switch and by BASELINES ONLY - an ML overlay is never a baseline, so BASELINES ONLY hides every one of them, and picking ML with it still on showed a completely empty table with no explanation. The empty table now names the switch that is hiding everything and says what to click.

THE PARAM DUMP IS OFF THE DETAIL ROW. It printed every knob of the configuration inline; the row now shows only where the leg came from, and the knobs ride in the same hover tooltip as the run note - one hover away instead of three wrapped lines on screen.

THE PAPER SIDEBAR IS STARTED OVER. The old one crammed the wide-screen control strip into a narrow column, where its pills and hint sentences wrapped into a wall of blobs. The new one is built for a column: full-width rows for TODAY / ALL TIME, the families and RAW / ML, one row of equal chips for BASELINES, DETAIL and ARCHIVED, a labelled COLUMNS switch, then the strategy table - which was never the problem.

EVERY EXPLANATORY SENTENCE MOVED INTO HOVER TOOLTIPS. The how-to-click hint, the today-source note, the archived clause - hover the control that owns them. The panel shows controls and numbers, nothing else.
ONE PAPER TAB. The two paper tabs are merged: the tab bar now has a single PAPER, showing the sidebar layout. A browser that saved the old tab as its view is routed to the merged one.

THE SIDEBAR IS ONLY THE SELECTION PANEL now - the strategy table with TODAY / ALL TIME, the family buttons, RAW / ML, BASELINES ONLY, the column switch and archived. The duplicate pill rail and its title strip are gone from the page; they were the legacy top strip crushed into a narrow column, saying the same thing as the table under them. Everything on the right - status, chart, calendar, trades, the folded panels - follows the sidebar selection.

THE PAPER PLUS SIDEBAR NOW HOLDS THE STRATEGY TABLE ITSELF, not just the leg buttons. The previous version moved the wrong block: the table lives inside the chart tile, so the sidebar came up with only the pill rail in it while the table stayed down beside the chart. The chart tile is now split, and the original PAPER tab is unchanged - the strip still sits under the chart there.

The render gate now fails if the sidebar is missing OR if the strategy rows are not inside it. That check is what caught this: the tab rendered perfectly well with the wrong content in the column, and every existing gate passed.

PAPER PLUS NOW CARRIES THE LEGACY STRATEGY PANEL, and it lives in a SIDEBAR. The LEGS panel - TODAY / ALL TIME, the family buttons, RAW / ML, BASELINES ONLY, the column switch and the strategy table - was the one part of the old PAPER tab that never came across. It is now a sticky left column, so what you have selected stays on screen while the chart, calendar, trades and panels scroll past it.

DRAG THE DIVIDER to set how wide it is; double-click it to reset. The width is remembered, and clamped on load so a width saved on a big monitor cannot squeeze the board on a laptop. Under about 1080 pixels wide it stacks instead, exactly as the old tab laid out.

THE SCREEN NO LONGER JUMPS when you click a strategy on or off. Every re-render rebuilt the page from scratch and threw away where you were scrolled, so toggling a leg near the bottom snapped you back to the top. In-place updates - leg toggles, filters, sorting, opening a panel - now hold your position. Switching tabs still takes you to the top, as it should.

THE CALENDAR HAS A WEEK COLUMN. Each row ends with that week’s total, coloured like the days. Hover it for the trade count, how many days traded and the win rate. A week with no trades stays blank rather than showing a green zero - a week the board never traded is not a flat week.

THE AUTO-RECOVER SWITCH IS NOW ON THE PAPER PLUS STATUS LINE TOO. It shipped only inside the NINJATRADER card, which on PAPER PLUS is folded away behind NINJATRADER DETAIL - so on that tab you had to open an accordion to reach a switch whose whole purpose is a five-second decision. It now sits on the top status strip, next to the live and gate lights, on both tabs.

AUTO-RECOVER now has a button, on the NINJATRADER card in both paper tabs. It switches off the scheduled job on your PC that restarts NinjaTrader, logs it in, reconnects the Simulation account and re-enables the strategies. Useful on a weekday morning, pointless on a Saturday when the only thing it can do is reconnect a platform nobody is trading.

IT SHOWS THE PC’S REAL STATE, not what you last clicked - the status arrives in the same snapshot the NinjaTrader card already reads, so a change made on the machine itself shows up here too. If it cannot read the PC it says UNKNOWN rather than a confident OFF.

TURNING IT OFF DOES NOT STOP NINJATRADER. Anything already running keeps running and any enabled strategy keeps trading. All that stops is the automatic repair - so if NinjaTrader does die while it is off, nothing puts it back until you switch it on again. The button says so before it does anything.

SWITCHING LEVEL WITH A STRATEGY STILL PICKED NO LONGER EMPTIES THE BOARD IN SILENCE. A configuration row is tagged RAW or GATE or TILT, never NOISE, so arriving on CONFIGS with NOISE held on the rail filtered every row away and left a blank chart with no explanation. A filter that cannot match anything on the level you are looking at is now ignored; one that CAN match still applies exactly as before.

THE VERTICAL CAPTION WAS BEING SLICED BY THE TOP OF THE CHART. It is drawn rotated, so its length is bounded by the chart HEIGHT and nothing warned - EV read ...ores PROFIT STAGE and COMPARE ON. Every axis mode has a short caption now, and anything still too long is trimmed with the full sentence kept on the hover.
AND EV IN R, SHARPE AND SORTINO HAD NO CAPTION OF THEIR OWN - they fell through to the profit wording, which described a different axis entirely.

RAW / GATE / TILT / the three HYBRIDS are now one click each. On the CONFIGS level the strategy rail lists the six 1E families with a count each, and clicking one shows only that family - the toggle asked for, on the control that was already there.

THE CONFIGS LEVEL NOW CARRIES ALL SIX 1E FAMILIES, not four: RAW, GATE, TILT and the THREE hybrid sizings - one lot, redeploy and equal drawdown. A hybrid record is one configuration measured three ways, and the two sized-up views were missing.

THE SIZING FACTOR IS THE RUN OWN, the same arithmetic the 1E matrix uses: REDEPLOY spends the same total contracts as the no-gate book, EQUAL DD sizes until the worst drawdown matches it. Money scales; PF, WIN percent and EV in R are scale-free and do NOT move, which is exactly why they are the axes worth reading. Where the ungated twin is missing the factor is one and the column repeats the one-lot column rather than inventing a number.

RANKINGS IS OFF THE TOP-LEVEL NAV. It became one of the COMPARE views yesterday and was being offered in two places at once. The view itself is unchanged and still renders - the compare rail navigates to it - it just is not a primary tab as well.

SCATTER AND LATTICE COULD BOTH LOOK SELECTED. The SCATTER chip lit whenever the chart was not PARALLEL, so it stayed lit under RADAR and LATTICE too - two chips on at once in a control where exactly one can be true. It now lights only for its own drawing.
CHART IS THE FIRST CONTROL, above LEVEL. It decides which drawing everything under it is describing, so it leads.
STUDIES LEADS THE COMPARE RAIL now - it is the view that answers what has been tried, so it is the one to land on.

AND RANKINGS IS ONE OF THE VIEWS. It sat on its own top-level tab even though it is a comparison like the other four. The same rail now appears on it, so clicking any other view takes you straight back into COMPARE on that mode, and clicking RANKINGS from COMPARE goes the other way. Five views of one thing.

LATTICE, the fourth drawing: every measure against every other in small panes. It answers the one question the other three cannot - WHICH OF THESE MEASURES ARE SAYING THE SAME THING. A pane whose cloud lies on a line is two measures that move together, so reading both is reading one twice; a shapeless cloud is two that genuinely disagree, and those are the pairs worth judging a strategy on.

FIVE MEASURES, NOT TEN: Sharpe, Sortino, MAR, EV in R and profit factor. Ten would be a hundred panes at forty pixels each, which is a texture rather than a chart. All five are scale-free, so every pane is a fair comparison whatever the instrument, size or window.
Capped at 250 rows, strongest by MAR, with the number left off said out loud - twenty-five panes of every row would be tens of thousands of dots. Same rule the radar learned the hard way.

CRITICAL FIX: every run report has been failing to open since 73.367 with THIS RUN DETAIL COULDN-T RENDER (ReferenceError: _reXNm is not defined). The 1A RISK MAP x-axis caption had been pointed at the RANKINGS scatter axis-picker variables, which live in a different function. The RISK MAP x is always max drawdown, so its caption says that again.
TTM HAD NO FAMILY RULE, so every TTM Squeeze run read UNTAGGED and the strategy rail counted TTM as zero while three crowned TTM runs sat on the chart. It has one now.
AND THE RAIL COUNTS WHAT THE LEVEL ACTUALLY BUILT - crowned runs on CROWN, every run on AUTO VAL - instead of counting every run either way.

CROWN READS PAST RUNS NOW, like AUTO VAL. It listed registry rows tagged as champion, so a crowned run nobody had written up was absent, and a stale write-up outlived the crown it described. It is one row per CROWNED RUN, off the same Past Runs list, so it cannot go stale.

WHAT MAKES A RUN CROWNED IS YOUR OWN MARK, never a computed maximum. Two marks count: a starred run, and a run cited by a studies row you tagged as the champion of its family. A family with neither is simply absent - naming the biggest number would be inventing a crown nobody awarded, which is the one thing this level must not do.
Crowned rows fill every axis, like every other run row, and the strategy rail counts runs on this level too.

THE RADAR IS CAPPED AT TWELVE ROWS, and that is a fix rather than a limit. It draws a FILLED shape per row; at the ALL level that is a thousand semi-transparent ten-sided polygons stacked on each other, and compositing them froze the tab outright. It draws the strongest by NET and says how many it left off, instead of pretending to draw everything and delivering a locked page. Narrow the strategy or the level to see different ones.

RADAR, the third drawing. The same ten measures as the parallel chart, drawn as a closed loop. Read a radar for SHAPE - whether two rows are the same KIND of thing - and the parallel chart for VALUES.

ITS HONEST COST, said on the chart: ten measures in ten units cannot share one radius, so every spoke is scaled to the ROWS ON SCREEN - lowest near the middle, highest on the rim. A position there is relative, and changing the filter changes the shape. The figures are on the hover; the parallel chart prints them on its axes. A row that records fewer than three measures makes no shape and is counted underneath rather than faked.
THE RECOMMENDED MEASURE LEADS EACH AXIS LIST now - EV in R up the side, Sortino across the bottom.
VERTICAL AXIS and HORIZONTAL AXIS sit on one line instead of two.

The Y numbers are back on the left. They moved right for one version and the owner moved them back - correctly: the best rows sit toward the TOP RIGHT, so a scale over there sits on top of the answer.
THE TWO AXIS PICKERS SIT ON THE SCATTER ITSELF now, not in the sidebar. They are the chart own questions and nothing else on the page reads them.
AND THE BOARD OPENS ON THE COMPARABLE PAIR: Sortino across the bottom, EV in R up the side. It used to open on dollars, which do not survive different instruments, sizes or windows.

BOTH SCATTER AXES ARE YOURS NOW. A new HORIZONTAL AXIS control: DRAWDOWN, SORTINO, SHARPE, EV R or PF. Drawdown answers the original question well, but it is dollars - so it flatters a row that traded small and punishes one that ran long.

THE APPLES-TO-APPLES PAIR IS SORTINO ACROSS THE BOTTOM AGAINST EV IN R UP THE SIDE. EV in R is the edge on each bet with size and instrument divided out; Sortino is what a year of those bets delivered after the downside is charged for. Neither can be flattered by trading bigger or by running longer. It says so on the control.
VERTICAL AXIS gained EV R, SHARPE and SORTINO, and the old dollars-per-trade option is named EV, which is what it always was.
The Y numbers moved to the right - the side a price scale lives on.
LEVEL now leads the sidebar: which grade of evidence first, then which drawing, then which stretch of history, then which strategy.
The sidebar has its own faint tint, so it reads as a surface rather than as empty page beside the cards. It follows the theme colour, so it lands right on light, dark and monochrome.

THE DUPLICATE NOISE MARKS, chased down: NO run is listed twice. FIVE GROUPS of NOISE runs record byte-identical figures because the same configuration was validated more than once - 287 and 285, 254 and 242 and 231, 253 and 241, 252 and 243, 251 and 245. Nineteen NOISE runs, about twelve distinct results. They are different runs landing on exactly the same spot, so both marks and both numbers were drawn on top of each other.

Each extra mark at a point is nudged a few pixels now and its number stacked under the last, so every run stays readable and clickable rather than one hiding the other. The figures are not wrong and nothing is being double counted - it is a genuine repeat, and the board now shows it as one.

AND THE RAIL RUNS THE WHOLE PAGE. The divider is only as tall as the row it sits in, and the row is only as tall as its panels - so on a short board it stopped part way down. There is a viewport floor on the row now, so it reaches the bottom of the screen whatever the panels hold.

THE BLANK CHIP IN THE VERDICT ROW, chased down: ELEVEN rows carry a verdict this board has never had a shape for - ten written as warn (TTM round 5, rows 1056 to 1082) and one with no verdict at all. Each of them drew an EMPTY mark on the chart as well as producing that blank sixth segment. The board has five verdicts and the owner named them, so rather than invent a sixth an unrecognised one is read as FRAGILE, which is what a warning is. The row keeps what it actually recorded, so nothing is lost.

THE MORE / LESS TOGGLE IS GONE and every control is always shown. It existed when the controls were a wide block above the chart and half of them were pushing it off the screen; they are a sidebar now, so hiding half of them only hid them.

THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE THE POOLED TABLE IS GONE - the row count, what the grey study tag means, how to read one study at a time. The count is on the TABLES heading already and the VIEW control is two inches away.

A CONTROL TRACK IS NOW AS WIDE AS ITS BUTTONS. The grey track behind each group was being stretched to the full width of the sidebar column, so a two-button control drew a bar running off to the right with nothing in most of it. It shrinks to its contents.

AND THERE IS ONE DIVIDER INSTEAD OF A LINE THAT GIVES UP HALF WAY DOWN. The sidebar carried its own right-hand border, which stopped where its content stopped; the drag bar beside it runs the full height of the page. The border lives on the drag bar now, so the divider and the handle are the same edge, top to bottom.

THE SIDEBAR IS A SIDEBAR NOW, not a card in a column: full height, flush to the left edge, a hairline dividing it from the panels, and no tile background of its own - the panels are the cards, the sidebar is the frame. DRAG ITS EDGE to set how wide it is; the width is remembered and a double-click puts it back.
AND THE GREY BAR UNDER CLEAR FILTERS IS GONE. It was a horizontal scrollbar: the sidebar scrolled on both axes, so any control a pixel wider than the column produced one. It scrolls vertically only.
A CONTROL IS ONE SEGMENTED SWITCH instead of a row of separate bubbles. The group carries the fill and the selected option lights up inside it, so you can see where a section starts and ends.

EVERY CONTROL IS IN ONE PLACE. The COMPARE view picker (PICK RUNS through STUDIES) and the table settings (VIEW, COLUMNS, ORDER, SPLIT BY RUN, COMPARE ON) moved into the sidebar, each under its own heading.

THE STACKED SPLIT RESIZES TOO. Side-by-side has always had a drag bar; stacked had none, so the tables ran as long as they ran. There is a horizontal bar under them now - drag down for more table, up for more chart.

THE NOVELS ARE BEHIND THE INFO ICON. Nothing was deleted - every caveat is still there on the hover, because each one exists to stop a specific misreading - but the chart gets one line instead of fourteen.

HOVERING THE TABLE NO LONGER REPAINTS ROWS AS YOU MOVE THROUGH IT. Coming from a table row there is nothing to point at, since the cursor is already on it, so that direction only isolates the chart line. Hovering a CHART line still lights its table row.

EV R REPLACES PF IN THE KEY COLUMNS: the average trade divided by the average LOSING trade, which is leverage-blind where dollar expectancy is not. PF is still on the chart and still in the READ hover, and the $/TRD column beside it is the same expectancy in dollars.

Two controls in the new sidebar wore the same number as their neighbour - AXIS shared 4 with STRATEGY, and VERTICAL AXIS and the run picker both shared 3 with LEVEL. The sidebar puts every control in a fixed vertical order now, so those three simply lost their ordinal rather than renumber ten controls whose numbers the help text cites by name.
A run row on AUTO VAL printed its family ordinal as well as its run number - #252 - 12 - NOISE. The run number is the identity there, so the family ordinal is dropped: it reads #252 - NOISE.

THE STUDIES BOARD IS THREE COLUMNS NOW: a LOCKED SIDEBAR holding every control, then the TABLES, then the CHART. The controls used to sit inside the chart tile, so scrolling down to read a table scrolled the settings off the screen; the sidebar stays put while both panels scroll past it.
The drag bar still governs the split, and it now divides the TABLES from the CHART rather than the chart from the tables. Double-click puts it back to half.
HOW TO READ and MORE moved to the top of the sidebar, beside the CONTROLS heading, so every setting is in one place.
CONTROL ORDER, as the owner reads it: which drawing, then which stretch of history, then which grade of evidence, then which strategy - each answer narrowing the one before it. Renumbered to match.

THE STRATEGY RAIL COUNTS WHAT THE LEVEL ACTUALLY HOLDS. On AUTO VAL the rows are runs, so the rail now counts runs - it was offering NOISE 130 when there are a dozen NOISE runs to compare. Every other level counts registry rows as before.

FIX on the new AUTO VAL level: it drew nothing. The run rows were being put through the same test as registry rows, and that test now asks the LEVEL gate first - which on this level correctly says no to every registry row, and was refusing the runs along with them. Only the filter chips apply to a run row.

AUTO VAL NOW READS PAST RUNS INSTEAD OF THE WRITE-UPS. It used to list study rows that happened to cite a run number, so a real Auto-Validate nobody had documented simply was not there - measured: the registry cites 66 run numbers between 202 and 301, and 34 runs inside that range are cited by no row at all, plus everything below 202. Picking NOISE showed the NOISE runs somebody wrote up rather than the NOISE runs that exist.

It is one row per RUN now, off the same Past Runs list the RUNBOARD reads, so it is complete by construction and cannot go stale. Pick a strategy on the rail and every run of it is on the parallel chart, compared on the same ten axes.

AND RUN ROWS FILL EVERY AXIS. A run records its own date window and its own validate block, so win rate, Sharpe, Sortino and expectancy in R are all there - the four a local sweep still cannot fill. Each row carries its verdict, its window and its run number, and the run number opens the report.

THE SPLIT BETWEEN THE CHART AND THE TABLES CAN BE GRABBED AGAIN. The drag always worked - what was missing was anything to aim at. The bar is as tall as the whole page (2,783 pixels on the owner screen) and its 64-pixel handle was centred in it, which put the grip about 1,400 pixels down and usually off-screen. The grip is sticky now, so it rides at eye level however far down the page you are, and it is a little wider and lighter.
HOVERING A CHART LINE NOW LIGHTS ITS TABLE ROW as well, and brings that row into view inside its own scroller - never by scrolling the page, which would move the line out from under the cursor.
THE HIGHLIGHT LETS GO. A mouse-over only fires when the cursor lands ON something, so sliding off a line into empty plot left the last row lit. Every mouse-over that is not on a row now clears it.

THE CONTROL CHIPS ARE THE BOARD OWN NOW. An unselected option is FILLED rather than transparent, so a row reads as a segmented control with one segment lit instead of one chip floating in space; the letter-spacing and padding came in, which is most of the width the row was spending on air.

AND THAT FIXES THE VERDICT CHIPS HANGING BELOW THEIR ROW. Each carries a 10-pixel mark set to display:block, and a block child inside an inline chip opens its own line box - measured 41 pixels tall against 14 for every other chip. The chips are inline-flex at line-height 1 now and the mark is inline.

WHY AUTO VAL LOOKS EMPTY, answered on the board rather than left to be wondered about: only a small share of the rows here were ever persisted as a real run - the level now prints that share against the whole board. It is the state of the research, not a filter and not a drawing bug. Most of what was tried was tried locally and never saved as a run.

AND WHY THE LINES ARE DIFFERENT COLOURS: a line is coloured by its VERDICT and never changes colour along its length - blue champion, green held up, amber fragile, red failed, grey reference, the same five the marks use. What looks like a colour change is two rows crossing. It says so under the chart.

BACKFILL GROUNDWORK: the shared NOISE research helper now computes the win rate, Sharpe, Sortino, average loss and expectancy in R for every cell it measures. Seven NOISE drivers call that one function, so they all gained the figures at once rather than being edited seven times. Same definitions augur_engine/analytics.py gives run_backtest and a validate, so a sweep row and an Auto-Validate row can share an axis honestly.
What is still needed per study is a machine-readable results dump and a name-to-cell mapping - 39 of 1,143 rows carry the figures so far.

HOVER ISOLATION NOW ACTUALLY WORKS. The first pass did it in CSS and the CSS did nothing: every line and dot on that chart carries its opacity as an SVG presentation attribute, and measured on the live page neither a group-level nor an element-level rule moved the computed value, while an inline style did. It is written inline now, and each mark stashes its resting opacity so leaving restores exactly what was there.

THE STUDIES CONTROL BLOCK IS ABOUT A THIRD SHORTER. The label column, the gutters and the row leading were all sized for a page with far fewer controls on it. Nothing is hidden and no control moved - the same block is simply denser.

AN UNSELECTED OPTION NOW READS AS OFF. Every option in a section was rendered a shade apart from its neighbour, so five live-looking buttons sat where one was actually in force. The unselected ones are greyed now, still legible. Only this board changed; every other tab strip on the site is untouched.

HOVER A LINE AND THE REST FADE. A row is drawn as several segments plus its dots, so hovering any part of it now isolates the whole row and thickens it - its path across ten axes can be followed end to end. Hovering a STUDY TABLE ROW does the same thing from the other side: the matching line lights up and the rest fade.
LEVEL reads in the owner order and in his words: SWEEPS, CONFIGS, AUTO VAL, CROWN, then ALL last as the escape hatch rather than first as the default-looking option. Saved picks are unaffected.

THE CHART AXES ARE ORDERED THE WAY THE QUESTION IS ASKED: what the edge COST to earn (Sharpe, Sortino, money per dollar of drawdown), then how RELIABLE it is (win rate, profit factor), then what it PAID (expectancy in R, expectancy, money per year, trades per year), ending on NET. The earlier arrangement put the sparsely-recorded axes on the left to stop lines fragmenting; hover isolation and the backfill make that unnecessary.

THE FIRST STUDY IS BACKFILLED. All 39 rows of the NOISE plateau sweep now carry a WIN percent, a SHARPE, a SORTINO and an average losing trade, so four axes that read not recorded on the SWEEPS level are filled for that study. Nothing was looked up - no sweep ever recorded those figures - the study was RE-RUN and they were recomputed from its own trades, using the same definitions augur_engine/analytics.py gives run_backtest and a validate. The plateau verdict is unchanged: still 7 of 7 axes on a plateau.

THE MAPPING IS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. Every row is matched to its re-run cell on figures the registry ALREADY held - the trade count must agree exactly and the profit factor to a hundredth - before a single figure is written. A cell that does not line up is refused and named, because putting one configuration Sharpe under another configuration name is worse than leaving a blank. 39 of 39 matched, 0 refused.

tools/backfill_risk_rows.py does the mapping and the writing; adding the next study is one function plus one line. 39 of 1,143 rows are done - the other 43 studies each need their driver re-run first.

SWEEPS CAN NOW CARRY THE FOUR RISK FIGURES THEY NEVER HAD. Until today a local .py sweep recorded money, drawdown, profit factor and a trade count and nothing else, which is why WIN percent, SHARPE, SORTINO and EV IN R were blank for every stage-1 row on the STUDIES board. The fix is one place, not 153 driver files: every sweep reaches the engine through run_backtest, so run_backtest now attaches win rate, Sharpe, Sortino, average win, average loss and expectancy in R to EVERY result it returns, derived from the trade list it already had in hand.

AND IT IS THE SAME ARITHMETIC A VALIDATE USES. Sharpe, Sortino and the average win / loss pair were written out inside validate.py and nowhere else. They now live once in analytics.py and validate calls them, so a sweep and an Auto-Validate put the SAME definition on the same axis - two definitions of Sharpe sharing one axis is exactly the silent blending this project keeps guarding against. Verified bit-identical on a 1,825-trade run.
A STUDIES ROW CAN NOW RECORD THEM: wr, sh, so and avl (or evr outright) are registry fields, documented in STUDIES_BOARD.md. Paste what the sweep prints and the axes fill.

CACHE HONESTY: a trial cached before today has no risk figures in it and no trade list to derive them from, so returning it would hand back a result silently missing the keys the engine now promises. Rather than throw away an 80MB cache on an epoch bump, every row written from now on carries a marker and an unmarked row is treated as a miss - recomputed once, on demand, then re-cached. Nothing shows a Sharpe that depends on cache state. The first sweep over old ground will be slower once.

BUG THE OWNER SPOTTED: axis labels sliced in half at the top of the parallel chart. An axis that NO row on screen records - $ / YEAR and TRADES / YR at the CONFIGS level, where no row carries a dated window - had no scale, so every tick value came out NaN and a NaN position put those labels at the very top edge where they were cut. Such an axis now draws no ticks at all and says under its own title that nothing on screen records it. The chart also gained a little headroom so a title can never crowd the top tick.

TWO NEW AXES, both from the owner metric review. EV IN R divides expectancy by the average losing trade, so it is LEVERAGE-BLIND - dollar EV scales with size, which is the thing that flattered the wrong rows. SORTINO sits beside MAR because a max drawdown is ONE worst event and this project already measured its confidence interval to be wider than the statistic itself; Sortino reads downside volatility across the whole run instead.
The third suggestion, EV times trades per year, is ALREADY the $ / YEAR axis - the same number by a different route - so it was not duplicated. The line under the chart says so.
Both new axes are run-document figures (total_sortino, total_avg_loss), so they fill on an Auto-Validate row and on a configuration row and stay blank on a local sweep, like WIN percent and SHARPE.

PBO now says NOT MEASURED instead of showing nothing. Before, a run with no PBO number simply omitted the whole card - so a report where the overfit-of-selection check never ran looked exactly like one with no concerns.

THIS AFFECTS EVERY CROWNED CHAMPION. ORB #234, NOISE #243, ENGU-Q #265 and #226, ORB #230 and the new cooldown #286 all have NO PBO number, because they are pinned single-config files and the check works by ranking the candidates a search tried against each other - one config leaves nothing to rank. Their PASS is five checks, not six.

The tile now reads n/a in grey with NOT MEASURED under it, never green, because an absence of evidence must not read as a clean bill. If a config came out of an earlier search run, that run PBO is the one that applies to it.

THE CONFIGS LEVEL WAS DRAWING HALF A CHART AND NOT SAYING WHY. Caught on run 243: with WALK-FORWARD ticked, every gate, tilt and hybrid row lost its money, its MAR, its EV and its NET and drew as two lonely dots, because a configuration record is scored on ONE window - the optimize window - and holds no walk-forward or lockbox figure of its own. The reason was sitting two controls away with nothing pointing at it.

PROFIT STAGE IS NOW PINNED ON THAT LEVEL, to the one window those rows actually have, and the buttons say so on hover. Offering three ticks there was offering a choice that does not exist. Leave the level and the tick is yours again, untouched.
Every caption, column highlight and dash-reason on that level follows the pinned stage too, so nothing prints WF over a figure measured on the optimize window.

A CONFIGURATION ROW NO LONGER CALLS ITSELF A LOCAL SWEEP. The parallel chart knew two sources - run-backed and sweep - so the new CONFIGS rows, which are neither, fell through to the sweep wording. There are three now: SOLID is a real Auto-Validate run, DASHED is a local .py sweep, and DOTTED is a configuration read out of one run. Each hover says which, and the dotted one says in full that it is optimize-window only, unjudged by any lockbox, and one of the top few the search returned.

PARALLEL CHART AXIS ORDER FIXED, caught on the live board: adding WIN percent and SHARPE in the middle chopped most lines into fragments too short to draw, because a line breaks wherever a row records nothing and only a run-backed row records those two. The four axes that only some rows can fill - WIN percent, SHARPE, dollars per year and trades per year - now sit on the LEFT, so a row without them starts late and then runs unbroken through PF, MAR, EV and NET. Nothing is bridged; the break just happens at the edge instead of in the middle.

COMPARE > STUDIES NOW SEPARATES THE FOUR STAGES OF THE PIPELINE, on a new LEVEL control at the head of the chart rail. A local .py SWEEP, a real AUTO-VALIDATE run, the CONFIGS inside one such run and the standing CROWN of each family are four different grades of evidence, and ranking them in one list reads as if they were comparable. One level at a time keeps the axes measuring like with like; ALL stays the default and says out loud that it is mixing stages.

CONFIGS OF ONE RUN is new and is the deep one: pick an Auto-Validate run and its RAW, GATE, TILT and HYBRID candidates - the same four tabs the run report 1E card shows - load onto the chart and into the tables. Those records are not part of the fast page load, so the full run document is fetched on demand and the board says LOADING while it is in flight.

THE HONESTY LINE ON THAT LEVEL, printed under the chart rather than buried: those rows are scored on the OPTIMIZE WINDOW ONLY, so no lockbox has judged any of them, and they are the best of hundreds the search tried, so the leader is flattered by the picking itself. They are candidates, never survivors, and they are kept off the same axes as a board row for exactly that reason.

WIN PERCENT AND SHARPE ARE NOW AXES ON THE PARALLEL CHART. Neither has ever existed in the studies registry, so they are read off the run document behind a row - validate.total_win_rate and validate.total_sharpe, both already carried by the projected run list - and off the candidate record itself for a config row. A SWEEP row shows neither, because my local sweeps have never printed them, and a blank there is the truth rather than an oversight. Eight axes now: WIN percent, PF, SHARPE, MAR, EV, dollars per year, trades per year, and NET last.
Every level states in words, under the chart, what it is showing and what that grade of evidence can and cannot be read as.

NOISE ROUND 5 ON THE STUDIES BOARD (rows 1090-1140, owner: "do more testing while im away. new / better params / versions of this"). Two pre-registered studies on the configuration NinjaTrader is trading right now, with the bar written down before a single cell ran.

DOES THE CROWN TRAVEL? Run 243 moved verbatim onto seven other bar sizes and onto the 24-hour session - nothing re-fitted, not one knob touched. On the day session it travels: all eight bar sizes from one minute to one hour clear all four legs, and the money stays inside a 271k-325k band while the trade count falls almost fourfold. On the 24-hour session it FAILS outright, the same shape ORB showed. Two honest reductions the review pass forced: the eight day-session cells share most of their sessions and correlate at 0.97, so they are one observation rather than eight, and the configuration with BOTH crown filters switched OFF clears the same bar on seven of the eight - so what travels is the NOISE band mechanism, not specifically run 243.

IS THE CROWN A PLATEAU OR A SPIKE? Every one of its seven knobs nudged one step each way, everything else pinned: seven of seven sit on a plateau, no slope and no spike anywhere, and the verdict survives tightening the test from keeping 80 percent of the crown to keeping 90. Run 243 is not a lucky cell.

THE LEAST FLATTERING NUMBER IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE. Inside the live configuration the wildest-10-percent volatility skip is worth MINUS 400 dollars across 694 trades, and it fails the concentration rule at every threshold tested. It is the second of the two filters the crown was chosen for. Recorded, not acted on - the selection window is spent and this needs fresh forward evidence, not a re-read of the same years.
EVERY CELL EARNS 92 TO 102 PERCENT OF ITS MONEY AFTER 2018. That is a property of the strategy, not of this round, and it is now on the board in writing.
