2B / 2C SCATTER: taller charts, larger axis numbers, axis titles moved clear of the ticks, and the double-click expanded view now has the crosshair readout (trade # and $ / heat and reach) on top of the per-dot tooltips.
PROFIT CONCENTRATION is a ROBUSTNESS chip now (section 3, the dashboard chips and the CAUTIONS strip all read the same chip).
Section 2 no longer goes silent on a single-config validate (run 241): the SURFACES and BARS columns show an N/A card that says the run validated ONE pinned config and how to get the surfaces.
PAST RUNS: the CHAMPIONS chip is unmistakable when ON (filled, reads CHAMPIONS ON) and a note beside it says champions only - n of N runs - click to show all.

PAPER: the ENGU-Q raw leg (run 226) is retired from the forward test and replaced by run 265, the efficiency-gated config, which appears as ENGUQ_ER with its crowned logistic hybrid beside it as ENGUQ_ER_H. One backtest, two rows, so the raw row is the hybrid row exact control.
STUDIES: row 250 added for run 265 and tagged PAPER; row 87 keeps the CROWN tag but no longer reads as forward-tested.

The PROFIT CONCENTRATION caution is now EXACT on new runs: the engine saves the full trade-list net and top-10 trade PnLs (trade_conc) next to the sampled distribution. Older runs keep the sampled read and say so in the caution (SAMPLE read: n of N trades saved).

2B TRADE PNL DISTRIBUTION and 2C MAE / MFE each gained a HIST / SCATTER rail. 2B SCATTER = every champion trade as a dot in time order, dot AREA = size of the win or loss, a linear-regression trend line (is the edge fading?), mean and one-sigma lines, and the five biggest winners ringed and numbered so you can see when a handful of trades carry the whole result. Under the chart: top 1 / 5 / 10 share of net and the net WITHOUT the top 5.

2C SCATTER = heat (MAE) vs reach (MFE) per trade, won / lost colour, dot area = trade $ when the run saved both at the same sample size, a regression line of reach on heat, and the same stop / target guides the distribution draws. The WF / LB / TOTAL scope switch drives both views.

New CAUTIONS strip directly under the report header, in every layout: a PROFIT CONCENTRATION warning (over 50% of net in 5 trades, or over 25% in one) that turns red when the net goes negative without the top 5 - the ENGU-Q trap - plus every robustness chip that is not a pass (PBO, adversarial, synthetic, DOF...). Hover a caution for the detail.

PAST RUNS: new CHAMPIONS toggle in front of the family chips - one click shows only the champion of every family (the starred run of that family, or its highest SCORE when none is starred). Click again to show everything.

ORB crown confirmed and paper brought in line. The open search over the same configuration space (run 264, 353 configs) could not find run 234 and the configuration it crowned instead failed its lockbox, so 234 stands as the ORB baseline. Both ORB paper legs now run it, with the gate leg re-based on run 234 own crowned gate and a freshly calibrated size divisor.

COMPARE > STUDIES: the crown-versus-paper mismatch the board was showing is closed. Row 47 now reads CROWN and PAPER, rows 26 and 83 record the dates they were in paper, and the paper-legs study points at run 234. Row 67 had two status sentences and now has one.

THE 1A FUNNEL IS BACK ON PINNED CHAMPION RUNS. A pinned single-config Auto-Validate (run 241 and the other NOISE variants, ORB 234) stores one RAW curve plus the full gate / tilt / hybrid set, but the funnel was skipped whenever fewer than two RAW curves existed - so the family toggles, the expanded explorer and the gate overlay all vanished on exactly the runs that matter. The chart now draws whenever the run holds at least one RAW curve and any other family; normal 300-trial runs like 231 are untouched.

THE NOISE CROWN MOVED TO SHORT VETO (run 241) at the owner decision, on the combination study recommendation: the champion core plus one filter - skip short trades the day after the prior session closed in the bottom fifth of its own range. Run 241 is now starred in Past Runs, so it pins to the top of the list. The star on run 226 (the ENGU-Q crown) stays - one star per family.

STUDIES board: the NOISE crown tag moved from row 1 to row 2. Row 1 stays on the board as the reference baseline - nothing was deleted or renumbered - and the what-is-running-in-paper study gained row 249 for the new Short Veto shadow leg.

PAPER: a new shadow leg, NOISE-241 SHORT VETO, runs the crowned config nightly with NOISE-225 as its matched control - the filter is the only difference between the two rows. NinjaTrader still runs the baseline core with the gate: the NinjaScript port gained the filter knob, default off, and flipping it on waits for a NinjaTrader restart and an owner call. That gap is recorded on the board, not hidden.
RESULTS - Past Runs: starred runs are now PINNED to the top of the list whatever sort or filter is active, and carry a BASELINE chip, so the crowned run never has to be searched for.
Run 226 (ENGU-Q 24-hour, the paper baseline) is now the one starred run; the eight stale stars from July were cleared so exactly one crown remains.

ONE TABLE. New control 14, VIEW, on the TABLES block. ONE TABLE pools every surviving row from every study into a single ranked table - the consolidated read of a strategy - with a grey study tag on each row so nothing loses its provenance. BY STUDY is the old per-study list, where each study notes live. Left alone the board decides: one table while a strategy is picked, by study when everything is showing.

THIS ALSO ANSWERS WHY A NOISE-TITLED STUDY KEPT APPEARING UNDER ORB: that study holds the old ORB crown as its comparison baseline, so it contributes one ORB row. The row is ORB; only the study title said NOISE. In ONE TABLE view the row simply sits with the rest of ORB, tagged with where it was researched.

THE REGISTRY WAS AUDITED AGAINST THE REAL RUN HISTORY. All 38 run numbers the studies board cites exist in Firestore - no row points at a run that is not there. In the other direction, 13 persisted Auto-Validate runs were cited by no row and matched no row figures. They are on the board now as one new study, RECOVERED BY THE REGISTRY AUDIT, every figure verbatim from its run doc: the July NOISE pair (202, 203), three mid-August runs that saved no verdict (214, 215, 217), the two pre-registered ML-gate tests (218, 219), the nine-trade ENGU-Q failure (216), and the five ORB_3_4 profit-target variants (209-213).
ROW 2, SHORT VETO, GAINS RUN 236. That run carries exactly row 2 figures - it is the original short-veto validate; run 241, already cited, is the SBS re-run.

WHAT WAS NOT ADDED, deliberately: the six BOOK runs (multi-strategy portfolios, which live on the RUNBOARD), the four ORB_3_1_125C runs (the closed look-ahead family), and the 151 runs from before the studies era - TTIBS, SUPERTREND, VWAP-FADE, RSIDIV, REVERT and the spring ENGU evolution, all ruled out elsewhere.

THE TABLES OPEN ON THE FAIR-COMPARISON FIGURES ONLY. New control 13, COLUMNS. KEY - the new default - prints the row, its name, PROFIT FACTOR, DOLLARS PER TRADE, MAR, the trade count behind them and the one-line verdict. Those are the figures that survive two rows covering different stretches of history, which most of this board does: profit factor is gross winnings over gross losses across the whole trade population, dollars per trade is the same money divided by the trades that earned it, and neither is a property of the calendar. Raw totals are left OUT on purpose - side by side they invite a comparison the windows do not support. ALL brings back the three stages, the recorded total, the drawdown and the whole context block.

NOTHING IS HIDDEN BY IT. Every figure KEY leaves out is still on the READ hover of the row, which prints the entire row - all three stages, the total, the drawdown, the trade count and where it came from, the run, and the data window.

A CONTROL IS ONE LINE AGAIN: its number and name in a narrow fixed column, its buttons filling the rest. The card version put every label on its own line above its buttons, which in the narrow half of the split became twelve two-line stacks with a gap under each one. Now the labels line up down the block, the buttons all start at the same x, and a control whose buttons wrap wraps inside its own row without moving its neighbours. The grid fits as many of those rows side by side as the width allows - one column in the split pane, two or three across a full-width board.

THE CONTROL BLOCK IS ONE TILE AND ONE GRID. It was a four-column arrangement of label, buttons, label, buttons, so any control whose buttons wrapped shoved its neighbour label away from its own buttons - which is what made the block read as scattered with holes in it. Every control is now a card of its own, its number and name over its own buttons, and the cards sit on one auto-fitting grid inside ONE box. A card that wraps can no longer move anything else. The tables controls are the same grid, in the same kind of box, directly under their own heading.
STUDY TABLES is just TABLES.

9 STUDY NOW LISTS ONLY THE STUDIES THE STRATEGY PICK LEAVES STANDING, with the number of rows each one still contributes. It was built from the whole registry, so with NOISE on the rail it still offered ORB and ENGU-Q studies - and picking one emptied the board. A study you have already picked stays listed even if the rail later excludes it, so it can be seen and cleared rather than vanishing while it is still narrowing the board.

AN EMPTY CHART NOW SAYS WHY IT IS EMPTY, in the registry own words. Pick the NOISE trade-context scan and nothing plots, because that study is six SCANS: a scan asks whether a market condition predicts profit and produces no profit and no equity curve of its own, so there is no drawdown to place it by. The chart used to answer with a sentence about the basis selected, which reads like a setting is wrong. It now prints the study own reason and points at the table, where what the scans DID measure is sitting.

THE STUDY TABLES WERE SHIFTED BY ONE COLUMN AND ARE FIXED. The TOTAL cell was being wrapped in a second table cell, which is not legal HTML, so the browser lifted the inner one out and every row gained a cell: TOTAL drew empty, its money sat under DRAWDOWN, the drawdown sat under PF, and everything to the right of it was one heading out of place. No figure was ever wrong - they were printed under the wrong headings. The render gate now counts cells against headings on every table in every case, because the row COUNT was right the whole time and nothing noticed.
DRAWDOWN IS RED, heading and figures. It is the only loss on the row and it is printed without a minus sign, so the colour is what says so.

THE TOTAL COLUMN NO LONGER FLAGS ITSELF. A row recorded total is not always the sum of its three stages, and that is still stated on the hover of the cell - but the board is read on ratios and on the stage columns, neither of which uses that number, so it is a fact rather than a warning.

WHICH STRATEGY A ROW BELONGS TO, now that two of them can share the chart. The mark shape is the VERDICT and never said anything about the family, so: each mark carries its strategy beside its row number, every point hover names it in the headline, and every table row wears it as a tag after the name. All three appear ONLY when more than one strategy is on screen - with one selected they would be the same word on every line.

THE BOARD OPENS WITH THE CHART. There is no separate heading tile any more: the first tile IS the chart, it is called SCATTER PLOT, and every control that decides what it plots sits directly under that title. The old chart heading, which restated the strategy selection and the row count, is gone - the rail says the first and the line under the chart says the second.
1 STRATEGY LOSES ITS ALL BUTTON. An empty rail already means nothing is held back, so ALL was a second way of saying the same state.
9 STUDY IS A DROP-DOWN. Sixteen study titles as buttons was the tallest thing in the control block; it is one line now, and one study at a time, which is what reading them one at a time meant anyway.

10 ORDER, 11 SPLIT BY RUN AND 12 COMPARE ON now sit in a block directly under the STUDY TABLES heading. They were pinned to the far right of that heading, which on a wide screen put them the width of the page away from the tables they change.

ENGU-Q TRADES THAT HAPPENED OVERNIGHT OR ON A SUNDAY COULD NOT DRAW A CHART AT ALL. ENGU-Q trades the 24-hour tape, but the chart was always asking for cash-session bars, so any entry outside 9:30 to 4:00 came back as trade date not found. Those charts open now.

ENGU-Q LIMIT 0.50 was drawing 5-minute candles for a 1-minute strategy. Every leg on the board now asks for its own market and session rather than only the three original ones being recognised by name.

THE STRATEGIES YOU PICK ON THE PAPER BOARD ARE REMEMBERED NOW. Which legs you have switched off used to be forgotten the moment you reloaded, so the board kept resetting to showing all of them. It is a saved setting like every other choice on the page.
A SELECTION OF TRADES OPENS AS ONE LONG SCROLL. Picking twenty trades used to give you ten and a LOAD 10 MORE button - you already chose them, so all of them are there and you just scroll.
THERE IS A LOADING BAR ACROSS THE TOP OF THE CHART WINDOW while the charts fill in, so you can see it moving rather than reading a count. It disappears when everything has landed.
PREV and NEXT sit next to each other in the single-trade chart window. The position readout used to sit between them, which broke the pair up.

THE DUPLICATE CROWN IS FIXED IN THE REGISTRY. ORB carried two: row 47, which is run #234 and the standing crown, and row 67, the SAME configuration restated inside the plateau-hunt study. Row 47 keeps the tag; row 67 keeps its figures and its champion verdict and now reads as that study baseline. One family, one champion - so the BASELINE SELECTOR is gone, because there is nothing left to choose between.

1 STRATEGY AND 2 PROFIT STAGE TICK instead of switching. Click NOISE and ENGU-Q and both are on the chart together. PROFIT STAGE loses its TOTAL button and is IS, WF and LB - tick the ones you want and the chart plots their sum.

ONE THING THAT HAD TO BE HANDLED HONESTLY THERE: only 46 of the 215 rows record a separate walk-forward figure. The rest have no walk-forward STAGE at all - their first money column is PRE-LOCKBOX, which already holds the tuning years pooled together. So the sum adds the ticked stages a row ACTUALLY RECORDS and only drops a row that records none of them; ticking all three on a pre-lockbox row gives pre-lockbox plus lockbox, which is its whole run. Any row that lacks a ticked stage says so on its own hover and the count is stated under the chart. Requiring all three would have emptied the chart from 203 rows to 47.

AND THE OTHER: a row TOTAL is not always the sum of its three stages - the NOISE champion records $335,981 while its stages add to $313,409. They are separate measurements. The TOTAL column prints what the row recorded and marks the gap with a sign you can hover; the chart plots the sum you ticked.

READ AS IS NOW 4 AXIS, and its two settings are ABSOLUTE and CHAMPION. The words crown and baseline are off this board - the verdict reads CHAMPION in the key too. The dashed crosshair that only CHAMPION used to draw is now drawn in ABSOLUTE as well, on the champion own position, so both settings show the same reference: right of the vertical is a deeper drawdown than the champion took, above the horizontal is more money than it made.
THE AXES ARE DRAWN: two solid lines and a tick mark at every gridline, rather than a frame implied by the gridlines alone.

HOVERING A POINT LEADS WITH THE ANSWER - row, name, rank, total and profit factor in caps above a rule, with everything else underneath. Hovering the READ cell of a table now gives the whole row: the verdict and what it means, what the variant does, the money, the ratios, the trade count and where it came from, where it ran and over what stretch of history.

EVERY PAPER TRADE CHART SAID SHORT, INCLUDING THE LONGS. The shadow log records direction as the engine’s own +1 / -1, and the board was comparing that to the words long and short - which never match, so every chart drew and labelled the trade as a short. ENGU-Q only ever buys, so every one of its charts was wrong.
The SIDE column in the trades table said 1 for the same reason. It reads LONG or SHORT now.
THE VERDICT BUTTONS ARE MARK-SIZED. They were rendering at legend size, which made five of them read as a row of pictures rather than a row of controls. The legend keeps the full-size mark.

THE STATUS CHIP STRIP IS GONE - rows shown, comparison basis, range and shared window. Every one of them summarised something the board already says where it matters: the row count is on the chart heading, the basis and the range are on their own controls, and the shared window is the DATA WINDOW column with a warning sign on any row reaching outside it. HOW TO READ was the one thing on that strip worth keeping and it moves up beside MORE.
CHAMPION OR BASELINE IS JUST BASELINE in the key, which is what it is: under VS CROWN it is the row sitting on the crossing of the two zero lines, with every other point measured from it.

THE BASELINE RAIL NAMES ITS ROWS. It was printing bare row numbers - row 1 or row 97 - with no way to tell what either was. It now reads Champion (row 1) and Paper: NOISE (row 97), says which study each came from on hover, and says that the one you pick is the point on the crossing of the zero lines.

YOU CAN NOW SELECT SEVERAL TRADES AT ONCE IN THE PAPER TAB AND OPEN ALL THEIR CHARTS TOGETHER. Click a row to select it, hold the button down and drag across rows to take a run of them, shift-click to stretch the selection to where you clicked, and ctrl-click to add or drop a single row. The heading counts what is selected and offers OPEN N CHARTS.

The charts arrive in one scrolling window, one card per trade, instead of a modal you had to close and reopen for every trade. Each card zooms with ctrl and the wheel, pans by dragging, and can be saved on its own as a PNG or all together through SAVE ALL.
The selection survives re-sorting and re-filtering the table, and the CHART button on a row still opens that one trade on its own.
That chart window used to assume every trade came from one run of one instrument. It now reads each trade’s own market and timeframe, which is what let a mixed list of paper legs open in it at all.
CONTROL NAMES ARE LEFT ALIGNED. Right-aligning them against an auto-width column meant every row started somewhere different.

TIME SCOPE AND THE DISCOVERED FILTER WERE THE SAME QUESTION ASKED TWICE - one as a rolling window, one as a list of every distinct date in the registry. They are one control now, 5 RANGE: ALL, TODAY, WK, MO, 3MO, and SELECT, which opens the calendar on a from and a to. Either end of SELECT can be left blank for open-ended. The word past is gone from every label.
VERDICT is the marks themselves now, not five lines of words - the same shapes the chart draws, with the name on the hover.

RUN STATUS is just RUN, and its two buttons say EL and .PY: EL is a real Auto-Validate run persisted in EDGELOG with a run number and a report, .PY is local research run on the machine and never saved as a run.
THE STATUS FILTER IS GONE. Crowned and in-paper are already pills beside the name in the table, so filtering on them was a third way to say the same thing.

THE LINE OF TEXT UNDER THE CHART IS GONE. Only the verdict legend is left, with a small circled i beside it whose hover still carries every count and every reason that line used to print - the rows plotted, the rows that could not be, and why. Nothing measured was dropped; it is one hover away instead of always on screen.

THE AXES ARE READABLE. Tick numbers and axis captions were drawn in the faintest ink the theme has, at a size chosen when the chart had the whole page - in the split layout it has half that and they disappeared. Both go up in size and contrast, and the two axis lines are drawn rather than left to the gridlines.
Controls renumber 1 to 12.

ENGU-Q LIMIT 0.50 now carries a limit entry tag on its row. Two ENGU-Q rows sitting side by side with identical columns is a puzzle unless the row says what makes them different, so hovering the tag explains it: same settings, the only change is that it rests a limit order half an ATR below the signal close and drops the trade if it never fills.
The tag also carries the honest caveat from its validate - entering lower against the same stop widens risk, so it fails the pre-registered net-per-drawdown bar. It is a candidate, not a winner.
Any leg can now carry a tag like this, rather than the board hard-coding one strategy name.

ENGU-Q LIMIT 0.50 now has a row on the board. It has been computed every night since 18 August but was never added to the leg list, so it was running and completely invisible - it never appeared in the strip, the curve or any table.

What it is: the same 24-hour ENGU-Q settings, entered with a resting limit order half an ATR BELOW the signal close, which is dropped if it does not fill within ten bars. ENGU-Q RAW is deliberately kept beside it as the matched control, so the only difference between the two rows is the entry.
It is engine-only on purpose. It shares a contract with ENGU-Q, so the two could never be traded together in one account.

FOUR RUNS WERE THE SAME RUN TWICE, and they have been archived. On 18 August the same four NOISE configurations were validated a second time - runs 251, 252, 253 and 254 repeat runs 245, 243, 241 and 242. Every field was checked before archiving: same strategy file, same date window, same data source, same costs, the same fifteen crowned settings and the same headline figures down to the cent. Nothing was deleted and one click un-archives any of them.

WHY IT HAPPENED: one session queued the jobs and then died. A second session looked at the queue, saw nothing waiting or running, and queued four of them again. The four originals had already FINISHED, so the check of the day could not see them.

THE SYSTEM NOTICES NOW. Every job is fingerprinted on the things that decide its numbers - the strategy file, the date window, the data source and session, the costs and the search settings - and that fingerprint is compared against jobs that have already FINISHED as well as ones still waiting. The free-text note, the provider and the worker count are ignored, because two jobs that differ only in those compute the same answer.

IT WARNS, IT DOES NOT BLOCK. Queue a repeat from the Builder and you are told which run already did it and on what date, and asked whether to go ahead - because running something again to check it reproduces, or on newer data, is a fair thing to want. Jobs queued straight in by a script have nobody to ask, so those run and get labelled as a repeat instead.

A REPEAT NOW SAYS SO. A run the guard recognised carries a REPEAT OF badge on its own report, and on the STUDIES board a row no longer counts an archived repeat in its plus-N marker - it shows a separate archived mark whose hover explains what happened.

ORDER BY WAS THREE QUESTIONS IN ONE CONTROL and is now three controls. It offered DISCOVERED, DATE RAN and RESULT, which mixed up sort-by-date with sort-by-performance and quietly threw in the auto-validate grouping on top - DATE RAN did all three at once. Now: ORDER is DATE or RESULT. SPLIT BY RUN is its own on/off switch for the grouping into rows that were persisted as a validate run and rows that never were. And DATE - one control, asked once - decides WHICH of the two dates a row carries the board means: it sets the date column, what ORDER BY DATE sorts on and what TIME SCOPE reads. Its old FOLLOWS ORDER BY setting is gone, because ORDER no longer names a date to follow.

COMPARE ON MOVED TO THE STUDY TABLES and now changes only them. It adds the per-year columns, which is a table thing - but it also used to move every point on the chart, reach it never announced. The chart reads what VERTICAL AXIS says and nothing else. Everything that belongs to the tables now sits on the tables: ORDER, SPLIT BY RUN and COMPARE ON.

THE COLOUR CONTROL IS GONE. The board always colours: it follows the app theme where the theme carries real colour and uses the five approved colours where it does not, which is what the setting resolved to anyway. Every mark still carries its own shape, so nothing here ever depended on colour to be readable.
Controls renumber: 1 to 4 decide the chart, 5 to 11 sit behind MORE, and 12 to 14 belong to the study tables.

ORDER BY MOVED TO THE STUDY TABLES, on their own heading, because that is the only thing it orders. It is control 14 now and the chart block is down to four: STRATEGY, PROFIT STAGE, VERTICAL AXIS, READ AS.

It does NOT change what is on the chart, and the reason is worth saying plainly: sorting cannot move a point, so no row is ever gained or lost by it. Two couplings survive and both are on its hover. Under DATE RAN the chart fades the never-run points, so it matches the ran and never-run split the tables are showing underneath. And while TIME SCOPE is on, SCOPE DATE defaults to following this control, so it decides which of a row two dates the scope reads - set SCOPE DATE explicitly and even that is gone.
The controls behind MORE renumber to 5 to 13.

PF IS A CHART AXIS NOW. Profit factor was readable in the table and nowhere else, which is backwards for the most window-robust figure on the board: it counts trades rather than calendar, so two rows covering different years can still be read against each other. It also has the widest reach of any axis here - 203 of the 215 rows plot on it, against 146 on $/TRADE. Like $/TRADE it says on the axis that it ignores PROFIT STAGE and COMPARE ON, because a profit factor is recorded once per row.

PROFIT÷DD IS CALLED MAR. It always was the same division the RUNBOARD and the 1E matrix call MAR - profit over the worst drawdown - and this board was the only place using a different name for it. Same number, same maths, one name. The per-year column reads MAR / YR. The heading still opens by saying MAR is NOT profit factor: PF counts trades, MAR rests on a single worst event, and a row can score well on one and badly on the other.

TRADE COUNTS ARE NOW READ WHERE THEY EXIST. A row without its own count takes one off the saved run document when it has a run number - the same source rule the DATA WINDOW column already follows - and a small circle marks a figure read from the run rather than written in the registry. THAT REACHES 2 OF THE 73 MISSING ROWS. The other 71 are local research: nothing recorded their trade count and they have no run to read one from, so there is no source and a number would have to be invented. They keep a dash, and the dash now says what would fix it - record the count on the row, or persist the variant as a validate run.
FRONTIER is removed, as asked. The chart is a plain scatter again.

PF AND PROFIT÷DD ARE DIFFERENT MEASUREMENTS and both columns stay. PF is gross winnings divided by gross losses, counted trade by trade, so it says how much the winners outweigh the losers and a mismatched window barely moves it. PROFIT÷DD is net profit divided by the single worst peak-to-trough loss, so it says how much money the worst stretch cost to earn - one event, which is why it is the most fragile figure here. The column headings now spell out that difference.
The controls renumber to 1 to 14.

COMMON WINDOW IS REMOVED from COMPARE ON. It was the most rigorous option on the board and it could reach almost nothing: slicing a row needs the equity curve a real run saved, and 31 of the 216 rows here have a run behind them at all. The other 185 are local research with no curve to cut, so the basis dashed 85 percent of the board by construction - and that gap only widens, because windows naturally diverge as testing goes on.

What answers the same question instead is already on the board and needs no slicing: PROFIT FACTOR and the new $/TRD are properties of the trade population rather than of the calendar, so a longer window does not flatter either of them. PER YEAR remains for reading money against the length of the window it was earned over, and it reaches every row that records a window.

NOTHING THAT MEASURES A WINDOW WAS TOUCHED. The DATA WINDOW column still says what stretch every row covers, the WINDOW status chip still names the stretch the visible rows share, and the warning still names the rows that reach outside it. Knowing the rows do not share a stretch is the point; slicing them was only one way to act on it, and it was the way that could not reach the board.

MONEY IS ABBREVIATED in the study tables: 400,000 reads 400k, 6,190 reads 6.2k, and a million-plus reads 1.24M. Anything under a thousand stays whole, because shortening 671 to 0.7k loses a digit and saves nothing. THE EXACT FIGURE IS ON THE HOVER of every abbreviated cell, so this costs space and not precision.

NEW $/TRD COLUMN, and $/TRADE as a chart axis. With profit factor it is the pair of figures on this board that a mismatched window barely touches, because both are properties of the trade population rather than of the calendar - a longer window does not flatter either of them. It is whole-run money divided by the trade count, so it says out loud that it cannot follow PROFIT STAGE or COMPARE ON: a trade count is recorded once per row, not per stage. 137 of the 216 rows record both figures; the rest show a dash saying which one is missing.

The PROFIT÷DD axis button now carries the warning it deserves: a drawdown is one single worst event, and this project measured the confidence interval around a maximum drawdown to be WIDER than the drawdown itself, so it is the most fragile reading here. PF is the most robust.

THE STATUS COLUMN IS GONE. It was a full column of dashes for the sake of the one or two rows per family that carry a pill. CROWN and PAPER now sit beside the name of the rows that have them, and rows that have neither show nothing at all rather than a dash.

THE MONEY MOVED LEFT. The order is now rank, row, name, then the four stage figures, drawdown, profit factor, profit-divided-by-drawdown and trades - the numbers you came for - with the read. The grey descriptive block (what it does, run, discovered, data window) sits at the far right where it can be ignored until you want it.

EVERYTHING IS A STEP SMALLER: the table drops to 8.5px, the headings to 7px, cell padding to 2px, and the grey block is dimmer than the numbers. Twenty-five rows now fit where fifteen used to, and nothing was dropped to do it - the two clipped prose columns still carry their whole sentence on hover.

VALUE ZOOM is gone. The axes have always spanned only the rows now shown, so the strategy rail and the filters already rescaled the chart; trimming the range was a second and blunter way of doing the same job, and it needed a pinned-to-the-edge special case to stay honest about the rows it pushed out of range. The chart now always fits every point it draws.

COLOUR had three settings and two of them were the same button for anyone on the monochrome theme. THEME already fell back to the five approved colours whenever the app theme is greyscale, which MONO is, so THEME and COLOUR painted an identical chart. There are two now: COLOUR follows the app theme where the theme carries real colour and uses the approved five where it does not, and SHAPES ONLY is unchanged. The app theme is still never touched.
The controls renumber to 1 to 15.

ONE STRATEGY CONTROL, NOT TWO. The STRATEGY rail at the top and the STRATEGY TYPE filter chips further down were always the same setting - the rail writes that very filter - so the chips were a second copy of the same buttons. They are gone. The rail is control 1 and it is the only place a strategy is picked.

THE CONTROLS ARE TWO PER LINE and NUMBERED 1 to 16. One per line left the right-hand half of the tile empty and cost twice the height for it. The block is roughly half as tall now, and the numbers mean a control can be named in a sentence rather than described - set 4 to VS CROWN, turn 5 off. Control 16, the sixteen study titles, takes a full-width line of its own.

THE CONTROLS ARE A GRID. Four ragged rows of chips wrapped wherever they ran out of width, so a label could end up nowhere near the buttons it named. Every control is one line now: its name on the left, its buttons on the right, and a group that runs long wraps inside its own cell instead of shoving the next control away from its label.

Two blocks. Always on screen: STRATEGY, PROFIT STAGE, VERTICAL AXIS, READ AS, FRONTIER, ORDER BY - the six that decide what the chart plots. Behind MORE: COMPARE ON, VALUE ZOOM, TIME SCOPE, SCOPE DATE, COLOUR and every filter chip, with CLEAR FILTERS on its own line.

READ AS and FRONTIER MOVED UP into that first block. They shipped on the chart tile header, where they were easy to miss: the owner went looking among the controls and did not find them. Same two controls, same behaviour, now beside the rest.

THE FRONTIER IS DRAWN. With a hundred marks on one chart the question that matters is which of them NOTHING BEATS - no other variant made more money AND took a smaller worst drawdown. That set is now ringed and joined by a dashed staircase, its row numbers are named under the chart, and a point on it says so when you hover it. It is computed from the points on screen, so filtering recomputes it, and it is a shape rather than a judgement: a row can sit on the frontier and still carry a FAILED verdict. FRONTIER ON / OFF sits on the chart header.

NEW READING: VS CROWN. It measures both axes FROM the champion of each row own family, so the crown lands on the zero lines and every other variant reads as the money it added and the drawdown it added against the thing actually being traded. That is the question these studies were really asking. It changes the CHART only - the tables underneath always print the absolute figures - and it is the same numbers subtracted, not new data.

A BASELINE RAIL appears with it, and it surfaces a real problem rather than hiding it: EVERY family currently has more than one row tagged crowned, because the what-is-running-in-paper study restates configurations other studies already crowned, and the contract says one family one crown. The chart reads against the LOWEST-numbered of them - a row number is a permanent handle handed out in order, so the lowest is the first time that crown was recorded and the rest restate it - it says so on the rail, and one click reads against a different one instead. No tag is changed by any of this.

THE SPLIT SCREEN RESIZES. Drag the bar between the chart and the study tables to give the chart more or less of the width; double-click puts it back to half. The width is remembered. The bar underneath the chart still sets its height, so the chart now resizes both ways.

THE GREEN ROW TINT IS GONE, as asked. The mark beside the name already carried that verdict. The blue tint stays on the one champion or baseline row per study, and it now explains itself on hover, as does the brighter flash that follows your pointer - which was never a verdict at all, but the live link between a table row and its point on the chart.

STUDY TABLES COMPRESSED. A row was three lines tall because two columns of prose were set to wrap. WHAT IT DOES and READ are now one line each, clipped with the full sentence on hover, the cell padding is halved and the type is a step smaller. A row is one line, so an open study shows about three times as many of them in the same space.

SPLIT SCREEN. The same two glyphs, in the same corner of the sub-tab bar, that RESULTS, LIBRARY and RESEARCH already use. Side puts the chart on the left and the study tables on the right, and the chart stays pinned while you scroll the tables past it; stacked is the old layout. Remembered like every other view setting.

THE TINTED ROWS NOW SAY WHY. Three different things were shading a row and nothing on screen explained any of them. A faint blue tint means the row verdict is champion or baseline; a faint green tint means it beat the champion and held up - both are saying exactly what the mark beside the name already says, and no other verdict tints at all. The brighter flash that follows your pointer is a fourth thing entirely: the live link between a table row and its point on the chart, which is why it disappears when you move away. Hover any tinted row and it tells you this itself.

STUDIES IS SHORT NOW. The board was still a wall of text: four paragraphs of running commentary above the chart, a full reference essay below it, an explainer around the chart itself, and sixteen study tables sitting open one after another. It is three rows of controls, the chart, and a list of study headings.

THE STUDY TABLES ARE CLOSED until you open one. Click a heading and it opens; click again and it closes; the board remembers which you left open. Clicking a point on the chart opens that row study table for you and scrolls to the row. A study the controls have emptied is not listed at all, and the heading above says how many that was.

THE FOUR STATUS PARAGRAPHS ARE FOUR CHIPS on one line - rows shown, comparison basis, time scope, and the shared data window - and each chip carries on its hover the entire paragraph it replaced, word for word. A chip that is warning you about something is still coloured, so a glance still tells you where to look.

MORE / LESS hides the six secondary control rails and the filter chips. They keep working while hidden, and the status chips always say what is in force. ? HOW TO READ hides the reference text - what each comparison basis means and which ratio survives a mismatched window. Both settings are remembered.

The paragraph under the chart is one line of counts, with every reason behind it on the hover. NOTHING MEASURED WAS REMOVED and nothing was rounded away: every sentence the board used to print is still on the board, on the hover of the short thing it explains or behind one of the two toggles.

STUDIES IS ONE SCATTER CHART AGAIN. It was meant to be one chart, and sixteen studies had quietly grown fourteen of them - fourteen sets of axes on fourteen different scales - so a strategy whose research is spread over five studies could not be read as a single picture, which was the whole point of the board. There is now ONE chart at the top, carrying every variant on the board: 203 of the 215 rows plot, and the twelve that do not are named underneath with the reason, as always.

A STRATEGY RAIL sits above it - ALL, ENGU-Q, NOISE, ORB, each with its row count - and that is how you step from one strategy to the next. Picking one narrows the chart AND every table below it together, because the rail writes the same strategy-type filter the chips further down already used, so the two can never disagree.

Every study still keeps its own table, its own notes and its own row numbers. Only the charts were merged, and nothing was invented to merge them: all fourteen already plotted the same two things, the worst drawdown across the bottom and the selected profit stage up the side. The two studies that never had a chart at all are on it now too.

A NEW STUDY FILTER, so one family with five studies behind it can still be read one study at a time on the single chart. A break-even line is drawn whenever the chart range crosses zero. Past 45 points the row numbers beside the marks are hidden so they stop overlapping into a smear - hover any point for its row, its strategy and its study - and the chart says when it has done that.

THE SHARED-HISTORY CHECK IS NOW A BOARD FIGURE, not a per-study one. One chart means the common window and the COMMON WINDOW basis have to be worked out across everything on screen, so the chart and every table under it are read on exactly the same stretch. Picking a single strategy usually WIDENS that stretch, because you stop intersecting families that were never run over the same years.
VERTICAL AXIS loses its PER STUDY setting, which had nothing left to mean once there was one chart - every study declared raw profit anyway. The chart size is remembered once rather than per study.
FIX: opening STUDIES before the run list had finished loading showed NO RUNS TO COMPARE YET. This board is registry data and needs no runs at all to draw itself.

New pre-push gate, tools/studies_render_probe.py: it renders this board headlessly under twelve control combinations and fails on any that throws or draws more than one chart. The boot gate only ever proved the app starts.
LEGS table tightened. Row height is roughly halved: every row is now a single scannable line of numbers, because the two wordy columns were what forced them to wrap and grow tall.
The gate summary and the run and parameter line now appear UNDERNEATH their strategy as one full-width line, not as wide columns beside it. Press show config and gate to reveal them.

THE LEGS BLOCK IS NOW A TABLE. Six strategies rendered as side-by-side tiles had grown into an unreadable overlap. Each strategy is now one row, with net, trades, win rate, days live, last trade, forward and backfilled counts, NinjaTrader status, cross-engine check and gate comparison each in their own column - so legs can be read down a column instead of hunted for.
The run and parameter line is off by default and appears as its own CONFIG column when you press show config.
Clicking a row still includes or excludes that strategy from the curve and from every figure in the table.

FIX to the leg toggling shipped earlier today, which did not work. Clicking a visible leg sent the word ALL instead of the leg name, so nothing was ever excluded and the hidden list filled with junk. Each leg now names itself, so clicking really does remove it from the curve and from every total, table and row beneath - and clicking it again brings it back.
The show all control is now wired on BOTH places it appears, the LEGS row and the rail in the header. Previously only the first one worked.

The run and parameter line under each strategy is hidden by default. With six legs on the strip it doubled the height for something you read once, not every glance. A show config button on the LEGS row brings it back for every tile at once.

THE APP NOW OPENS IN ABOUT THREE SECONDS INSTEAD OF THIRTY. Loading the page used to download every one of your last 75 runs in full, including the parts only a run report ever shows - the gate bake-off tables, the full set of config equity curves, the per-config scatter data and the trade excursion tables. That was about 25 megabytes of saved data, which Firestore sends as roughly 387 megabytes once it wraps every number in its own tag. The first screen needs about a fifth of a megabyte of it.

Past Runs now asks the server for only the columns the list actually shows, and fetches a run report in full the moment you click that run. You will see a brief LOADING line the first time you open a report; after that it is instant, and the last eight reports you opened stay in memory.

This is also why the app used to lock up for a minute when you clicked quickly between the COMPARE modes. It was never the drawing - each redraw takes about a fifth of a second. The browser was busy unpacking that run data in the background and could not answer the clicks. With the data gone, the clicks answer straight away.

The Builder job list now reads the newest 12 jobs rather than 50. It only ever displayed 12, and the other 38 were carrying a full copy of their finished results - about 12 megabytes of it - on every single page load.
Nothing was deleted and no run lost any detail. If the faster read ever fails the app quietly falls back to the old way of loading, so the list can never come up empty.

LEGS ARE NOW INCLUDE / EXCLUDE. Click any leg to take it out of the cumulative curve AND out of every total, table and cross-engine row beneath it, then click it again to bring it back. Several variants of the same strategy run side by side - three NOISE rows alone - so reading one of them means removing the others from the maths, not just dimming them on the chart.

Nothing is deleted when you exclude a leg. The runner still computes it every night and its history comes straight back. A show all button appears whenever anything is hidden, and the board refuses to let you switch off the last leg.

TODAY now says where its money comes from. The figure is EDGELOG own engine, and it sits next to how many fills NinjaTrader actually recorded that day. On a day NinjaTrader was down those two disagree, and that is the point: the strategy still has a result and this is where you read it.

COMPARE > STUDIES: the board now compares individual strategies only. Every study about pooled books - several strategies traded together as one account - has been taken off it, at the owner request. Forty-six rows removed: the pooled-books study, the book leg weighting grid, the book legs re-measured the book way, and the ORB plus NOISE book row that sat inside the NOISE study.
The research itself was not touched. Every one of those results is still written down in the repository book round log.
Row numbers are permanent handles, so nothing was renumbered. Rows 25, 28 to 46 and 236 to 261 are retired and will never be handed to a new row. The next free number is 262.

The explanatory notes that talked about pooled books have been reworded, because their subject is gone. The board now says plainly why a combination cannot be compared with one strategy: it ties up more margin, so the two are not like for like. Use the RUNBOARD mode to compare whole combinations.
COMPARE > STUDIES: six new studies covering the research that was run locally in Python over the past fortnight and never became a saved run. One hundred and one new rows, numbered 161 to 261.

NOISE parameter sweep, the cells behind the headlines. The August 17th campaign reported whole families as one line - it said the volatility-conditional exits were dead across all eight settings, but only two of them ever reached the board. The missing cells are now rows of their own, re-run through the committed harness so the figures are measured rather than remembered.

Do the NOISE filters carry to the ES contract? The nine configurations re-run on a second contract with nothing re-fitted, as the outside check that the filters are not simply fitted to NQ. Every filter beats the champion and none of them clears the promotion bar.

NOISE trade-context scan. Six blind scans over sixteen market-condition measures, ninety-six statistical tests behind six rows. The study says so in its own description rather than pretending each row is a tested configuration.

ORB hunt, the rest of the local cells. The August 17th exit hunt ran fifty-eight configurations. Ten were already here as saved runs and eleven more went up in the ORB ideas study, so this is the remaining thirty-seven. Nothing appears twice.

Book leg weighting grid. All sixteen weightings, re-run so the board carries real dollars instead of the two ratios the round log printed. The rule picked a fitted weighting and it was rejected, and the shape of the grid shows why.
Book legs measured the book way. The same ten strategies re-measured on the book drawdown convention, marked plainly as re-measurements rather than as new things tested, so nobody counts them twice.

Two rows carry dashes instead of money on purpose. Both were genuinely run and both failed, but their settings and figures were never written down, and a blank that says why is better than an invented number.

COMPARE > STUDIES: the charts resize. Every study chart carries the same slim drag bar the run report puts under its charts - drag it down to make that chart taller, up to make it shorter, double-click it to put it back. The size is remembered per study and survives a reload. It stores a drawing height rather than a pixel count, so a resized chart still fills the width of its tile at any window size and its axis captions, tick numbers and legend stay exactly the size they were - the plot area is what grows.

A VALUE ZOOM control - FIT ALL, TRIM 5%, TRIM 10%, TRIM 20%. The axes always spanned only the rows actually shown, so filtering already rescaled them and FIT ALL is that reading. The trims drop that share of the most extreme values off both axis ranges so a cluster can spread out instead of being flattened by one distant row. NOTHING IS HIDDEN: a trimmed row is still drawn, pinned to the edge it ran off, ringed with a dashed warning, and named under the chart with the figure it actually holds.

A COMPARE ON control, because raw totals over mismatched windows are misleading and this board had already proved the windows do not match. Three honest bases, and the board always states in words which one is in force and how many rows it can reach.

COMMON WINDOW is the rigorous one and it costs no re-running: where a row has a real run with a saved equity curve, that curve is sliced to the stretch every row on the tile genuinely shares and the profit and worst drawdown are recomputed on exactly that slice. Four columns appear and the chart plots the sliced figure. A row with no saved curve shows a DASH SAYING WHY and never its un-sliced number - mixing sliced and un-sliced figures in one column is the silent blending this board exists to prevent.

Three limits are printed on the figures themselves rather than buried. A cut may only be placed inside a dated stretch of at most 800 days, so a run that saved no lockbox boundary is refused outright. The sliced drawdown is read off a downsampled curve, so it is a FLOOR and it is not the same measurement as the DRAWDOWN column. And a profit factor cannot be recomputed from a curve at all, because netting trades into curve points destroys the gross winnings and gross losses it is made of - so COMMON PF is always a dash carrying that reason, never an estimate.

PER YEAR divides each row profit by the number of years its own window covers, so a longer window stops being automatically flattered. It needs only a recorded window and not a curve, which makes it the widest-coverage basis - a local research row that records its window is readable on it.

A plain-English guide under the controls saying what each basis means and when to trust it, including which ratio survives a slightly different window: profit factor is the most robust because it is a property of the whole trade population, profit divided by drawdown is the most fragile because a drawdown is one single worst event and this project measured its confidence interval to be WIDER than the drawdown itself, and Sharpe sits between the two.
PROFIT STAGE is ignored under COMMON WINDOW and the board says so out loud rather than quietly - a shared stretch is a calendar range and a stage is a different cut of the same run.
STUDIES_BOARD.md documents the new controls, how the slice works, its three limits, and every view preference this board persists.

COMPARE > STUDIES: four new ENGU-Q studies covering the research that was measured and never became a run. The whole limit-depth curve, the short mirror, bar type and trailing stop, and concurrent positions.

Thirty-one new rows, numbers 130 to 160. None of them has a walk-forward figure because none was ever run as a validate, so each shows a dash that says so on hover and leaves the chart when the walk-forward stage is selected.

The limit-depth study is the one to read. It shows the adopted depth sits on a broad shoulder rather than a spike: profit factor beats the control at every depth from 0.15 to 1.00, and the adopted depth has the strongest lockbox of all of them.

Rows 138 and 139 show the best profit divided by drawdown on the whole board and are marked fragile on purpose. A five thousand sample bootstrap put their drawdown advantage over the adopted depth at minus two hundred and forty five dollars, winning barely half the time, so the board says so rather than quietly recommending them.

The short mirror study records a clean negative: the mirrored short side loses in fifteen of seventeen years, and running both directions is worse than long alone because the shorts also take the single position slot away from the longs.

COMPARE > STUDIES: two new ORB studies covering the research that was measured locally and never became a run. The entry scan that re-tested the opening range against the current exit, and the nine ideas that were tested and killed.

Thirty new rows, numbers 100 to 129. None of them has a walk-forward figure, because none was ever run as a validate. They show a dash that says so and they leave the chart when the walk-forward stage is selected. Nothing is substituted.

One row carries no figures at all. The volatility-floor stop was rejected on a diagnostic before any configuration existed, so every cell is a dash with the reason written out rather than a number nobody measured.
Every row records the stretch of history it covers, so the data-window column and the common-window warning work on them the same as on everything else.

FIX, COMPARE > STUDIES: the study charts really were colourless on the monochrome theme, and the COLOUR control shipped defaulting to the one setting that could not help. THEME means follow the app theme, and the MONO theme has no colours to follow - its blue, green, yellow and red are all greys, and two of them are almost invisible on the dark background - so every verdict came out the same grey no matter how many colours the board thought it was painting.

THEME now reads the theme at draw time and measures how much colour it actually carries. When the theme is genuinely greyscale the board falls back to the five approved colours - blue for the champion, green for held up, amber for fragile, red for failed, grey for reference - instead of five greys. On a colour theme THEME does exactly what it always did.

Your app theme is still never touched, the verdict shapes are still drawn on every mark in every setting, and SHAPES ONLY still gives the pure one-ink reading. The chart, the legend, the name column and the row tints all follow the same resolved setting, so they can never disagree.
The line under the controls now says in words which of the two things is happening, so a grey board is always a stated choice rather than something that looks broken.

COMPARE > STUDIES: the common-window warning now reads correctly when exactly one row differs. It said "1 of them differ" and "Row 47 cover history the others never saw". Wording only, no change to which rows it names or to the day counts.
STUDIES: four new studies. The ORB breakeven and plateau hunt, the ORB grail hunt round one, the ENGU-Q session and entry variants, and a list of what is running in paper right now.
STUDIES: every row now says whether it is CROWNED, running in PAPER, both, or neither. It is a new column, a new filter, and a ring around the chart mark.
STUDIES: the ORB configuration being forward-tested is the PREVIOUS crown, not the current one. The board now says so on the rows themselves.
STUDIES: four older rows gained the run number that produced them, so they open their report instead of reading as local research.

COMPARE > STUDIES: a TIME SCOPE control - ALL TIME, PAST WEEK, PAST MONTH, PAST 3 MONTHS. It narrows the charts and the tables together and always says how many rows it is holding back, beside the count the filters already print.

A row carries TWO different dates, so the scope never picks one quietly. The date it was DISCOVERED in research, which every row has, and the date it RAN as a real validate run, which only rows saved as runs have at all. SCOPE DATE is its own control - FOLLOWS ORDER BY, DISCOVERED or DATE RAN - and a line under the controls states in words which date is being read and from what cut-off. ORDER BY RESULT is not a date, so FOLLOWS ORDER BY falls back to the date discovered and says so.

Scoping on the date ran cannot place a row that was never run. Those rows are held back but never dropped without a word: they are counted and named by row number under the controls and again under the study chart, with the two ways to bring them back spelled out. It is the same honesty the DATE RAN ordering already uses when it puts them in their own labelled block.

A COLOUR control for this board alone, which never touches your app theme. THEME keeps what the board always did. COLOUR forces the five approved colours whatever the theme is doing - blue champion, green held up, amber fragile, red failed, grey reference. SHAPES ONLY drops to one neutral ink. THE VERDICT SHAPES ARE DRAWN IN ALL THREE, on the chart, in the legend and beside every name, so colour is reinforcement and never the only signal. Money keeps its minus sign in every setting. The choice is saved like every other view preference here.

A DATA WINDOW column on every study table: the stretch of history that row’s figures actually cover, read from the saved run document where the row has a run number and from the studies registry where it does not. It is never guessed - a row that records no window shows a dash saying so.

THE COMMON WINDOW, printed under every study chart and once for the whole board: the stretch every visible row genuinely shares. When they do not share one the line warns you, names the rows that reach outside it and says by how much. Those rows also get a warning sign in their own window cell. This matters because some runs are older and saw less data than the backfill has since added, so their totals were never comparable - the board now says so instead of leaving you to find out.
Nothing was recomputed, re-run or refreshed. This release only surfaces the window each row already covers and warns when the windows disagree.

The studies registry gains an optional data window per study and per row, so a locally computed result can record the stretch it covers instead of showing a dash. STUDIES_BOARD.md documents the new field and both new controls.

COMPARE > STUDIES: a PROFIT STAGE toggle (in-sample, walk-forward, lockbox, total). It sets the height of every chart point, highlights the matching money column in every table and drives the profit divided by drawdown column, so every row on screen is compared on the same stretch of history. A row with no figure for that stage shows a dash saying why and leaves the chart, and the line under the chart counts it. No figure from another stage is ever put in its place.

A VERTICAL AXIS toggle: raw profit, or profit divided by the worst drawdown. On the ratio the tick labels read as plain numbers rather than dollars. Each study keeps its own default - books open on the ratio because more legs means more margin, single strategies open on raw profit - and PER STUDY honours those defaults.

Filter chips for strategy type, verdict, discovered date and run status. They are built from the tags the rows carry rather than written into the code, so a new study tags its rows and gets its buttons for free. Filters narrow the chart and the table together and the board always says how many rows are hidden.

The dots no longer rely on colour. Every verdict has its own shape, size and outline - a filled circle for the champion, a filled square, a hollow circle, a cross and a hollow triangle - so all five read on the monochrome theme. The legend and the name column show the same marks. Colour is still applied on top for the colour themes.
The chart and the table now talk to each other both ways. Clicking a point scrolls the table to its row and lights it up; hovering a row lights up its point. The permanent row number is the link.
Each study table scrolls on its own with its headings pinned, so a long study no longer runs off the page, and the wide columns still scroll sideways without moving the page.

Ported from the summary file: a RANK column, tinted champion and winning rows, the bulleted notes under each table, the shapes in the legend and the note that the best results sit toward the top left. ORDER BY gains a RESULT option that sorts best first on the selected stage.

A new document at the repo root, STUDIES_BOARD.md, explains the whole registry for anyone adding the next study: every field, how to tag rows, what a row needs to appear on the chart, the permanent-row-number rule, the dash-with-a-reason rule and why a pooled book is never compared head to head with a single strategy.

THE FIVE OLD BOOK RUNS NOW READ CORRECTLY ON SCREEN. Runs 238, 258, 261, 262 and 263 were saved before the units fix, so their headline money was counted twice and printed 20 times too large. Nothing in Firestore was rewritten - the app now corrects those figures as it reads them. Run 261 reads $984,200 with a $56,090 drawdown instead of $19.7 million with a $1.1 million drawdown.

The correction is worked out from the run itself, never from a run number or a date. A book run always carries its own pooled block, and that block was always right. If the stored headline already matches that block the run is left completely alone; only when the headline is exactly that block times the saved contract size is it divided back down. A book run saved from today onward matches its own block, so it is never touched.

Corrected: the headline net, the max drawdown, the dollars-per-day and everything derived from them, which includes MAR and the equity scaling in COMPARE. Left exactly as saved: the profit factor, the trade count, the lockbox figures, the equity curve values and the PASS or FAIL verdict, because none of those were ever wrong.
The RUNBOARD BOOKS table and the RUNBOARD matrix read the pooled block directly and were always right. They are deliberately not corrected a second time, so their numbers are unchanged.
A corrected run carries a small amber UNITS CORRECTED tag in Past Runs, on the RUNBOARD list and at the top of its report. Hover it and it says what was adjusted and what was left alone.

COMPARE > STUDIES: every study now shows a scatter chart above its table, the same risk map you were reading in the summary file. Worst drawdown runs left to right and the champion or baseline point is drawn larger with a white outline, so you can see at a glance which variants sit up and to the left of it.

The chart is driven by the same study registry the tables read. A new study you add gets its chart automatically once it names its two axis columns and their captions, with no change to the drawing code.
A row missing either axis figure is left off its chart, and the line underneath the chart says how many were left off and why. No figure is ever substituted to fill a gap.
COMPARE > STUDIES: a losing money figure now keeps its minus sign, matching the study table you were already reading. Drawdown stays positive, because its heading already says drawdown.

FIX to a wrong number, not an ugly one. The big headline dollar figure on a BOOK run was 20 times too large. A book already counts its money in dollars - it converts each leg with that leg own contract size before pooling the trades - but the step that saves the run treated that figure as raw points and multiplied it by 20 a second time. Run 261 read 19,684,006 when the book actually made 984,200 over that stretch, and run 262 read 12,980,663 instead of 649,033. The max drawdown and the dollars-per-day on those cards were inflated the same 20 times.

What was always right: the BOOKS table on the RUNBOARD, the equity curve, the lockbox figure, the profit factor, the trade count and the PASS or FAIL verdict. Those read the book own pooled block and never went through the bad step. That is why one run doc could show a correct 261,794 lockbox next to a 19.7 million headline.

Books started through the RUN A BOOK button were never affected. The five that were - 238, 258, 261, 262 and 263 - were queued by script. From the next book run onward the headline is correct. The five old cards are left exactly as they were saved: divide their headline net, drawdown and per-day figures by 20 to read them.
Second thing worth knowing, and it is by design rather than a bug: a book headline covers the stretch BEFORE the lockbox, not the whole window. The whole-window total lives in the BOOKS table.

The new COMPARE mode is called STUDIES, not RESEARCH. The Backtester already has a RESEARCH tab (the backtesting stack), and two nav items one row apart with the same name was confusing. Nothing else changed.

COMPARE has a fourth mode: RESEARCH. It holds the completed research studies as tables you can read on the site instead of in chat - the 26 NOISE variants, the pooled books, and the cross-family filter transfer tests on ORB and ENGU-Q. Every row keeps the row number you were already given, its short name, a plain-English line saying what it does, and the same verdict colour coding: blue is the champion or baseline, green beat it and held up, amber works but is fragile, red failed, grey is a reference.

Each study gets its own table on purpose. A pooled book uses more margin than a single strategy, so a book cannot be compared head to head with one strategy - the board says so and points you at profit divided by drawdown instead of raw profit.

ORDER BY toggle: DATE DISCOVERED or DATE RAN. Date ran is read live out of run history, so it is the date the real validate run actually finished. Rows that were only ever computed locally have no run, so under DATE RAN they move into their own block marked never run as a validate run and show a dash. No date is ever invented.

A row that was saved as a real run shows its run number and opens that run report when you click it. A row that was not shows the word local, the same convention the RUNBOARD uses. FIX: the board was telling you the wrong thing about what is running. The leg NinjaTrader is ACTUALLY trading - NOISE-225 with the rf bouncer - was showing OFF, because the live-state lookup still named the NOISE leg that was retired earlier today. It now reads the same field the tiles do, so the two can never drift apart again.

Legs that were never meant to run in NinjaTrader no longer wear a warning colour. The two comparison legs (NOISE-225 on its own, and the tree bouncer) and the ORB bouncer are computed here on purpose - they are the controls and the alternative brain - so they now read ENGINE in neutral grey instead of OFF in yellow, which looked like three broken things.

ORB still reads OFF, and that one is real: its NinjaTrader port was switched off today because it still runs the old pre-#230 settings, so its fills would measure a config nothing else on the board uses. Hovering the badge now says exactly that instead of leaving you to guess.

NinjaTrader is now on the recycle hybrid too, and the guardrails were left alone to do it. The obvious way to make room was to scale every limit up to fit 3.85x sizing - but that would have meant raising the daily loss limit, the one guardrail measured in real money. Running the numbers gave a better answer: drop the BASE size from 10 micros to 3 instead. Recycle is a ratio, so the experiment and its equity curve are identical either way, just at a third of the exposure.

What that buys: the leg averages about 11 micros a trade (roughly the one-contract exposure it has had all along) and the untouched $1,500 daily limit still trips at about 65 adverse points - which is essentially the 75 points it was set for. At the naive setting it would have fired after 20 points and switched every strategy off on an ordinary day.
Only the contract count moved, 30 to 40, because the worst case a score can reach is 35. Verified live: all three gates released by the size interlock, worst case 34.7 against the 40 limit.

The tile comparison against the no-gate control now states the size it was earned at, and shows the per-contract figure beside the dollar gap. Once a gate recycles it trades several times the control size, so a raw dollar difference mostly measures size rather than skill - it would flatter the gate in a good stretch and damn it in a bad one, for the same wrong reason.

The three gated legs are now RECYCLE hybrids, as asked. Recycle spends the money the bouncer frees up: it adds no trades, it makes each surviving trade bigger, so that the book commits the same total contracts as taking everything would have. On the board the average sizes are now 1.2x for ORB, 2.0x for the tree NOISE and 3.8x for the rf NOISE - the exact ratios of trades-taken to trades-kept, measured on the runs those gates came from and frozen, not recalculated from the days being tested.
Read the drawdowns with that in mind: recycle multiplies losses by the same number it multiplies gains. The rf NOISE row will swing about 3.8 times as hard in both directions.

NINJATRADER IS STILL ON PLAIN HYBRID, on purpose, and it says so. Its position limits are still set for one-lot trading, and a recycled order would have exceeded them - which would have made the circuit breaker flatten and switch off every strategy on the first trade Monday. The gate service now reads those limits itself and refuses to serve a size that would not fit, falling back to plain hybrid and stating why. Raise the limits and it switches over on its own, no restart.

1E MATRIX scope tags cleaned up and colour-coded. The IS / WF / LB names in every section header (return, reward vs risk, sample) now wear the same colours the 2A funnel chart shades those periods with - IS in the plain grey of the un-shaded stretch, WF in the walk-forward blue, LB in the lockbox purple - on all four tabs (RAW, GATE, TILT, HYBRID), including the return section that had a plain tag before.

The little window tags repeated on individual rows (MAR, PF, DD, TRADES and friends) are gone where they only said the same thing as their section header. A row keeps its own tag ONLY when it genuinely measures a different window than its section - e.g. TRADES and FOLDS HELD on the RAW tab, the size rows pinned to FULL on the sizing tabs, and the pinned windows on runs too old to slice - and those surviving tags wear the same period colours.

Retired the old hand-built NOISE leg. It was assembled from research and never actually won a validation, while three consecutive validations in a row (#202, #225, #231) all picked the NOISE-225 settings instead - and as of tonight NinjaTrader runs those too. It was the only thing left measuring a variant nothing else in the system uses. Its single logged trade was removed with it so the board does not carry an orphan row.
NOISE-225 inherits its teal colour, so the four NOISE-family rows are now three: the settings, and the same settings with each of the two bouncers.

The ML gate status is now in the TOP BAR, next to the trade count, on every tab - a green GATE dot when it is running, red GATE DOWN when it is not, yellow GATE STALE when it is answering but its decision-maker has not been re-taught in days. Hovering gives the detail; clicking opens the gate service own status page.

It belongs up there rather than buried in the PAPER tab because its failure is SILENT: the gate is fail-open, so if it dies NinjaTrader simply takes every signal at normal size and nothing else on the screen changes. Same reasoning as the DATA warning beside it.

To make that work on every tab, the board now reads the NinjaTrader status doc on a slow timer rather than only when the PAPER tab loads. The browser cannot check the gate service directly - this site is https and the service is plain http on your own machine, which browsers block - so the status comes via the runner, and the clickable link is the direct check that always works.

You can now SEE whether the ML gate is running. It went live earlier today with no indicator anywhere, and it is the one piece whose failure is invisible from the outside: if it dies, NinjaTrader keeps trading and just takes every signal at normal size, so everything still looks fine while the experiment has quietly stopped. There is now an ML GATE line on the NinjaTrader card - green UP with how many models are loaded and how fast it answers, or red DOWN saying outright that NinjaTrader is trading ungated.

It also watches how fresh the decision-maker is. The gate re-teaches itself every evening after the close; if that has been failing the line turns yellow and says how many days old it is, which you would never notice otherwise because the service keeps answering perfectly with a stale brain.
The line is always visible - it does not hide behind the detail toggle - and hovering it explains what happens if it is down and how to restart it.

Added NOISE-225 · rf HYBRID 55 - your pick - and on the evidence it is the better grounded of the two NOISE gates, so it goes on the board beside the tree one rather than instead of it. Both are scored against the same raw NOISE-225 control, so they are also directly comparable with each other.

Why yours is better grounded: judged only on the years the selection rule is ALLOWED to see, rf recovery 19.72 beats ungated 14.23. Only two of the five hybrids clear that bar, and tree is not one of them - tree is the WORST of the five there. rf is also 2nd of five on BOTH sides of the lockbox boundary, the only variant that is neither a pre-lockbox favourite that collapsed nor a hindsight pick that never earned its place.

The honest weakness, so it is not oversold: out of sample rf does NOT beat taking every trade. Recovery 1.69 against 1.79, on less than half the money. What it does do is HALVE the drawdown, 831 against 1,640, for about the same risk-adjusted return. That makes it a risk reducer and a sizing-up lever, not an edge, and the forward test should be read that way.

Note on the size shape: HYBRID rows always slide linearly, 0.25x to 3x with 1x at a 50% score. The stepped 0.5x / 1x / 2x shape only ever existed on TILT rows, which are retired - so there is no stepped hybrid to choose between.

HONESTY FIX on the paper legs. The runner re-runs the whole window since 11 Aug every night, so the moment a leg is added it instantly shows trades going back to the 11th that nothing actually watched happen. Those are BACKTEST rows, and they were sitting next to ENGU-Q, which genuinely has been running since the 11th, looking exactly the same. A config added this morning was reading as a fortnight of evidence.

Every leg now records the date its CURRENT config went on the board, and trades before it are marked backfilled. The tile shows the split in yellow: how many rows are backfill and what they made, then the forward-only count underneath. Only that second number is evidence.

ORB is in that list too. Its trades predate 16 Aug but its config does not - the leg was swapped off the retired look-ahead #125 cut that morning, so its two rows were produced by a config that was not on the board when they happened.

LEG NAMES now say exactly which overlay is running. +GATE was useless because this project runs four kinds that behave nothing alike - RAW (none), CUT (skip the weak ones, one lot each), TILT (take everything, just size it - retired, 0 of 12 cleared the bar) and HYBRID (skip AND size the survivors). Both gated legs are HYBRID, so they now read ORB · rf HYBRID 45 and NOISE-225 · tree HYBRID 55: model, kind and cut-off, no cross-referencing.

FIX, found while checking the new gated legs: the ORB leg was showing 6 trades and -$566 when its actual config produces 2. Trade rows are written by id, which refreshes a trade that still exists but can never remove one that stopped existing - so when ORB was swapped off the retired look-ahead #125 config, that config four trades stayed on the board and kept being drawn. The ORB curve was a blend of two different strategies.

The four stale rows are gone and ORB now reads its real 2 trades. This mattered more than it looks: gated legs are scored AGAINST their raw control, so a control carrying another config trades made every gate comparison meaningless.

The runner now prunes rows a leg no longer produces, so the next config swap cleans up after itself. Deliberately narrow: it only runs when the backtest actually completed (a leg that fails to load its data returns no trades, and pruning on that would delete real history), and it can only touch rows inside the forward-test window.

The ML GATE now runs on the paper board. Until today every ML result this project produced lived in the optimize/validate side and none of it was ever forward-tested; the paper runner only ever ran plain configs. It can now run a gate as an overlay: the strategy picks its trades exactly as before, and a second model - trained only on trades that had already FINISHED before each new trade fires - either skips the weak ones (cut) or skips them AND sizes the survivors by score (hybrid).

Three new legs. ORB +GATE is run #230 with its own crowned rf gate at 45% in hybrid mode - that gate was picked on pre-lockbox data by the pre-registered rule and then HELD its one look at the held-out year, and its hybrid row was the best of five on BOTH halves. NOISE-225 is the config two consecutive auto-validates actually crowned (lookback 44, 0.75/1.5 bands, stop 1.75), which the old hand-built NOISE leg is not. NOISE-225 +GATE is that config with a tree hybrid gate at 55%.

READ THE NOISE ONE AS A TEST, NOT A CROWN. The gate run #225 actually crowned FAILED its lockbox outright. The tree hybrid posted much the best held-out year, but its PRE-lockbox recovery was the WORST of the five, so the selection rule - which only ever sees pre-lockbox data - would never have picked it. That makes its win hindsight. It is on the board as a pre-registered forward test with the claim written down in advance: it should beat NOISE-225 from today on, and if it does not, that lockbox row was noise.

Every gated leg is paired with a matched CONTROL - the same backtest with the gate switched off - and the tile shows the head-to-head, because the question is never whether the gate made money but whether it beat the same strategy ungated. ORB +GATE reads against ORB; NOISE-225 +GATE against NOISE-225, which is emitted from the same backtest at no extra cost so nothing is confounded.

Tiles now show what the gate DID: model, mode, cut-off, how many trades it refused and the average size it traded. Without that a gated row is a bare number and a quiet market looks identical to a bouncer that refused everything. A gate that fails to run falls back to UNGATED and says so in red rather than silently reporting an empty day.

Housekeeping: the board leg list was five separate hardcoded arrays that had to agree by hand - which is how a tile once said grey while the curve drew yellow - and is now one definition everything derives from. The built-in ORB config card also still described the retired look-ahead #125 config long after the leg moved to #230.

The SAMPLE and SHOW selectors on the two 1A candidate charts are pinned to the RIGHT now, travelling as one group - the same controls-right layout every other header in the report uses. In a narrow column the pair drops to a second line together, still flush right, instead of one of them getting stranded back on the left. The trend readout and the family key stay on the left, beside the chart they describe.

HYBRID RECYCLE was missing from both 1A candidate charts and is now in, as the fifth family in the fifth funnel-key colour (pink). It was left out on the grounds that it is the same candidates re-sized rather than a separate family - true of WHICH candidates they are, but re-sizing a book changes its net AND its drawdown, so a recycled hybrid lands somewhere else entirely on a profit-vs-drawdown chart.
